# L29.1c Structural Nonlinearity in Wind Failures Across Structure Types (Exploring)

This sub-project, split from L29.1 by the PI, asks how high-rise buildings, low-rise buildings, bridges and transmission towers fail in windstorms, and whether the main structure enters nonlinearity. It tests the PI's "fuse" mechanism: cladding fails first and the main structure is automatically unloaded. Using primary post-disaster surveys and pre-registered criteria, the Lead agent compiled a failure-mode table. After a three-reviewer round, version 2 found partial support for modern curtain-wall high-rises: the lateral system showed no observed nonlinearity in the two surveys that covered the main structure, but there is no evidence for automatic unloading, and most events were at or below design wind speed. Transmission towers, where the wind-loaded members carry the load, buckled and collapsed near or above design wind speed. The low-rise and masonry-wall boundary cases were rated "insufficient evidence", and bridges "not applicable" because the Tacoma case was aerodynamic instability. A follow-up internal-pressure model (option B) found that a single-face breach does not reach the −5% unloading threshold. This holds only within its stated scope: fixed external flow, two TPU building shapes, 0° wind. Whether through-flow changes this remains unresolved.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: The start-up plan was submitted, with column definitions and criteria fixed before work began. The PI approved it and specified that the Zotero bot, not the wiki bot, should find literature.
- **2026-10-21**: Primary sources were retrieved, including FEMA and NIST hurricane and tornado reports, the 1941 Tacoma Narrows report, and tower-collapse investigations from China, Japan, Canada and Australia.
- **2026-10-21**: Table v1 went to three independent reviewer models. One did not support it as delivered; two supported it with reservations. Their must-fix items covered the "not observed" definition, qualitative evidence in the load-change column, mixed debris and surge cases, page errors and inconsistent tower event counts.
- **2026-10-21**: Table v2 was finalized under the original criteria. The masonry and low-rise rulings were withdrawn to "insufficient evidence", and the bridge ruling was changed to "not applicable".
- **2026-10-21**: The parent Lead released option B. A lumped internal-pressure model ran 648 main configurations, finding single-face breach changes of at most 2.4%. Multi-face breaches into one shared space reduced overturning moment by up to 8.3% at 10% opening and up to 29% at 35%.
- **2026-10-21**: Three reviewer models supported option B with reservations. In version 2, the multi-face reductions are stated to apply only when the upper half of the height is breached (a single band gives −0.5% to −1.0% at 10%). The pressure amplification bound was corrected to 5.6%. Whether through-flow can reverse the single-face result was ruled "insufficient evidence".
- **2026-10-21 to 10-22**: Quotes were gathered for option C. No physical wind tunnel was available. LBM was estimated at 390–750 Colab compute units with low confidence of passing the credibility gate. LES was quoted at about 13,000–20,000 core-hours, or about 200–310 SU on TACC.
- **2026-10-24**: Supplementary cards were appended to the latest report; both v2 conclusions were unchanged.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the start-up plan on 10-21. Literature retrieval goes to the Zotero bot, and the wiki bot only builds cards.
- On 10-24, asked every project to bring its latest report to the front of the conversation for review.

## Where it stands
The Lead agent recommends LES on TACC, released in two stages: inflow calibration plus the intact building first, and the breach cases only if the credibility gate is passed. LBM would serve as a supplement. The three-reviewer check and the go decision rest with the L29.1 Lead, and no jobs are running.

# L29.1d Wind-Induced Nonlinear Failure of Wind Turbines (Active)

This sub-project asks why wind turbines, unlike buildings, enter main-structure nonlinearity and collapse in strong wind, by building a case library of wind-induced tower collapses and buckling with every entry checked against the original source. It answers only why and how turbines fail; design is left to the core-lab project L31.8. A literature worker agent retrieved primary sources (Chinese, Japanese, Taiwanese, US and European) and a wiki worker agent built cards and per-turbine extraction tables; no computation was run (0 SU). After library expansion, typhoon collapses with primary investigations rose from 4 to 9 events, covering turbines from the 400 kW class to 6.25 MW, which meets the plan's success criteria. The reviewed stage conclusion (v3.1) finds three collapse paths among the checked events (shell buckling of the tower, connection failure, foundation failure), with one event whose initiating mechanism is unknown. It finds two differences from modern curtain-wall buildings: the wind-loaded tower wall is itself the load-bearing member, and loads depend on the parked attitude, which relies on power and holding devices. Exceeded design wind speed and lost attitude cannot be separated from the accident records, and "blade as fuse" has model support only for parked conditions. The conclusions are limited to the checked events: there is one large-megawatt case (with mechanism from a proxy model only), no offshore case, and several wind speeds are model estimates.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: The PI approved the start-up plan, correcting that source retrieval goes to the literature agent and the wiki agent only builds cards.
- **2026-10-21**: An early case (Maemi 2003) showed ultimate moments only 5–14% above design for three identical towers; the two whose typhoon moments exceeded design by 18–27% buckled near the door opening.
- **2026-10-21**: With only 6 typhoon events verified, the Lead agent stopped expansion and sent conclusion v1 to three reviewer models; all gave qualified support, and 14 must-fix items were applied in v2 (for example, the 5–14% figure is strength reserve, not ductility, and the blade-fuse claim lacked its counter-cases).
- **2026-10-21**: The parent Lead agent withdrew the stop, citing the PI's view that wind turbines are a future focus and that missing sources are not a reason to stop; expansion was set to run to 10-28.
- **2026-10-21**: New primary reports added Jangmi 2008, Hinomisaki 2018, Mulan Bay 2024 (8 unoperated 6.25 MW turbines collapsed while 2 operating 2 MW units were largely intact), Kimotsuki 2016 (control in storm mode with grid power, measured 10-minute wind 1.54 times the 50 m/s design reference) and Soudelor 2015.
- **2026-10-22**: Conclusion v3 was reviewed by three reviewer models (qualified support, 13 corrections); v3.1 was finalized, withdrawing the claim that exceeded wind speed and attitude loss are each sufficient on their own.
- **2026-10-24**: A follow-up check confirmed all retrieval tasks returned and 9 primary typhoon events, so the 10-28 "stuck" gate does not trigger; a 10-24 addendum noted that snowball searching on 10-22/23 added no new typhoon collapse cases.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the start-up plan on 10-21, with source finding assigned to the literature agent and card building to the wiki agent.
- On 10-24 asked every project to bring its latest report to the top of the conversation for review.

## Where it stands
Conclusion v3.1 is final, reported upward and available for L31.8 to cite. Library expansion stays open until 10-28, with any new primary source added the same way; there is nothing pending for the PI.

# L29.3 性能化与韧性设计走进最终设计需要什么

## 当前状态（10-21 更新）
10-21 进展与计划报告：（回答稿 v1 10-29；Liang Hu 待定 2 条：对外取数、 出口）。
10-24 最新报告：（末尾「10-24 补记」）；W1 延至 10-25、W5b 10-26，回答稿 v1 仍 10-29；Liang Hu 待定 2 条未变。

### 10-17 记录
在做（Liang Hu 10-16 批复开工）。第一周（10-17—10-23）按 推进，工作目录。
已派：
- litwiki （10-17 交回）：新建 15 卡，抽取表 22 篇；Pinelli 2008、Ellingwood 2004、IN-CORE 2023 仅摘要。

- better （10-17 交回）：已发表验证证据表 （Lead 复算 5 个相对误差一致）。

- better （10-17 交回）：Michael 数据闸门核查，小样本在 （6.9 MB）。

- 决定（10-17）：自建端到端回算暂停不放弃，判据不改；转"已发表验证证据表"＋"减灾效果实证" —。
- better （10-17 交回）：减灾效果摸底与设计。
- litwiki （10-17 交回）：第三批 5 卡。Sally 降幅无置信区间、未控年代；ARA 2024 为年化损失相对值且用 Irma/Michael/Ian/Idalia 理赔校核，不能当独立外验。

- reviewer-e（Gemini，10-17 交回）：FORTIFIED 屋面板钉固对应 Hazus 8s；reviewer-f（Grok，10-17 交回）：更接近 8s 但 8s 为下界表示。
- （10-17 已裁决）：J1–J4 均部分支持，按裁决收紧 —。
- Grok 快查（10-16 23:44 交回）：。线索：ASCE PBWD 预标准是规范替代路径但实务仍以规定法为主；Michael/Ian 已有 HAZUS 事件验证（仅摘要）；文献普遍区分单事件韧性与年化指标。DOI 两处错配（Pinelli 2008、Barbato 2013），已交 litwiki 核正。
知识库已有卡：Ciampoli 2011 PBWE、N449E3K6 统一框架、Ouyang & Spence 2019 围护、Spence & Kareem 2014、ASCE PBWD 预标准。

## 问题（Liang Hu 原话）
performance，resilience这些东西，为什么工程界无法使用他们进行最终的设计？当然用来做方案比选和概念设计师可以的。我考虑这主要是因为他们的可靠性不足以让人们相信。另外时间和空间尺度也是个问题，目前对于一次台风和几十年的统计，resilience和performance的概念完全不同，用途也不同。

补充（10-16）：1 能力边界（概念设计、初步方案比选）；2 缺乏验证；3 可靠性不确定，需要 trustworthy 的 resilience/performance；4 需要真正的框架，确定并尽量控制每个环节的不确定性，**环节的验证是比较可行的**。

## 对方结论的最强版本（复述）
头 claim。其最有力处：规范设计本身也含大量未量化的不确定性，只是被分项系数隐藏；性能化框架至少把不确定性摆上桌面。

## 我们的怀疑点（按四个分题）
- **3a 能力边界**：链条末端（损失、恢复、功能）的模型不确定性可能比危险性高一个量级，导致绝对值不可信；但**相对比较**（两方案差值）中大部分不确定性相关、可抵消——这正是"能做比选、不能做最终设计"的机理，可以定量说明。
- **3b 验证**：整体结果几乎不可验证（事件稀少、损失受非结构因素主导）；能验证的是环节：危险性（观测极值）、风荷载（风洞/实测）、构件易损性（试验）、损失（理赔数据，有偏）。
- **3c 可信度**：现有文献常给出单一期望值或均值曲线，缺少模型（认知）不确定性的区间，因而无法给"可信度"。
- **3d 框架**：把总不确定性写成各环节的方差（或分位宽度）预算；以环节验证缩小每一项；与 T5（UQ）共用方法。
- **尺度混用（概念错误怀疑）**：resilience 多指单次事件后功能损失与恢复（天—月尺度），performance 常指寿命期年超越概率/期望年损失（几十年尺度）；文献中是否把两者当同一量互换使用，需逐篇核对。
（待检验）

## 判据（开始前写定）
- **对方成立（可用于最终设计）**：在至少一个有独立数据的历史台风事件上，框架对损失/功能的预测落在实测的 ±30% 内，且给出的不确定性区间覆盖实测；并且框架总不确定性（如 90% 区间宽度/中位数）不大于现行规范设计所隐含的可靠度离散。
- **部分成立/适用范围窄**：绝对值不满足上条，但两方案**差值**的符号与排序在不确定性下稳健（概率 ≥90%）——即"可做比选、不可做最终设计"，并量化边界。
- **不成立**：连方案排序也不稳健。
- **尺度混用**：在 ≥15 篇代表文献中，若 ≥1/3 存在把单次事件指标与寿命期指标混用且影响结论，即判定"概念混用"成立（此项是对文献的判断，不是对框架本身）。

## 第一步
1. litwiki 补卡 10–15 篇（PBWE 框架、韧性量化、HAZUS 风损失、台风事件后损失回算），抽取：链条各环节用的模型、是否给不确定性、尺度（单事件/寿命期）、是否做验证。
2. 写一页"不确定性预算"解析骨架：各环节以对数标准差 β 表示，组合 β_total = √Σβ²（相关时另计），给出绝对值与差值两种情形的对比。
3. 3b 的验证途径清单（灾后调查、理赔、实测、构件试验、历史回算）各能验证哪一环。

## 需要的数据
公开理赔/损失数据（如 FEMA、NFIP 汇总，佛罗里达公共飓风损失模型 FPHLM 文档）；IBTrACS；知识库 designload 线卡片。只读引用 designload/eva 线结果。

## 预计工作量
文献与解析 2–3 周；事件回算 2–4 周（视数据可得性）。

## 与其他课题
- **与核心实验室课题 6（概率方法用进风工程）分工（10-16 同意并补充）**：核心实验室负责正向移植与落地（从概率工程力学 PEM、海岸 JPM/多灾种、地震 PSHA/PBEE/条件谱/IDA 里挑方法，做风工程试金石算例）；本实验室负责批判与聚合（T6 多方法并存、T5 最小可用 UQ、T3 的 3d 环节框架与不确定性预算）。方法作为工具出现在 3d 框架里时，它在风工程中适用与否引用对方课题 6 的结论。评判清单两边共用一份，放 下，本方只读引用。补充约定：(a) 对方判为"无用/冗余"的方法族名单，到本方只算**候选**，要批判须先经 Liang Hu 点头开题，并按本实验室判据补齐证据；(b) 两边碰到同一方法族、预判可能相反时（例如本方 T5 怀疑先进 UQ 不改变决策，对方要证明它有增益），用同一个试金石算例和同一份清单，由一方计算、另一方复核，不各算各的。
3d 与 T5 互通（同一套"最小可用 UQ"）；T2 的"复合灾害"部分可作为 3a 的实例。

## 试过与结果
| 日期 | 做了什么 | 结果一句 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-17 | 第一周开工，派 litwiki/better/Grok 快查 | 等结果 |
| 10-17 | 3d 解析骨架（全部 β 为假设） | 同方差、同ρ时 β_Δ=√[2(1−ρ)]β_total；示意 β_total≈0.61、中位损失比 1.5 时，排序概率 ≥90% 需方案间误差相关 ρ≥0.867（Lead 复算一致）。共用误差（危险性、损失换算）可抵消，但方案差异所在的损伤/恢复环未必共享误差——这是待实证的关键 |
| 10-17 | 文献抽取（22 篇）＋ Lead 抽查 | HAZUS II 汇总理赔对比：Andrew Dade 县实际损失率 19.1% 对模型 16.9%/17.5%，Hugo 2.96% 对 3.64%（PDF p. 8–9 / 期刊 p. 101–102，Lead 已核原文 PDF 第 8 页）。即聚合层落在 ±30% 内，但是否为独立留出、有无区间覆盖均未报告，不能直接对应判据；论文自注单栋估计须谨慎。Michael 理赔对减灾特征回归 R²=2.8%（Grant & Atkinson 2023，PDF p. 10）。文献多数把单事件与年化指标分开写，"尺度混用"怀疑暂无支持证据，待第二批 |
| 10-17 | Deep Research 第二步（Lead 读，未送审） | 线索：① Michael Mexico Beach HAZUS 验证——Level 2 聚合 91%、建筑级 64%；另报仅洪水 38.8%、风+洪 43.3% 的建筑级准确率（两组数字口径待 litwiki 核原文）；② Laura/Ida 区片级避难需求与 FEMA 相关 0.70/0.80。**报告的核心结论"方案间误差高度相关、差值可信"没有风工程的直接证据**：依据是气候模式类比与 FEMA P-58 CSPS 的"仅作比选"表述，问题 (B) 未找到任何方案间误差相关的实测估计——这正是 3d 骨架中 ρ≥0.87 是否成立的空白，也就是本课题能补的东西 |

## 10-20 Liang Hu 直投材料核查：航空安全系数与概率方法
核查表与分析：。一手来源 AGARD-R-661（1977）已存；文献卡 （litwiki 10-20 建）。
- **核查结论**：USAF/AGARD 1977 部分逐句属实。原文 PDF p.45 写：纯统计可靠度准则不实用，因为无法准确测量结构可靠度，也写不出可证明符合性的明确要求；p.48 写：单一可靠度数的解释问题抵消其优势；p.45、49 写：试验是揭示严重误差的手段；p.52 写：对算出的可靠度可能产生不应有的信心。
- **10-20 补充（年代/对象/分母、可迁移与不可迁移）**：已追加到核查文件末节。要点：文中概率数字至少四种口径（每次飞行失效 / 每飞行小时载荷超越 AGARD PDF p.24 / 寿命累积 3000 次飞行 PDF p.21 / 882E 项目寿命内），文章把 882E 与 1530D 并列成三档不成立；可迁移的是论证结构（符合性证明、单一数字可接受性、标定而非替代），不可迁移的是阈值数值、分母和"退回"叙事。出口建议仍为 X3，待 Liang Hu 批。
- **夸大与未核**：标题「试过→退回」夸大，实际是研究后不采纳为设计准则；MIL-STD-882E 的三档口径与原文不符；NLR/KAI 2019 的数字查不到，不能引用；MIL-STD-1530D 与 JSSG-2006 的阈值只有二手旁证。
- **对本题的含义**（推断，供回答稿 3a–3c 使用）：困境在「无法证明符合性」，不在「算不出来」；概率工具被接受的位置是补充与在役管理，不是新设计的合规证明；试验与实测只能在环节上兜底；土木（Ferry Borges，同报告 PDF p.65）用概率标定确定性分项系数，可能是性能化/韧性进入最终设计的现实路径。
- **类比边界**：对象（单一结构、可全尺寸试验 vs 长链条、无整体试验）、年代（1977）、监管制度均不同；本文不说明性能化/韧性算错，也不否定其比选用途。
- **建议出口 X3**（直接作为回答稿证据），待 Liang Hu 批。

| FORTIFIED Roof/Gold 屋面板钉固 → Hazus 编码 | 8s（8d 钉 @ 6"/6"）；FORTIFIED 2019 Hurricane Standards（Sally 时现行）：8d 环纹钉，≤130 mph 区全屋面 6"/6"，>130 mph 区边缘/屋脊 4"/4"；2020 版全屋面 4"/4" | reviewer-e（Gemini）查得：IBHS 2019 Hurricane Standards §[地址].3 Table 2-7 p.48、2020 FORTIFIED Home Standard §4.2.2 Table F-RS-2 p.29；Hazus 8d=6"/12"、8s=6"/6"（Hazus HU 技术手册 v5.1 Table 5-16）。Lead 核本地手册文本 第 11637–11649 行：屋面板抗拔试验确分 8d @ 6/12 与 8d @ 6/6 两组；reviewer-f（Grok）交叉印证：同意"更接近 8s 而非 8d"，但**不等于 8s**——FORTIFIED 用环纹钉（Hazus 未区分）、高风速档 4" o.c. 比 6/6 更密，故 8s 是 FORTIFIED 屋面板强度的**下界表示**；2020 版生效日期两方说法不一（Gemini：2020-11；Grok：新许可 2021-11-01），不影响 Sally（2020-09）适用 2019 版。IBHS 原文未亲核 | 手册、DLML 配置、IBHS 标准（经 Gemini） |

## 文献依据
- Rahimian, Udilovich, Shleykov, Kelly & Garber (2025) On performance-based wind design of tall buildings, JWEIA 267:106248（Liang Hu 10-20 发来；卡，PDF）。业界（WSP、RWDI）对 ASCE PBWD 预标准的评述，用于 3a：现行高层实践（风洞＋分级重现期）已近性能化；除强飓风区外 SLS 控制刚度，ULS 非线性边际（PDF p.3）；预标准期望强度＋φ=1 使构件屈服重现期由约 1135 年降到约 232/116 年（PDF p.5–6，构件级、非体系可靠度）。页码经卡片核对（PDF 页＝文章印刷页）。**10-21 晚更正**：10-20 称 Eq.(4) 多乘 0.9、应为 1.53/1.83 是错的；印出的 1.375/1.65 与预标准一致（DCR 1.25/1.5 的最低强度条款取期望强度＋材料 φ，PBWD PDF p.75–76；φ=1.0 用于 §[地址] 变形控制构件容量，PDF p.73，配 DCR>1.0 须做非线性时程的触发，PDF p.74；10-21 审查 校正页锚）。

# L29.3 Why Performance / Resilience Fails to Enter Final Design

## Current Status (Updated 10-21)
10-21 progress and plan report: (response draft v1 on 10-29; 2 items pending Liang Hu's decision: external data request, output).
10-24 latest report: ("10-24 addendum" at the end); W1 extended to 10-25, W5b to 10-26, response draft v1 still 10-29; 2 items pending Liang Hu's decision unchanged.

## Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Sentence Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-17 | Week 1 kickoff, dispatched literature bots and a Grok quick check | Waiting for results |
| 10-17 | 3d analytical skeleton (all β values are assumptions) | Under equal variance and equal ρ, β_Δ=√[2(1-ρ)]β_total; illustratively, at β_total≈0.61 and median loss ratio 1.5, a ranking probability ≥90% requires inter-option error correlation ρ≥0.867 (verified consistent by Lead recomputation). Shared errors (hazard, loss conversion) can cancel out, whereas the damage/recovery links where option differences reside do not necessarily share errors: this is the key point awaiting empirical verification |
| 10-17 | Literature extraction (22 papers) + Lead spot check | HAZUS II aggregate claims comparison: Andrew Dade County actual loss ratio 19.1% vs. model 16.9%/17.5%, Hugo 2.96% vs. 3.64% (PDF pp. 8-9 / journal pp. 101-102, PDF p. 8 verified by Lead). Thus the aggregate level falls within ±30%, but whether it is an independent holdout and whether interval coverage is achieved are unreported, so it cannot directly map to the criterion; the paper itself notes that single-building estimates require caution. Regression of Michael claims on mitigation features yields R²=2.8% (Grant & Atkinson 2023, PDF p. 10). Most literature separates single-event and annualized metrics, so the "scale conflation" suspicion currently lacks supporting evidence, pending Batch 2 |
| 10-17 | Deep Research Step 2 (read by Lead, unreviewed) | Leads: (1) Michael Mexico Beach HAZUS validation: Level 2 aggregate 91%, building-level 64%; separately reports building-level accuracy of 38.8% for flood-only and 43.3% for wind+flood (bases for the two sets of numbers pending original-text verification by litwiki); (2) Laura/Ida tract-level shelter demand correlates with FEMA at 0.70/0.80. **The report's core conclusion that "inter-option errors are highly correlated and differences are reliable" lacks direct wind-engineering evidence**: it relies on climate-model analogies and FEMA P-58 CSPS wording ("for relative comparison only"), and Question (B) found no empirical estimates of inter-option error correlation: this is precisely the gap regarding whether ρ≥0.87 holds in the 3d skeleton, and what this project can address |
| 10-17 | Sally proxy pilot (component proxy, not on an identical basis, descriptive) | Key finding: the modeled effectiveness of FORTIFIED Roof depends almost entirely on a single mapping choice: when roof sheathing nailing takes the 8d branch, P(DS≥1) reduction at 85 mph is only -4% to 6% (reversing sign on some archetypes), whereas under the 8s branch it is 82% to 88%; Gold similarly shows 0% to 9% vs. 87% to 98% (four-archetype range, lines 18-25). The observed claim-frequency reduction of 73%/76% (ALDOI PDF physical p. 28) is of the same order of magnitude only under the 8s branch. The ranking of Gold vs. Roof flips in 4 of 32 cells under 8d and 1 of 32 cells under 8s. **That is, in this example, the option comparison conclusion is dominated by epistemic uncertainty in "how the option is represented in the component library", far exceeding the effect of the wind-speed range**: a concrete instance of 3a/3d (pending testing, unreviewed); 8d/8s correspondence: verification shows FORTIFIED corresponds to **8s** (see parameter source table); under the 8s branch, modeled reductions (Roof 82-88%, Gold 87-98% at 85 mph) exceed observed reductions (73%/76%), while Gold showing a larger reduction than Roof aligns in direction with observed severity; since 8s is a lower-bound representation of FORTIFIED, a more faithful representation would only increase the modeled reduction further and widen the gap with observations (pending testing) |
| 10-17 | Batch 4 cards (review gap-filling) | Watson & Johnson 2004 (PDF p. 9 Table 8): the **pre-calibration initial version** is currently the closest to an "unseen observation" event prediction in this project: 5 of 7 regional aggregate endpoints fall within or near the target range, but the PR severe-damage/destruction proportion is 13% vs. 0.9-1.3% (approx. 10x), and USVI direct economic loss is 5.7B vs. 1.0-2.0B (approx. 3-6x); the authors then used the same set of metrics to calibrate parameters (final version 8% and $4.1B still exceed targets). Target ranges are not prediction intervals. Whether the initial version truly had no exposure to these observations remains pending verification |
| 10-17 | Table of published validation evidence (unreviewed) | Only 5 configurations across 2 events allow computing same-basis single-event insured loss ratios (HAZUS 2006: Andrew 4 configurations e=-8.4% to -11.5%, Hugo +23.0%), with all point estimates within ±30%; however, **0 of the 5 items have both independent holdout and reported interval coverage**, nor is there a code-reliability dispersion benchmark. Sypniewski 2026 on Michael evaluates damage states (DS4 aggregate count 297/324, building-by-building exact-match rate 270/577≈47%, conflicting with 43.3%/64% in the main text, pending verification). Ellingwood 2004 on Andrew reports roof sheathing loss ratio of 92% vs. 69% (+33%). Existing evidence is insufficient to compute the probability of achieving 90% option-ranking accuracy. **Post-review wording: at the county/state aggregate level, 5 configuration point estimates fall within ±30% (with same-direction underestimation on Andrew), but the full criterion is unjudgeable due to lacking proof of independent holdout, interval coverage, and code-reliability comparison; cannot be extrapolated to the single-building / final-design scale** |
| 10-17 | Mitigation effectiveness scoping | Individual measures (roof covering / sheathing nailing / connections), opening protection, roof shape, and premium discounts: none pass the entry gate for same-basis ranking tests; FORTIFIED package: pending determination (observation side is relatively complete). Lead verified original text: Alabama DOI & CRIR 2025 Sally report PDF physical pp. 28-29 (printed pp. 18-19) Tables 7-8, near-neighbor (within 0.25 miles) tree-fall-excluded FORTIFIED Roof/Gold relative to conventional: claim frequency reduced by 73%/76%, severity reduced by 15%/24%, loss ratio reduced by 72%/67%; across all three analyses, the direction of "better than conventional" is consistent, but whether Roof or Gold achieves a larger reduction flips depending on the analysis method (frequency: 56/70, 69/63, 73/76). **Corrected after review**: severity reduction is larger for Gold across all three analyses, and only the ordering of frequency reduction changes; the three analyses differ in sample, Roof/Gold differ in control group, and Gold is located in higher-hazard zones, so one cannot infer that "effect size governs ranking robustness", leaving that mechanism solely as a 3d hypothesis pending testing |
| 10-17 | A completion + B alternative events | A overall gate failed: a complete denominator within the survey footprint cannot be established (NSI demonstration rectangle has 329 buildings vs. 47 in StEER, with unknown sampling mechanism), and 0 of 161 rows are confirmed wind-only; StEER→HAZUS mapping remains candidate only. B: Laura/Ida/Ian/Sally (Florida segment) all failed within the public channels verified in this round (Louisiana has parish × all-peril payouts but lacks parish × residential cross-tabulations and policy denominators; Alabama Sally has aggregate policy counts and payouts but no policy-level data). **Within the public channels verified in this round, this line cannot independently construct an end-to-end hindcast to test the ±30% criterion** (a judgment on data availability, not an evaluation of any model; corrected on 10-17 per review) |
| 10-17 | Michael data gate | A. Physical damage: pending determination (PRJ-2113 has 736 records, Panama City single-family 161 → 160 after coarse screening; missing undamaged denominator, water mask, and HAZUS damage-state mapping). B. Insurance claims: failed (no contemporaneous co-located residential paid losses and policy denominator). C. FEMA verified losses: pending determination (DR-4399 Bay County has 58,044 registrations, wind and water inseparable). Same-event option comparison can only use non-random grouping, and a single event cannot identify ρ. **Lead decision: stop pursuing B on Michael, hold off on C, turn A into a hindcastable component-level validation first; search for another event for B** |
| 10-17 | Hindcast pre-registration design | Specified basis, holdout, and stopping rules: if same-basis monetary values / exposure denominators / holdout conditions cannot be established, stop testing the ±30% criterion and report only verifiable links; single-event StEER cannot estimate inter-option loss/recovery residual correlation ρ, which requires multiple events |
| 10-17 | 3b validation pathways and public data scoping | Candidate benchmarks: NFIP (OpenFEMA, primarily water damage), StEER (physical damage), Florida OIR (event-level insured losses); the three differ in basis and conflate wind and water, so they cannot be directly combined into an independent ground truth for wind loss |

# L29.3a Layered Performance Metrics (Exploring)

This sub-project is work package W1 of the L29.3 plan v2. It builds a 9-cell table (single building/community/region × single event/annual/design reference period) giving, for each cell, the metric definition, algorithm, users and decisions, and data for checking it, plus a one-page unified formula based on the PEER chain, with resilience treated as a variant that adds a recovery model. The Lead agent produced the start-up plan and table v0 on 2026-10-24 as desk work, not reviewed. Its tentative reading, limited to the cited literature: final design sits in the hardest-to-check cell, while most validation data are regional single-event; regional agreement does not imply building-level accuracy (for Hurricane Michael DS4, about 91% regional agreement versus about 64% at building location).

## Timeline
- **2026-10-24**: Sub-project opened; start-up plan and table v0 written and reported upward.
- **2026-10-25**: The 91%/64% citation was checked against the card extraction table and found consistent; the Centerville 2016 paper was noted as available for reading.

## What the PI decided
- Turn the plan's work packages into sub-projects and layer metrics by building/community/region × single event/annual/design reference period.

## Where it stands
The inter-building loss correlation is still an assumption. Next step: finalize v0 on 10-26 for the W1 section of the 10-29 answer draft.

# L29.3b Large-Scale Validation (Not started)

This sub-project is work package W2 of the L29.3 plan v2 (why performance and resilience approaches do not reach final design). W2a will audit published hurricane damage and loss model validations paper by paper: whether validation events were used in development, tuning or model selection, whether criteria were set in advance, and whether data were held out and prediction intervals reported. The parent Lead agent's brief already records findings from source documents: in FPHLM v8.3 the same claims data serve both validation and calibration, and in Hazus-MH 2.1 the Andrew roof validation contains a 0.8 calibration factor and the end-to-end validation reuses Andrew, with only a rainfall case (Bertha) held out. W2b will estimate analytically how many events and buildings a large-scale validation needs, given that damage within one event is correlated so the event count dominates, and will supply a pre-specified validation protocol template. A known obstacle is that the only public building-level datasets that include undamaged buildings (Ian and Helene) mainly record storm surge damage and cannot validate wind damage alone. Conclusions are to be limited to the papers audited.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-24**: Sub-project created at the PI's request that the plan v2 work packages become sub-projects; the start-up plan (under 2 pages, citing 13 groups of existing cards) was written and reported to L29.3.

## What the PI decided
- As relayed in the brief, the PI's framework: trustworthiness has only two routes, large-scale validation and precise quantification of every step of the computational framework; constrained optimization comes only after trustworthiness.

## Where it stands
Awaiting approval of the start-up plan; only desk work until then. Milestones: W2a audit table 10-27, W2b estimate draft 10-29.

# L29.3c Precise Quantification of Each Link in the Chain (Exploring)

This sub-project is work package W3 of the L29.3 plan v2, opened on 2026-10-24 at the PI's request to turn the plan's work packages into sub-projects. It addresses the PI's second pillar of trustworthy design: quantifying each link of the chain hazard, wind field/load, response, damage, loss/function, recovery. For each link it will record method error, parameter uncertainty, current magnitude with its source, data for separate validation, and room for reduction, then combine them into an uncertainty budget over 9 cells (single building/community/region × single event/annual/design reference period). A demonstration will compare StEER post-event damage surveys from Hurricane Michael (2018) with HAZUS damage states. The Lead agent wrote a start-up plan; no computation has been done.

- **2026-10-24**: Plan sets milestones: link table v0 on 10-28, demonstration pre-registration on 10-29, link table v1 and combined budget before 11-04.

- Turn the L29.3 plan v2 work packages into sub-projects (10-24).
- Framework: trustworthiness rests on large-scale validation plus precise quantification of every link; optimization under constraints comes only after that.

The plan awaits the PI's approval, including one Colab CPU demonstration run estimated at under 1 CU. A stated risk: none of the 161 existing records is confirmed as pure wind damage; if fewer than 30 comparable houses exist, only the gap will be reported.

# L29.3d Trustworthiness Criteria (Not started)

This sub-project is work package W4 of the L29.3 plan v2. It aims to combine the PI's two pillars, precise quantification of each step giving a predictive distribution and large-scale validation that checks calibration and detects uncovered bias, into operational graded criteria, then trial them on 3 to 5 published performance-based or resilience studies. The Lead agent's draft grades, with thresholds still to be set in v0, run from G0 (computation only) through G1 (per-step quantification with a combined prediction interval), G2 (one independent event with pre-set criteria, observation inside the interval), G3 (many events, adequate coverage, no unexplained systematic bias) to G4 (G3 plus anchoring to current code reliability and third-party reproducibility, modelled on why safety factors are trusted). Items a paper does not report are to be marked "not reported", not "not done". Trial candidates come from existing cards. No results yet.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-24**: Sub-project created at the PI's request; start-up plan written and reported to L29.3 (0 SU, 0 CU).

## What the PI decided
- Relayed in the brief: trustworthiness rests on two routes, large-scale validation and precise quantification of each step, with indicators layered by building, community and region and by single event, annual and design reference period.

## Where it stands
Awaiting approval. The G2 and G3 thresholds depend on L29.3b and L29.3c; if those are not delivered by 10-28 they will be marked "pending". Criteria v0 and the trial table are due 10-30.

projects.digest:
# L29.3e Does Performance-Based Design Still Save Money Under Multiple Loads? (Not started)

This sub-project is work package W5 of the L29.3 plan v2. W5a will gather evidence on whether current designs are "more than safe enough", treating tall-building main structures (for example component yielding at a return period of about 1135 years, and β≈3.0 from McAllister 2018) separately from low-rise envelopes, which often fail in hurricanes. W5b, following the PI's suggestion of mathematical modeling, will build an analytical model in which one resistance R must carry wind, earthquake, snow, gravity, deterioration and model or human error, and ask how much the failure probability under other actions rises when R is reduced by wind-only performance-based design, how the wind-only and all-hazard cost-optimal resistances differ, and how concurrent actions and deterioration amplify the gap, under both risk-consistent and minimum-total-cost criteria. Opposing evidence (Wen and Kang 2001, Nikellis 2019, Kleingesinds 2021) must be addressed directly. All parameters are labelled as assumptions and used only for sensitivity analysis. W5c will insert the performance-based relaxation (yield return period from about 1135 to 232 or 116 years) into W5b.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-24**: Sub-project created at the PI's request; the start-up plan was written and reported to L29.3, with the Lead agent recommending approval.

## What the PI decided
- Relayed in the brief: the PI views the cost-saving motive for performance-based design as questionable under multiple loads, and suggested mathematical modeling for W5b.

## Where it stands
Awaiting approval. Milestones: W5b model draft v0 on 10-27 (derivations first given an informal check by other models), W5a and W5c on 10-29.

projects.report:
# L29.4 结构优化与拓扑优化走向工程应用的条件

## 问题（Liang Hu 原话）
结构优化，拓扑优化这些，理论非常精巧，但是实际结构设计不愿意使用。这当然是由于安全第一的考虑。但这个合理吗？

## 对方结论的最强版本（复述）
头 claim。

## 我们的怀疑点
- 论文报告的节省（常见 10–30%，待核）多数来自**确定性**优化：把冗余（=未量化不确定性的储备）优化掉，同时让多个约束同时临界，系统可靠度下降；计入不确定性后节省可能大幅缩水。
- 可建造性（节点、标准截面、施工误差）、多荷载工况（风向、地震、施工阶段）在论文中常被简化。
- 规范验算体系是构件级的，优化结果仍需逐构件验算，优化的"全局最优"信息无处落地。
- 合理性判断：若在**同等可靠度**下仍有显著节省，"安全第一"就不是合理理由，属惯性——这是本课题要量化的。
（待检验）

## 判据（开始前写定）
- **对方成立（不用优化不合理）**：在 ≥1 个代表性风控高层上，计入风荷载与模型不确定性、约束为与常规设计相同的系统可靠度指标 β，并离散到标准截面后，优化方案材料节省仍 ≥8%。
- **部分成立**：节省在 3–8% 之间，或只在概念阶段（体系/支撑拓扑选择）显著、在构件尺寸阶段消失。
- **不成立**（安全第一合理）：同等可靠度下节省 <3%，或确定性优化方案的系统 β 显著低于常规设计（降幅 ≥0.5）。

## 第一步
1. litwiki 补卡 8–12 篇（含报告节省数字及其假设：确定性/可靠度、荷载工况数、是否离散化）；建"节省数字—假设"表，先看节省是否随假设的完整性递减。
2. 选一个公开的风控高层模型（如 CAARC 标准高层或文献模型），设计三种方案的对比计算框架。

## 需要的数据
公开高层模型与风荷载（CFD 线 CAARC 结果只读引用）；优化与可靠度计算在 CRC 单节点或 Colab。

## 预计工作量
文献 1–2 周；算例 3–4 周。

## 与其他课题
6c（结构优化算法众多）处理"算法谁更好"；本课题处理"优化本身值不值得用"，两者共用算例。

## 当前状态（10-16 23:50）
在做（Liang Hu 10-16 23:3x 批复全部课题开展基本工作）。第一周 10-17—10-23，按 的 L29.4 行。工作目录。
在跑委托

projects.brief: 你这个确实也做了一些工作，但是和我想的还有差距。这个应该首先广泛搜索风工程中优化的例子，看看到底有多少应用。注意，结构可以多种多样（桥梁，建筑，构筑物等，甚至阻尼器也可以），也可以是多荷载耦合，可以包含结构和拓扑优化，但是要点是，必须是在实际工程中得到了真实的应用，需要核实。其次才是分析原因，根据我前面给你提的原因和你自己找到的，每一个都进行仔细的分析；最好是针对第一步找到的典型应用（这时候可以放松为没有真实用过但是比较接近的）的例子，进行分析，需要针对不同类型的结构（元器件）、不同优化种类分别讨论：多大程度合理，多大程度惯性，如何从数学和可靠性、不确定分析的角度来建立模型。最后再讨论是否存在给定可靠度约束下的优化，能被工程接受，这是我们最终要根据分析提出来的解决办法。这是一个很大的课题，建议你分拆之后，用多个子项目开始研究，注意要用足量的搜索和文献。

# L29.4 Engineering Adoption of Structural and Topology Optimization (Exploring)

Project L29.4 examines why structural and topology optimization are rarely adopted in wind-engineering practice, whether "safety first" is a valid justification, and whether reliability-constrained optimization can be made acceptable to practitioners. Discrete member sizing on the public NIST 60-story reinforced concrete benchmark (7,800 members in 24 groups under 36 wind directions and 999 Miami hurricanes) compared looser (0.60 step-down threshold) and tighter (0.85 threshold, 8.0% to 11.4% cheaper) baselines against cost-optimized designs, while omitting column tension let the optimizer push column utilization to 3.98 versus 1.08. After a second six-reviewer panel rejected the draft v2 "partly holds" verdict (ruling that lateral-system concrete mass is the pre-registered main metric, cost cannot substitute for material, and interpolated or nearest points do not count as equal-reliability discrete designs), response draft v1 reported only about 8% to 10% savings over the looser baseline (concrete savings not yet settled under the strict reading; point-estimate |Deltabeta_U| le 0.26, 95% interval up to +0.295) and an undetermined 0% to 6% cost difference over the tighter baseline (from 0.25% more expensive to 5.2% saving at L1) by using more concrete in place of reinforcing steel, saving cost but not concrete, with carbon essentially unchanged. On 2026-10-21, the PI directed surveying real applications first, then analyzing causes, and finally formulating reliability-constrained solutions, splitting the work into L29.4a, L29.4b, and L29.4c. Limited to about 40 primary sources read, the audited 62-entry census in L29.4a found 9 built projects with primary designer or owner evidence (only 3 numerical optimization and 6 scheme comparisons), 0 with third-party verification, and 0 among 22 verified or near-application cases that considered uncertainty. Sub-project L29.4a is recommended for closure, while L29.4b and L29.4c continue.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16**: Project L29.4 opened; after PI approval, the Lead agent began literature reviews and benchmark selection.
- **2026-10-17**: Switched to the NIST 60-story benchmark shared with L29.6c, verified the 2D finite-element baseline within 0.10% to 0.14%, calibrated the 10-year wind speed to 45.32 m/s, and found that omitting column tension under 0.9D + 1.0W let the optimizer drive column utilization to 3.98 versus 1.08.
- **2026-10-18**: Redesigned four baselines with 150-storm by 200-sample reliability runs; after a six-reviewer panel rejected an initial draft verdict over search asymmetry and material trade-offs, eight symmetric reliability-capped optimizations were run.
- **2026-10-19**: A second six-reviewer panel rejected the draft v2 "partly holds" verdict (lateral-system concrete mass is the pre-registered main metric, cost cannot substitute for material, and interpolated points, nearest points with confidence intervals spanning zero such as Deltabeta = -0.009, or points with Deltabeta = +0.196 cannot count as equal-reliability discrete designs; at L1, the single verified discrete point with reliability at least matching the baseline saved 7.8% over the looser baseline but was 0.25% more expensive than the tighter baseline, versus 9.8% and 5.2% by interpolation). Draft v2 was withdrawn without classification, and after about 40 SU of jobs were submitted before the Lead agent saw the PI's 2026-10-19 pause order, compute halted.
- **2026-10-20**: Following the PI's redirection to stop classification runs, the Lead agent cancelled the planned ~130 SU supplementary run (no jobs were running) and delivered response draft v1.
- **2026-10-21**: In a goal-alignment audit, the Lead agent self-reported about 3 days and 400 SU of compute drift on verdict classification; the PI instructed surveying real applications first, then analyzing causes, and finally formulating reliability-constrained solutions, suggesting a split into sub-projects.
- **2026-10-22**: The PI approved L29.4a, L29.4b, and L29.4c; L29.4b delivered its 11-cause framework v1, and L29.4a completed its three-reviewer-audited 62-entry census (limited to about 40 primary sources read: 9 built projects with primary evidence comprising 2 member sizing, 1 closed-form damper parameter tuning, and 6 scheme comparisons; 0 with third-party verification; 13 near-applications; all 22 deterministic; gaps remaining in transmission towers, roofs and cladding, and Chinese literature).
- **2026-10-24**: Latest reports were surfaced per PI instruction, with L29.4a recommended for closure (pending the PI).

## What the PI decided
- Approved launching L29.4 ("create all and start basic work"), issued the 2026-10-19 pause order on unapproved compute, and endorsed the 2026-10-20 redirection to stop classification runs ("Good, proceed as you said").
- Required progress reports on 2026-10-21 to audit goal alignment and whether practical solutions had been found.
- Directed on 2026-10-21 to first broadly survey verified real-world optimization applications, then analyze causes via mathematical and reliability modeling, and finally study acceptable reliability-constrained optimization, approving L29.4a, L29.4b, and L29.4c on 2026-10-22.

## Where it stands
Sub-project L29.4a is recommended for closure (pending the PI), while the 60-story sizing study is retained as case input for L29.4b and L29.4c. Next steps are L29.4b modeling ideas due 2026-10-30 (and the cause matrix v0 over 4 structure types by 4 optimization types due 2026-11-03) and the L29.4c framework draft v0 due 2026-11-04, with one PI decision pending on whether to add a 100 to 200 SU topology or system optimization case.

## 问题（Liang Hu 原话）
现有的UQ（uncertainty quanfication）到底能完成什么任务？我不赞成对其方法进行过分研究，但是如何能利用现有的数据和基本方法，把它真正的用到工程中？

## 对方结论的最强版本（复述）
头 claim。

## 我们的怀疑点
- 风工程中真正影响决策的不确定性主要是：极值统计的抽样误差、风洞/CFD 到原型的模型误差、地貌与风向的情景不确定。这些用**基本方法**（bootstrap、蒙特卡洛、方差分解、简单贝叶斯更新、分项比对）就能量化到决策所需精度。
- 先进方法在已有算例上与基本方法给出的区间差异，常小于输入不确定性本身（输入分布定错比传播方法粗糙影响大得多）。
- 因此瓶颈是"有没有数据、问题定义是否清楚"，而非方法。
（待检验）

## 判据（开始前写定）
- **对方成立（先进方法必要）**：在 ≥3 个代表性风工程任务中，有 ≥2 个任务的先进方法与基本方法的结果差异足以**改变设计决策**（如设计风速/荷载分位值差 ≥5%，或排序改变），且差异不是由输入假设不同造成。
- **部分成立**：只在高维、计算极昂贵的任务（如 CFD 参数 UQ）先进方法有必要。
- **不成立**：所有任务中差异都不改变决策 → 交付"最小可用 UQ 流程"作为改造方案（remedy）。

## 第一步
1. 列出风工程 UQ 落地任务清单（设计风速置信区间、风洞到原型误差带、CFD 入流/湍流模型选择、峰值因子不确定性、结构响应可靠度），每项写：需要的数据、基本方法、决策用途。
2. 选 3 个任务做"基本 vs 先进"对比：(a) 极值风速 50 年值置信区间（bootstrap vs 贝叶斯层次）；(b) 风洞峰值压系数的不确定性（重复试验统计 vs 代理模型）；(c) CFD 入流参数 UQ（读 CFD 线已有结果，只读）。
3. 起草"最小可用 UQ 流程"一页。

| 10-17 | (c) 组 v4：对 FORM 不利的情形（同一风速驱动两种失效模式的串联系统，含窄带共振）；尝试 AK-MCS | Gumbel 场景下 FORM 偏高 14%/20%（两档 βt），**FORM 在此失效，方法选择在这里确实起作用**；1e4 档单设计点 IS 偏 −2%/−0.2%，子集模拟偏 −5%/−3%。GEV 场景 β3.8 档单设计点 IS 偏低约 10%（漏掉第二种失效模式），子集模拟有无效重复、离散宽。输入变化：分布族设错 −59%/−16%，阻尼 COV ±2%。参考积分仍漂移约 2%；AK-MCS 在 β4.7 档候选池需约 7700 万，没有结果。已派 v4b 补收敛、多设计点 IS 和 β3.8 档 AK-MCS |
| 10-17 | (c) 组 v3：OpenTURNS 子集模拟、SORM、FORM 交叉核对；AK-MCS 尝试 | 同预算下，基本法 FORM/FORM+IS 优于成熟库的子集模拟：1e3 档子集模拟偏 −11%～−31%；1e4 档中位偏 −1%～−4%，但重复间离散约 −25%～+36%，与 FORM 逐次差 ≥5% 的比例为 46%～94%。SORM 准确，但需 2000–5000 次调用。AK-MCS 没有有效结果。这是 FORM 的主场（光滑、低维、单设计点），已派 v4 补 FORM 不利的情形和忠实版 AK-MCS |
| 10-17 | (c) 组 v2：非线性风致响应（年最大风速 Gumbel/GEV，准静态 + 共振，模型误差），比较满足 βt=4.7/3.8 所需的设计抗力 | 风速分布族设错（真值 GEV ξ=0.1，按 Gumbel 算）使所需抗力低 71%/51%；阻尼 COV 0.3→0.5 只差约 2%。方法：1e4 次调用时 FORM 偏 −1.2%、FORM+IS 偏 −0.3%，两者没有一次重复差到 ≥5%；1e3 次时 24% 的重复差 ≥5%。粗 MC 在三档预算下都算不出（尾概率约 1e-6）。二阶 PCE 尾部低估约 38%，单步子集模拟只有 22/50 有效——实现偏弱，已派 v3 用成熟库重做。模型参数多为假设，未经校准 |
| 10-17 | (b) 组补充 v5：高斯峰值因子基线、短记录（训练 1/2/4 段） | 决定峰值估计好坏的是两件事：是否采用高斯假设（高斯法低估 18%～47%），以及记录长短。经验 Gumbel 分段峰值这种基本法，记录 ≥2 段时就够用；HPM 的内部口径离散（23%～46%）大于它带来的改进。初步读法（待真值 MC、待送审）：(b) 组的决策敏感项是模型形式和数据量，而不是 UQ 方法先进与否 |
| 10-17 | (b) 组复核 v4：上穿率三种口径、留出验证、加 225° 风向 | 经验 Gumbel 分段峰值稳健（覆盖 86%～93%，中位偏差 ±3%）；HPM 的差别取决于上穿率口径——原始计数偏高 33%，滤波后的结果又随风向变化——属于方法内部没有约束的设置，不是增益（单个模型、两个风向，待补短记录与高斯基线） |
| 10-17 | (b) 组 NIST m11 270° 峰值 Cp：Gumbel/BLUE 对比 Hermite/Sadek–Simiu 近似版 | 屋面 Hermite 比 Gumbel 高 16%～30%，迎风 ≤4.7%；但实现口径存疑（上穿率、gamma 尾部），正在复核 |
| 10-17 | (a) 组 v8 重算＋三条大值质控 | 三条大值都"可疑"（同日 METAR 里没有对应的阵风或雷暴）。v8 的 700 年：单站贝叶斯相对 MLE 为 −18.9%～+4.9%，层次为 −10.7%～+9.1%；而 GEV MLE 的 90% bootstrap 区间约为点估计的 −35%～+75%（如 DSM 69–165 kt）。**抽样不确定性比方法差异大好几倍（待真值 MC 检验）** |
| 10-17 | (a) 组四站小试（Iowa ASOS 2002–2025 年最大报告阵风，24 年/站；GEV/Gumbel MLE＋两种 bootstrap、单站贝叶斯、区域层次贝叶斯） | 50 年：换估计方法的差别在 ±5% 以内（单站贝叶斯 −4.8%～+2.0%，层次 −2.2%～+2.0%），换输入（只用最近 10 年）差 2%～24%，换分布族差 0.3%～9%。700/1700 年：方法差别升到 3%～23%，但分布族（最大 33%）、记录长度（最大 46%）、一条大值的质控（DSM 50 年值 77→99 kt、700 年 112→194 kt）的影响更大。方法差别主要来自 ξ 的先验和站间共享，不是纯算法差别。数据是报告阵风，不是规范设计风速；三条大值未核；bootstrap 只做了 120 次。**只是小试诊断，不作判据结论。** |

# T5 What UQ Can Actually Accomplish in Engineering

## Current Status (Week 1, 10-17 to 10-23, per)
Dispatched (10-17):
- better (delivered, verified by Lead): task inventory of 6 items, data reconnaissance, Group (a) four-station pilot test. Group (b) selected NIST-UWO m11 (1.33 GB, processed on Colab only); Group (c) has no pairable "inflow parameter to wind pressure" samples on this platform.
- better (partial delivery, accepted): METAR quality control results for all three large values are "questionable", raw track retained with screened track as primary; v8 four-station main table produced (bootstrap 1000 times, R-hat <=1.007, zero divergences); formal MC not delivered: measured runtime on the workstation is about 122 h, exceeding bounds.
- better (submitted, queued): formal ground-truth MC split into 27 single-core jobs and submitted, each 8 GiB, wall-clock cap 48 h, run root; resource application, revision; registered. 10-17 03:59 Lead checked qstat, all 27 queued (qw). Decision error rate changed to two-sided (decision record). **10-17 10:09 All 27 jobs failed at startup** (`module: command not found`; inferring run root from $0 was also buggy), no results, original run root retained. better L29.5-12 fixed the script (absolute paths, bash login shell), short test passed on 10-17 13:21 (exit code 0, both computation stages wrote results). **All 27 formal jobs submitted at 13:26 to 13:27** (resource application, run root, all registered, see record), all queued at 13:27; all running at 10-18 02:06. From 10-18 02:30 onward s00/s12/s15 finished first (exit code 0, MLE portion complete), **but Bayesian sampling was unqualified**: hierarchical model diverged in 62 to 79/100 replications, R-hat up to 3.1, minimum ESS 5. Bayesian results will not be interpreted before fixing. **Cause identified as our implementation defect rather than an issue with the method itself**: old code set log-likelihood outside the GEV support domain to a finite constant -1e6, creating flat regions, compounded by random initialization. Fix: change outside-support to true -inf, adapt_diag initialization, target_accept 0.995, 4 chains x 800 draws. Re-test on hard samples: 0 to 5 divergences / 3200 draws, R-hat <=1.0044, ESS >=1083. Therefore, old divergences **are not counted toward** the "usability cost of advanced methods"; only replications remaining unqualified after the fix are listed separately. Short test passed; 27 Bayesian re-run jobs all running as of 10-18 03:08 (resource application, run root). MLE portions of v3 original jobs collected as usual (9/27 completed as of 10-18 03:11). **10-18 09:17 All 27 fixed Bayesian jobs finished, with 8088 of 8100 method x replication runs passing diagnostic gates** (single-station weak 2700/2700, wide 2690/2700, hierarchical 2698/2700). 10-18 09:31 Lead verified: MLE stages of all 27 v3 scenarios are DONE; the remaining 18 original jobs are only running the voided old Bayesian portion, so they are neither canceled nor waited upon. Dispatched better L29.5-14 to produce the formal core table. Fallback follow-up: 10-18 around 04:00.
- better (delivered): Group (b) NIST m11 270 deg single record. At strongly non-Gaussian roof taps, Hermite is +16% to +30% higher than Gumbel, while at mildly non-Gaussian windward taps it is +0.1% to +4.7%; BLUE and Gumbel MLE differ by <=2.5%; truncating the record to 1/4 length has an effect of -17% to +5%; approximate Sadek-Simiu is 15% to 38% lower than Gumbel.
- better (delivered, verified by Lead): **Suspicion confirmed**. Hold-out validation (taking 4 of 16 segments for training and 12 for testing, rotated 4 times): Gumbel/BLUE on 270 deg/225 deg roof and facade groups achieved 86% to 93% coverage and -2.6% to +2.4% median bias, performing robustly. When HPM uses raw upcrossing counts, 270 deg roof coverage is only 39.9% with a +33.4% positive bias, **showing that the previously observed +16% to 30% was a bias caused by the upcrossing rate definition rather than a gain from an advanced method**. After low-pass filtering to 25 Hz, 270 deg roof improved (coverage 89.9%, +1.5%), but 225 deg roof worsened (66.7%, -23.6%), so no universal cutoff frequency can be selected. A faithful implementation of Sadek-Simiu is not achievable, so this column has been deleted. Evidence: 
- Group (c) changed to wind-induced structural reliability (basic vs advanced under equal budget), retaining CFD inflow as a candidate (decision record); better (L29.5-07) delivered v1 prototype: lognormal linear limit state, FORM is exact and tests nothing; crude MC at 100 calls has zero failures in 92% of replications; importance sampling has 12% rank reversal at 100 calls and about 4% relative RMSE at 1e3 calls. Compared quantities also did not align with criteria; v2 interrupted by gateway error, resent and delivered (see "Attempted and Results"); v3 delivered; dispatched v4 (scenarios unfavorable to FORM + faithful AK-MCS): interrupted by fetch failed, delivered after resending (partially completed); both gateway failures reported to platform Lead. v4b delivered (see "Attempted and Results"), concluding Week 1 work for Group (c); AK-MCS deferred to Week 2 as needed. v2 content: nonlinear wind-induced response, compared quantity changed to "design resistance required to meet beta_t", listing distribution family misspecification and damping COV variation side by side
- better (delivered, verified by Lead): (1) The Gaussian peak factor baseline generally underestimates across all four datasets (median -18% to -47%, hold-out coverage 2% to 31%), confirming that the critique "the basic Gaussian method underestimates peaks" holds on this dataset; (2) However, equally inexpensive empirical Gumbel/BLUE epoch peaks achieve 74% to 94% coverage and bias within +-4% when trained on >=2 segments, dropping to 43% to 90% coverage and -12% to -1% bias when only 1 segment remains; (3) HPM does not stably dominate on short records: when training on 1 segment for the 270 deg roof, only 6/24 folds satisfy monotonicity; the spread across 10 upcrossing rate definitions reaches 23% to 46% of the same-fold Gumbel median, exceeding any improvement it offers over Gumbel. Evidence:
- litwiki (delivered, accepted): the "basic practice" of US wind speed maps already borrows information across stations: Peterka & Shahid 1998 directly pool stations into superstations (method-of-moments Gumbel; 50-year sampling SD drops from about 5.8 mph at a single station to about 2.8 mph, journal pp. 209 to 210), and Pintar et al. 2015 use station-by-station POT plus spatial regression (NIST SP 500-301 pp. 24 to 28). **Therefore, when evaluating the gain of hierarchical Bayes, the control group is "naive pooling", while single-station MLE serves only as a reference.**
- litwiki (delivered, accepted): 8 new cards, index . Key points: Kareem 1988 shows differences among propagation methods are sometimes very small; Kikumoto 2021 shows deterministic and Bayesian ratings for pedestrian wind differ near threshold edges; Ciarlatani & Gorle 2025 show multi-fidelity reduces error, but the authors consider it unusable for final cladding design; Fawcett & Green 2018 show that the design quantity definition of "posterior mean vs posterior predictive" can cause a 1.4% to 9% difference. No study directly comparing design decisions between same-station bootstrap and hierarchical Bayes has yet been found. Added a fourth column "changing design quantity definition" to our reporting framework.
- Grok quick search (returned): clues: UQ enters standards mainly implicitly through load factors/return periods/partial factors; CFD inflow UQ and wind-induced reliability remain at the research level; **not found** any comparative study of "basic vs advanced methods on the same data reporting changes in design values"; some literature states input uncertainty (such as roughness) has a larger impact, while peak estimation method selection also has a practical impact on short records and strongly non-Gaussian wind pressures (counter-evidence, must be retained). All based on reading abstracts only, not used as basis. Citation check: the only "unfindable" DOI was a URL-encoded string for Gavanski 2016, which actually exists; first author of wes-9-1747-2024 is Verdonck, miswritten as Muller in the report.
- litwiki (delivered, accepted): 7 cards built and verified. Corrected three numbers from Grok against original texts: "15 peaks are enough" holds only under +-20% error and a specified duration (Gavanski 2016 PDF pp. 9, 12 to 13); inter-laboratory spread is 8% to 45% for frame bending moment and 8% to 30% for roof-corner negative peak (Fritz 2008 journal pp. 1888 to 1889); roughness misjudgment underestimates design wind load by 45% at 10 m (Nandi 2022 proof pp. 6 to 7). Input/data-level uncertainty is far larger in magnitude than the method differences seen so far (pending verification).
- Deep Research Step 2 (returned): advocacy-style, conclusions go further than evidence; item-by-item evaluation in . The only genuine "same-problem basic vs advanced" clue is Fawcett & Walshaw 2006 (single-station MLE vs regional Bayesian hierarchical): according to secondary summary, 50-year values differ by only about 0.3% to 0.5% between the two methods, with differences concentrated in >=200-year extrapolation (one number suspected of transcription error). The non-Gaussian peak examples compare "model form", not UQ methods per se.
- litwiki (delivered, accepted): Fawcett & Walshaw 2006 original table verified (journal p. 644 Table 4). Hierarchical Bayes relative to single-station MLE: Bradfield 50-year +0.2%, 1000-year +13%; Nottingham 50-year -11.5%, 1000-year -20%. **This is counter-evidence: exceeding 5% already at 50 years on the same dataset**, though without ground truth, and the difference comes from borrowing information across stations, to be tested via known-truth Monte Carlo and comparison against "current pooling practice". The 74.0/117.7 cited by DR is a transcription error on a poster, voiding the "86%" derived by DR from it. The 2.2 to 2.5x in Duthinh 2018 holds only in specified regions and compares direct database calculation against standard clauses.
- **Reporting framework (criteria unchanged)**: results reported in three columns: changing estimation/propagation method only, changing model form, and changing input; whether model-form differences count as "advanced method gain" will be reported under both classifications upon review submission.
Evaluation checklist: L31.6's v0 already includes our 5 critical items (6 to 10). One point pending alignment: its Item 4 "exceeding existing uncertainty band" differs in definition from this page's criterion "quantile difference >=5% or ranking change", to be aligned with L31.6 via root conversation at the end of Week 1 (this page's criterion remains unchanged).

- **Evaluation checklist v1 (aligned 10-17; upgraded to v1.2 on 10-18, Item 4 writes bandwidths separately by return period, reported alongside this page's 5% criterion)**: v1 agreed. Items 0, 11, and 12 are also adopted by our side; for Item 11, method families unrelated to wind-hazard physics such as optimization algorithms and surrogate models are marked "Not applicable" with a one-sentence reason. Also proposed three modifications to the other side: mark the roughly 30 events in Item 12 as this project's convention; Item 4 should distinguish between "impact smaller than uncertainty band" and "uncertainty band too wide to judge", recording the latter as "Unassessed"; state explicitly that veto items are failing Item 6 (complete equivalence) or failing Item 8. T5's criterion (quantile difference >=5% or ranking change) remains unchanged and is reported alongside Item 4.

**Week 1 Summary (10-18)**: . Formal core table of ground-truth MC produced: in five-station scenarios, hierarchical Bayes and naive regional pooling have comparable point estimation accuracy (median RMSE 6.5%/12.3%/14.9% vs 7.2%/11.4%/13.1%), though point estimates of the two methods often differ by >5%; the value of hierarchical Bayes lies in interval calibration (coverage 0.86 to 0.89, vs naive pooling parametric bootstrap 0.59 to 0.74; corrected on 10-21, originally written 0.57 to 0.71 was the non-parametric version).

**10-21 Liang Hu expansion**: requested surveying the current state of UQ methods by scenario (especially UQ for CFD simulations), selecting benchmark cases for coding comparison, and connecting to real wind engineering needs to build applications; subprojects may be split out. Launch plan (splitting into L29.5a landscape and framework / 5b CFD UQ / 5c benchmark comparison / 5d engineering application) pending approval by Liang Hu; literature only before approval (Grok quick search sent). Decision .

**10-20 Redirection**: no longer classifying into tiers, supplementary ground-truth experiments and six-model review canceled; changed to delivering a response draft (implementation checklist + minimal viable UQ workflow), due 10-24. Progress and plan report: .

## Attempted and Results
| Date | Action Taken | One-Sentence Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-17 | Group (c) v4b: reference truth convergence (adjacent refinement change <=0.04%), recalculation against new truth, multi-design-point IS, AK-MCS feasibility | Against converged truth: under Gumbel scenario FORM overestimates by +16.3%/+19.9% (conclusion firmer than v4); single-design-point IS bias -0.3%/-0.02%; subset simulation bias -3.5%/-2.8%. Under GEV, beta 3.8 scenario single-design-point IS underestimates by -10.6%/-10.8%, improved by multi-design-point IS to -3.1%/-2.7%, **but the same multi-point scheme underestimates by -28% in the Gumbel, beta 4.7 scenario**, showing no single method is stable across all scenarios and advanced methods require problem-specific tuning, which itself introduces new uncertainty. Input: distribution family misspecification -60%/-16%, damping COV +1% to +2%. Self-written AK-MCS smoke test did not pass stopping criterion, stopped per task brief (recorded as NA) |
| 10-17 | Group (c) v4: scenario unfavorable to FORM (series system with two failure modes driven by the same wind speed, including narrowband resonance); attempted AK-MCS | Under Gumbel scenario FORM overestimates by 14%/20% (two beta_t levels), **where FORM fails and method selection genuinely matters**; at 1e4 budget single-design-point IS bias is -2%/-0.2%, subset simulation bias is -5%/-3%. Under GEV scenario at beta 3.8 level, single-design-point IS underestimates by about 10% (missing the second failure mode), and subset simulation has invalid replications and wide spread. Input changes: distribution family misspecification -59%/-16%, damping COV +-2%. Reference integral still drifts by about 2%; AK-MCS candidate pool at beta 4.7 level requires about 77 million points, yielding no result. Dispatched v4b to supplement convergence, multi-design-point IS, and beta 3.8 AK-MCS |
| 10-17 | Group (c) v3: OpenTURNS subset simulation, SORM, FORM cross-check; AK-MCS attempt | Under equal budget, basic methods FORM/FORM+IS outperform mature-library subset simulation: at 1e3 budget subset simulation bias is -11% to -31%; at 1e4 budget median bias is -1% to -4%, but inter-replication spread is about -25% to +36%, differing from FORM by >=5% in 46% to 94% of runs. SORM is accurate but requires 2000 to 5000 calls. AK-MCS yielded no valid result. This is FORM's home turf (smooth, low-dimensional, single design point), so dispatched v4 to supplement a scenario unfavorable to FORM and faithful AK-MCS |
| 10-17 | Group (c) v2: nonlinear wind-induced response (annual maximum wind speed Gumbel/GEV, quasi-static + resonant, model error), comparing design resistance required to meet beta_t=4.7/3.8 | Wind speed distribution family misspecification (true GEV xi=0.1, computed as Gumbel) lowers required resistance by 71%/51%; changing damping COV from 0.3 to 0.5 differs by only about 2%. Methods: at 1e4 calls FORM bias is -1.2% and FORM+IS bias is -0.3%, with zero replications differing by >=5%; at 1e3 calls 24% of replications differ by >=5%. Crude MC cannot compute at any of the three budget levels (tail probability about 1e-6). Second-order PCE underestimates the tail by about 38%, and single-step subset simulation had only 22/50 valid runs: weak implementation, dispatched v3 to redo with a mature library. Model parameters are mostly assumed and uncalibrated |
| 10-17 | Group (b) supplement v5: Gaussian peak factor baseline, short records (training on 1/2/4 segments) | Peak estimation quality is governed by two things: whether the Gaussian assumption is used (Gaussian method underestimates by 18% to 47%), and record length. A basic method like empirical Gumbel epoch peaks suffices when records have >=2 segments; HPM's internal definition spread (23% to 46%) exceeds any improvement it brings. Preliminary reading (pending ground-truth MC and review): decision-sensitive items in Group (b) are model form and data volume, not whether the UQ method is advanced |
| 10-17 | Group (b) verification v4: three upcrossing rate definitions, hold-out validation, adding 225 deg wind direction | Empirical Gumbel epoch peaks are robust (coverage 86% to 93%, median bias +-3%); HPM differences depend on upcrossing rate definition, where raw counts overestimate by 33% and filtered results vary with wind direction, representing unconstrained internal method settings rather than gains (single model, two wind directions, pending short-record and Gaussian baseline supplements) |
| 10-17 | Group (b) NIST m11 270 deg peak pressure coefficient Cp: Gumbel/BLUE vs Hermite/approximate Sadek-Simiu | Roof Hermite is 16% to 30% higher than Gumbel, windward <=4.7%; but implementation definitions are questionable (upcrossing rate, gamma tail), currently under verification |
| 10-17 | Group (a) v8 recalculation + quality control of three large values | All three large values are "questionable" (no corresponding gust or thunderstorm in same-day METAR). In v8 at 700-year return period: single-station Bayes relative to MLE is -18.9% to +4.9%, hierarchical is -10.7% to +9.1%; whereas the 90% bootstrap interval of GEV MLE is about -35% to +75% of the point estimate (e.g., DSM 69 to 165 kt). **Sampling uncertainty is several times larger than method differences (pending ground-truth MC test)** |
| 10-17 | Group (a) four-station pilot test (Iowa ASOS 2002 to 2025 annual maximum reported gusts, 24 years/station; GEV/Gumbel MLE + two bootstraps, single-station Bayes, regional hierarchical Bayes) | At 50 years: differences from changing estimation method are within +-5% (single-station Bayes -4.8% to +2.0%, hierarchical -2.2% to +2.0%), changing input (using only the most recent 10 years) differs by 2% to 24%, changing distribution family differs by 0.3% to 9%. At 700/1700 years: method differences rise to 3% to 23%, but distribution family (up to 33%), record length (up to 46%), and quality control of a single large value (DSM 50-year value 77->99 kt, 700-year 112->194 kt) have larger impacts. Method differences stem mainly from the prior on xi and inter-station sharing, not pure algorithmic differences. Data are reported gusts rather than code design wind speeds; three large values unverified; bootstrap ran only 120 replications. **Pilot diagnostic only, not a criterion conclusion.** |

projects.goal:
1. Landscape table: classify wind engineering UQ by "application scenario (8) × UQ stage (7)"; each cell lists existing methods, maturity (in codes / engineering practice / research), how much results differ between methods (literature figures + cards + page numbers), and whether open-source implementations exist.
2. Unified framework: bring error analysis, mesh convergence/GCI, LES sampling error, V&V and validation metrics, wind tunnel repeatability / inter-laboratory comparisons, multi-model ensembles, and "differences between results of different UQ methods" into a single framework, stating the correspondences and "what counts as UQ and what does not". Each of the two includes "recommendations for 5b/5c benchmark selection". Milestone: deliver to parent project L29.5 on 10-28.

# L29.5a UQ 全景与统一框架

编号：L29.5a · 状态：在做（Liang Hu 10-22 批 A197，方案 第 1 节目标 1–2、第 2 节 L29.5a 行）
停止类别：—

## 目标

G3c grid finished computing on cluster, but reference integration did not converge (insufficient tail-integration resolution); remaining post-processing moved to workstation using the 318 KB grid (L29.5c-16, 15-minute time limit). G1b is still running on cluster, with monitoring temporarily unreadable.**

## Decisions Made
- 10-22 Benchmarks C1-C6 and operational definitions of decision terms finalized (v0); Week 1 results reused without recomputation -> see Design v0 Sections 1-2.
- 10-22 C4 realistic-structure version: load side uses NIST `HR_DAD_RC` + matching-geometry CAARC story forces (36 wind directions); resistance dispersion does not pursue true critical-column distributions, instead using three lognormal COV sensitivity tiers (0.10/0.15/0.20). Rationale: the question is whether the limit state of a realistic high-rise resembles a "single smooth design point" or "multiple design points", which is governed by the load side and wind directionality.
- 10-22 C2 area averaging: m11 is used only for 9 m^2; 0.9/2 m^2 switch to NIST-UWO jp1 (TN1903 has a 1 ft spacing dense zone), verifying the actual number of groups in the first wind direction and reporting realizable areas without interpolation if 0 groups match. The TPU low-rise database has a 2 m grid spacing and is not used for small areas.
- 10-22 C4 evaluated model uses a `(V, Θ, ζ)` grid-interpolation model (reference ground truth and all compared methods use the exact same model); conclusions address only "differences among methods" without reporting absolute β for the real structure; if there is only a single smooth design point, method comparison is run at one tier only.
- 10-22 Added 8 large-|ξ| scenarios to C1 (Week 1 ground-truth shapes favored Bayesian estimation).
- 10-22 Changed C1 generator to Poisson-GPD (annual maxima strictly follow the true scenario GEV): POT requires threshold exceedances, whereas Week 1 saved only annual maxima so samples could not be reused. Only the four frequentist methods are rerun on the original 27 scenarios (paired on the same new samples); hierarchical Bayes is not rerun and is compared against Week 1 results on marginal metrics only, unpaired. Trade-off: Bayes and POT lack paired differences and can be compared only on marginal metrics such as coverage and RMSE.
- 10-22 Released by parent project (G1 -> G4).

projects.report:
# T6 同一任务多方法：聚合、分解、比较

## 问题（Liang Hu 原话）
有很多任务，对于某一个任务，人们发展了数不清的方法，那些方法真的都有用吗？是否可以把这些方法聚合起来，分解。比较？注意这些方法在数学上经常是站的住脚的，这和气候变化的那种多路径不同。几个例子和我的研究相关：时程的随机模拟（包括inflow）；台风的路径和强度模型（特别是给风工程用的）；结构优化算法；数不清的动力和CFD的surrogate，真的都有用吗？这里面需要基准平台并且明确比较或者综合的方向和目的。我选择的PINO当然是觉得它真的有用。你后续还可以列举很多这种小的topic，重重叠叠，重复研究。

## 共用判据（开始前写定，各子课题按此判）
对每个方法族，先定**比较目的**（三选一，写进子课题节）：选出一个 / 组合使用 / 证明等价。然后：
- **对方成立（方法多样性有用）**：在统一基准上，≥1/3 的方法在至少一个**工程相关**指标上显著（超出随机种子/重复间离散的 2 倍）优于族内基线，且优势区间可以用问题特征（谱形、非平稳度、维度、数据量）预先说明。
- **部分成立**：少数方法（< 1/3）有可预言的优势区间，其余等价或劣于基线。
- **不成立（冗余为主）**：多数方法可证明为同一骨架的参数化变体，或在统一基准上与基线差异不超过离散的 2 倍。
- 方法"在作者自选算例上占优、统一基准上不占优"记为"适用范围极窄"，不记为"错误"。

## 6a 风速时程随机模拟（含 CFD 入流生成）
- **比较目的**：证明等价（主）＋ 选型指南。
- **怀疑**：SRM、AR、POD、小波等在二阶统计意义上可互相转换；多数"新方法"是采样或分解组件的替换。
- **第一步**：画谱系图（骨架：目标谱/相干/演变谱 → 分解（Cholesky/POD/小波）→ 随机相位/幅值 → 合成（FFT/递推））；建低成本基准：解析谱（Kaimal/von Kármán + Davenport 相干）＋ 1–2 组公开实测（非平稳例：下击暴流），指标：谱、相干、高阶矩、极值分布、计算成本。
- **数据**：解析谱、公开实测；工作站 小数据或 Colab。
- **10-22 分出四类子项目（启动方案 Liang Hu 10-22 批，A197）**：L29.6a1 平稳高斯、a2 平稳非高斯、a3 非平稳高斯、a4 非平稳非高斯（起步晚两周）；里程碑 1 为各类分类表＋推导核查清单（a1–a3 约 10-30，a4 约 11-04），6a 汇成分类总表 v1（10-30）。
- **与核心实验室分工（10-16 已定，同意）**：CFD 入流生成的等效性和适用性研究、基准，以及合成入流生成器的出口统计检验（谱、相干、积分尺度、雷诺应力、散度，不跑 CFD）**归核心实验室课题 3**（决定；只读引用）。本实验室不另建 CFD 入流基准，也不跑入流 CFD。面向结构分析的随机时程模拟谱系与基准**归 6a**。谱系图中 CFD 入流一支的结论直接引用核心实验室的结果。比较指标两边用同一口径：核心实验室课题 3 开题卡定稿时发来指标清单，6a 基准按那份清单对表。入流生成器的开发和 LBM 计算仍归 与 PETW CFD 线。

## 6b 台风路径与强度模型（面向风工程）
- **比较目的**：选型（按风工程用途：设计风速 / 事件情景）＋ 识别等价。
- **怀疑**：对**设计风速**这一输出，不同路径模型的差异可能小于参数风场模型（Holland B、衰减模型、边界层模型）和气候数据年限带来的差异——即"路径模型泛滥"对风工程意义很小，瓶颈在风场模型。
- **第一步**：谱系分解为五个组件（生成/路径/强度/登陆衰减/风场），逐组件替换做敏感性（方差分解），看设计风速方差主要来自哪一环。
- **数据**：IBTrACS；公开的合成路径集（如 STORM 数据集，待核可得性）；风场线/EVA 线结果只读引用。

## 6c 结构优化算法
- **比较目的**：证明等价/冗余（主）。
- **怀疑**：大量"新元启发式算法"在标准桁架/框架基准上与成熟方法（OC/MMA，或调好参数的 GA/PSO）差异在随机离散内；"新"在比喻而非机理。
- **第一步**：用公开标准基准（10/25/72 杆桁架，及一个风控高层尺寸优化）、相同函数评估预算，比较 6–10 个代表算法；与 T4 共用风控高层算例。
- **数据**：公开基准；Colab/CRC 单节点。
- **10-22**：问题—方法矩阵 v1 已过三审，分出 c1–c5 并获批（A197）。6c5 文献底稿：结构领域已有人做过算法选择（Clune 2013 博士论文，卡片），因此“算法选择在结构领域是新的”**不得再说**；6c5 的贡献只能落在风工程真实问题上的选法/调优规则。

## 6d 结构动力与 CFD 代理模型（含 PINO 的定位）
- **比较目的**：选型（按数据量、外推需求、物理约束）＋ 明确 PINO 的优势区间。
- **怀疑**：在**插值**（训练分布内）任务上，多数代理（GP、POD-ROM、CNN、FNO）精度相近，差异主要来自数据量和预处理；真正区分方法的是**外推**（新几何、新雷诺数/风向）和数据稀缺情形——PINO 若有用，应在这里体现。
- **PINO**：Liang Hu 认为有用；本课题把它当待检验对象之一同等对待，判据同上；若其在外推/少数据上可预言地占优，结论写"成立"并给出优势区间。
- **第一步**：谱系分解（降维表示 × 回归器 × 物理约束方式 × 训练数据保真度）；统一基准：一个风压场任务（公开风洞数据库，如 TPU）＋ 一个结构动力响应任务，划分插值/外推两种测试集，同训练预算。
- **数据**：TPU 等公开数据；liang2 共享库代理文献；GPU 用 Colab。

- **与核心实验室课题 6（概率方法用进风工程）分工（10-16 同意并补充）**：核心实验室负责正向移植与落地（从概率工程力学 PEM、海岸 JPM/多灾种、地震 PSHA/PBEE/条件谱/IDA 里挑方法，做风工程试金石算例）；本实验室负责批判与聚合（T6 多方法并存、T5 最小可用 UQ、T3 的 3d 环节框架与不确定性预算）。方法作为工具出现在 3d 框架里时，它在风工程中适用与否引用对方课题 6 的结论。评判清单两边共用一份，放 下，本方只读引用。补充约定：(a) 对方判为"无用/冗余"的方法族名单，到本方只算**候选**，要批判须先经 Liang Hu 点头开题，并按本实验室判据补齐证据；(b) 两边碰到同一方法族、预判可能相反时（例如本方 T5 怀疑先进 UQ 不改变决策，对方要证明它有增益），用同一个试金石算例和同一份清单，由一方计算、另一方复核，不各算各的。

## 候选小课题（同类"重重叠叠"，交 Liang Hu 选，未开题）
| 候选 | 多方法并存的表现 | 怀疑点 | 备注 |

| 峰值因子/非高斯极值估计 | Davenport、Sadek–Simiu、Hermite 矩、平移过程、POT、各种修正 | 等价/冗余 | 初步边界：非高斯风压模拟方法及其对幕墙的影响归核心实验室，极值估计方法的谱系比较归本实验室；Liang Hu 点选时双方再对齐 |
| 极值分布拟合与阈值选择 | Gumbel/GEV/GPD + 数十种阈值选法 | 差异小于抽样误差 | 与 T5 相关 |
| 非平稳风速分解（时变均值提取） | EMD/EEMD/小波/核平滑/各种自适应 | 结果强依赖人为参数 | |
| 台风参数风场模型 | Holland B 及大量修正、各边界层模型 | 意义很小 | 可并入 6b |
| 风压场 POD/DMD/SPOD 变体 | 多种分解与"改进" | 等价 | |
| 模态参数识别（实测） | SSI、FDD、ERA、贝叶斯 FFT 等变体 | 等价 | |
| 桥梁气动导数识别 | 各种时域/频域识别算法 | 识别误差小于试验离散 | |
| TMD/阻尼器参数优化公式 | Den Hartog 之后大量"最优"公式 | 意义很小 | |
| 风洞/CFD 风压插值与预测 | ANN/GP/各类 ML 回归 | 与 6d 重叠 | 可并入 6d |
| 下击暴流解析风场模型 | 多种经验/解析剖面 | 适用范围窄 | |
| 风荷载等效静力方法 | LRC、ESWL 多种变体 | 等价 | |

# L29.6a 风速时程随机模拟（结构分析用）

## 子项目（10-22 建，A197 范围内）
| 编号 | 名称 | 对话前缀 | 状态 |

## 目标
把结构分析用的风速时程随机模拟方法（SRM、AR/ARMA、POD、小波、演变谱/非平稳/非高斯变体）按共同骨架分解，在低成本统一基准上判等价与优势区间。

## 当前状态
**10-22 Liang Hu 批准启动方案 v2（A197），状态在做**；已建 a1–a4 子项目。本层：共用文献普查（清单 v5，含引文滚雪球）、基准规则、最后汇总选法表。里程碑 M1（10-30）：分类总表 v1＋理论可判清单；M2（11-04）：基准设计 v2 冻结。
**10-21 Liang Hu 指示重构**（决策 Hu指示重构为四类普查与基准_20261021.md）：按平稳高斯/平稳非高斯/非平稳高斯/非平稳非高斯四类做文献普查（近年+相邻领域）→ 分类 → 推导核查 → 实现（Python/MATLAB）→ 典型问题基准（误差与速度）；建议拆 L29.6a1–a4（启动方案 v2 待 Liang Hu 定）；inflow 交 L31.3。10-21 已发四份 Grok 快查（19_文献普查/briefs/）。
**10-20 更新**：按课题重定向，本子项目改为给 T6 回答稿供素材，不再以档位/六审为目标；初判已交。新计算（非高斯支等）等 T6 回答稿交 Liang Hu 并经其看过后再定；无在跑作业或。以下为历史记录。
在做（Liang Hu 10-16 批复开展基本工作）。第一周 10-17 至 10-23：谱系初稿 + 数据摸底 + 文献补卡；基准设计等 L29.6 统一基准模板到后再落。10-17 已派：L29.6a-01 Grok 快查已回（只是线索，见「试过与结果」）；L29.6a-04 Deep Research 已回（线索核对见）；L29.6a-02 litwiki 奠基文献建卡已交（18 篇，仅 2 篇有原文页码；Lead 接受，自动初查'缺清单'是回复未逐列，索引里齐全）；L29.6a-08 literature 补全文已交（6/11 入 Zotero；ScienceDirect 人工验证码挡住 5 篇）；L29.6a-09 litwiki 六篇原文回填已交（索引 v3；Lead 抽查 Ubertini Table 2/3 数值与原文 PDF p.15 一致）；L29.6a-03 better 谱系初稿与数据摸底已交（10-17 01:1x，Lead 抽查数据口径通过）；L29.6a-05 组件等价条件解析推导备忘已交（10-17 01:46，Lead 抽查公式通过）；L29.6 统一基准模板 v0 已出，L29.6a-06 基准设计 v0 已交并采纳，B9 事先声明 10-17 02:16 冻结（sha256 记于）。L29.6a-07 小试已交：解析自检过、原文闸门未过、发现指标估计器有偏。L29.6a-10 已交：A5/A6 估计规则在 Kaimal 长记录上通过留出自检并冻结规则；A4 未过；Ubertini 例1 缺目标参数，三法原文闸门未过。L29.6a-12 已交：M0 原文闸门通过（限定）入分母；10 min 的 A6/A4 记 NA（决策 L29.6a_M0入分母与短记录指标限定_20261017）。审稿人 E/F 查 Ubertini 例1 参数；L29.6a-11 literature 补全文已交：两篇均取不到（ScienceDirect 验证码/403、机构库关闭）。审稿人 F（Grok）10-17 回：Ubertini 例1 九点坐标、z0、各点均速、Solari–Piccardo 常数、相干系数、方差均查不到（只确认原文给顶部 48.0 m/s、对数剖面未给 z0、Δt=0.05 s）；审稿人 E（Gemini）10-17 回：从原文 PDF 矢量图读出九点高度、平均风速、σ，同课题组文献给出 Solari–Piccardo 谱式（Lead 核 Tubino & Solari 2020 PDF p.6 常数一致），相干系数有矛盾按假设做敏感性；整理成参数重建包，已派 L29.6a-14 重建例1并做 M1/M4 型/M3 多变量原文对照（写入 例1重建/）。任务书原文存。第一周末 10-23 向 L29.6 --report。开题内容（比较目的、怀疑点、第一步、数据）见父页 T6「6a 风速时程随机模拟」节。

## 边界
CFD 入流生成的等效性、基准和生成器出口检验归核心实验室课题 3（只读引用）；本子项目不建 CFD 入流基准、不跑入流 CFD；比较指标按核心实验室发来的清单对表。

## 与 L31.3 共用的比较指标口径（10-17 对表）
以核心实验室 的第 0 节和 A1–A6 为准（只读引用）。D 节 6 条全部同意，补三处细化：
- 相干拟合用两点平均高度处的平均风速；间距按结构特征尺寸归一，建筑取 H，桥梁取跨度或节段长。
- 谱的频带要覆盖所分析结构的前几阶频率；随机模拟一侧报的截止频率是模拟时设定的上限频率，与 CFD 的分辨截止含义不同，两者分开写。
- 「不可分辨」只在同一无量纲总时长下成立，报告必须写明时长，不能当作一般意义的「等价」。随机模拟的抽样误差也按单条记录等分 10 段计算，和 CFD 同一口径；样本间离散另报。
6a 另外自己采用、并请 L31.3 一起报的两项：(E1) 偏度和峰度；(E2) 计算成本，口径为每生成 10^6 个「点×时间步」所用的墙钟秒数，注明硬件。只在 6a 内部用的：非平稳算例的时变均值/时变标准差误差，以及参考结构（单自由度或高层）响应的均方根值和峰值。

projects.brief: 你这些探索很好，但是还差的比较远。主要原因是你没有深入搜寻最近的文献和相近邻域的文献。这种分为几种：平稳过程，平稳非高斯过程（一般为风压），非平稳高斯过程（一般为台风、雷暴等），非平稳非高斯过程（一般为前二者的组合）；inflow的模拟这里不涉及，交给L31.3就行。这些近年来已经发展成一个非常庞大的研究领域，虽然我觉得大部分都是完全不需要进行的研究，因为早期的方法就已经可以用了。深入搜索文献后，需要分类（除了不同的随机特征外，模拟方法也有多种），然后仔细检查各种方法的推导是否正确，能否编程实现。这方面可以用matalb编程也行，你可以自行选用。最后，选择一些风工程中的典型问题，作为benchmark，用这些实现的方法来进行比较，一般为误差和速度。有些比较从其理论就能分出优劣。你考虑一下，可以分拆为几个子项目进行。

# L29.6a Stochastic Simulation of Wind Speed Time Histories (for Structural Analysis)

## Objective
Decompose stochastic simulation methods for wind speed time histories used in structural analysis (SRM, AR/ARMA, POD, wavelets, evolutionary spectrum/non-stationary/non-Gaussian variants) according to a common skeleton, and determine equivalence and advantage regimes on a low-cost unified benchmark.

## Current Status
**10-22 Liang Hu approved launch plan v2, status In Progress**; subprojects a1 to a4 established. At this level: shared literature census (inventory v5, including citation snowballing), benchmark rules, and final summary method-selection table. Milestone M1 (10-30): classification master table v1 + theoretically decidable inventory; M2 (11-04): benchmark design v2 freeze.
**10-21 Restructured per Liang Hu's instruction** (Decision): conduct literature census (recent years + adjacent fields) across four categories (stationary Gaussian / stationary non-Gaussian / non-stationary Gaussian / non-stationary non-Gaussian) -> classification -> derivation verification -> implementation (Python/MATLAB) -> typical problem benchmarks (error and speed); recommended splitting into L29.6a1 to a4 (launch plan v2 pending decision by Liang Hu); inflow handed over to L31.3. Sent four Grok quick searches on 10-21.
**10-20 Update**: following project redirection, this subproject changed to supplying material for the T6 response draft, no longer targeting tier classification/six-model review; initial judgment delivered. New computations (such as the non-Gaussian branch) will be decided after the T6 response draft is submitted to and reviewed by Liang Hu; no running jobs. Below is the historical record.

# L29.6a4 Non-Stationary Non-Gaussian Wind Simulation (Active)

This sub-project covers the combined class of stochastic wind simulation: non-stationary and non-Gaussian processes such as thunderstorm or typhoon pressures and non-Gaussian wind speeds. It asks what recent specialized methods gain over simple early approaches. These are a stationary non-Gaussian process times a time-varying envelope (S1); a non-stationary Gaussian process with a pointwise marginal transform, without (S2a) or with (S2b) correction of the underlying correlation; and, added later, piecewise stationary non-Gaussian simulation stitched together (S3). The PI's own earlier code belongs to S2b. The work is literature-based so far, with no computation. From 30 literature cards (12 checked against the original, 18 only screened), the Lead agent drafted a classification of 8 method families. Its inference, still to be checked, is that the three largest families (about 18 papers) stay within the early pointwise-transform framework and change only one step. The only measured validation found so far supports the simple stitching approach, with errors under 10% in one wind-tunnel turntable study.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-22**: The sub-project started under the approved parent plan. The Lead agent wrote five theoretical predictions to check by 10-30. One is that iterative correction methods help only when targets are incompatible. A 2015 paper read in full showed errors of 0.014% and 0.23% for compatible targets and 35% and 40% after iteration for incompatible ones.
- **2026-10-22**: Full texts were obtained for 5 of 19 papers; 14 were blocked by publisher rate limits or security checks. A performance-based wind engineering paper turned out to use the stitching approach, so the Lead agent added S3 as a baseline.
- **2026-10-22**: Eight verified cards were built. Fourteen cards could not be built because cloud-stored PDFs had not synced locally; after export and checksum verification they were sent for card building.
- **2026-10-22**: A 2025 validation study of the stitching approach (512 taps, 6 rates of wind-direction change) reported all spectral errors within 10%. The Lead agent noted this holds only for that wind-tunnel data. The non-stationary data are available only on request from the authors. Contacting them is the PI's decision, so the thunderstorm/typhoon benchmark would be calibrated on public stationary data.
- **2026-10-22**: Classification v0 (8 families) was written. The parent project ran one merged citation snowball for all four classes (pool of 11432, 306 included) and told sub-projects not to run their own.
- **2026-10-24**: Status: about 40% of the 10-30 milestone was done. The five theoretical checks had not started.

## What the PI decided
- On 10-21, the PI said stochastic wind simulation has become a huge field, most of which need not be done, and early methods are mostly enough. The PI asked for recent and neighboring literature to be searched, classified, checked derivation by derivation for correctness and implementability, and benchmarked on typical wind-engineering problems.
- Approved the parent L29.6a start-up plan v2 on 10-22, which covers this sub-project.
- Asked on 10-24 for every project's latest report to be brought to the front.

## Where it stands
Milestone a4-M1 (classification v1 plus results of the five theoretical checks) is due 10-30. It will add this class's entries from the merged snowball, and the benchmark design is due to be frozen on 11-04. Fourteen key papers remain blocked; the PI could download them with university access if willing.
