- 10-17 检查点一（Vickery 2010 Fig.4）不再追：记为方向复现、量级未复现；第 2 层继续推进，但把 A×W 交互列为必须估计的项。依据：trial04–06 三轮诊断，剩余差距与原文专有模型（路径集、边界层）相关，继续追成本高于其价值。错了的代价：若交互实际很小而量级差另有原因（如我们的风场实现有误），第 2 层的风场效应会被系统低估——用检查点二（Hong, Kareem & Li 2020 Rmax 切换）交叉核对。
- 10-18 TCRM 现配置不作第 2 层底座（trial08 闸门未通过）。下一步并行两条：①给 TCRM 一轮有限修正（用 EBTRK/IBTrACS 重拟合、查压力演化与环境气压），修正后两个种子重过同一闸门；②向 WRF 线问 ERA5 是否已在集群上，评估 FAST 路线。一轮修不过就转 FAST。错了的代价：修 TCRM 白花 2–3 天，或 FAST 的输入准备比预期更重。
- 10-18 **第 2 层工程暂停，先做第 1 层预试验**。三个候选平台（TCRM、STORM 代码、FAST）改造成五组件可拆都要数周（trial03/09/10），超出"基本工作"范围；而开题卡怀疑的核心（路径模型之间的差异是否小于风场模型的差异）用第 1 层（公开路径集 × 风场子组件）就能先回答一部分。第 2 层平台选型与估工写进周报交 L29.6/Liang Hu 看。错了的代价：第 1 层只能把"生成+路径+强度"当一个整块，不能拆开，结论范围相应收窄。
- 10-18 TCRM 有限修正一轮已用完，按既定规则不再调；第 2 层平台改为**先试 STORM 原代码**（生成、移动、气压、Rmax、陆上衰减分脚本，可逐个替换；输入只要 IBTrACS 加 ERA5 月平均海平面气压与 SST，比 FAST 轻；且有已发布的 STORM 万年数据集可作复现对照），FAST 作第二候选。依据：trial03 摸底与 STORM 卡 KHFQRECZ PDF p.4–5。错了的代价：若 STORM 代码也难以拆组件，再转 FAST，多花约 1 周。
- 10-18 WRF 线答复：集群上没有 ERA5，也没有 CDS 通道（CDS 账号属 Liang Hu 的凭据）；可走 NCAR GDEX 镜像，北大西洋 0.25° 1980–2018 约 35–40 GB，1° 再小约 16 倍，下载可由 WRF bot 在 TACC 做。已请对方先核 GDEX 字段与登录要求、不下载；是否下载等 10-20 晚 TCRM 修正结果再定。
- 10-17 新意边界措辞："已核文献中尚未找到五组件同框、同口径的设计风速方差分解"，不写"无人做过"。依据：审查 （3/3 有保留支持）。

## 试过与结果
| 日期 | 做了什么 | 结果一句 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-17 | 五组件谱系表 v0（基于知识库已有卡，缺卡条目标「待建卡」） | 风场组件分支最多；定量依据待补 |
| 10-17 | 先例核对：Vickery 2009/2010 原文 | 70% 是参数不确定性；换 B 统计模型单点风速降约 9%；"无逐组件换模型分解先例"待建卡后送审 |
| 10-17 | 数据与代码可得性摸底（gemini） | 选定 CLIMADA 主干＋TCRM/pyTCR 组件；STORM/IRIS/RAFT 公开可下；CHAZ 原始路径需申请、MIT 专有；第一站点迈阿密 |
| 10-17 | 先例全貌（33 张卡） | 参数逐项分解、单子组件换模型、整链互比都有先例；"同站点逐组件换模型的设计风速方差分解"未找到——待 审 |
| 10-17 | 审查 （3/3 有效）裁决 | 新意边界有保留地成立（措辞收窄，不写"无人做过"）；"初步迹象"删除；补 8 个先例；设计改 v1（两层，第 2 层是五组件归因前提；风场接口表；三类不确定性；"不可分辨"措辞；按事件标定） |
| 10-18 | trial14 ER11 修正后重算（探索性） | 只修角动量换算：ER11 降约 2–4%；再加静态核 ×0.9（探索性）：与 H1980 的差缩到 −0.1～+2.5 m/s，与 H10 的差 −2.2～+0.1 m/s——**ER11 的"离群"主要来自 CLIMADA 实现口径，不是模型本身**。统一后描述性份额：三套路径集 V100 路径集 85–91%、风场 7–9%（压差/原生口径），V700 路径集 83–96%；仅 STORM+IRIS 的 V700 路径集 63–68%、风场 21–34%。风场之间（Holland 族加修正 ER11）的差只有约 ±2 m/s（≈5%），路径集之间约 6–8 m/s（15–20%）。仍是描述性、探索性（0.9 是近似，环境气压 1010 hPa 假设，RAFT 年构造，每格一份目录） |
| 10-18 | trial13 ER11 口径核查 | CLIMADA 6.1.0 的 ER11：①没有任何梯度→地表折减（Holland 族有）；②把角动量换回风时只除以 r，没有按原文 Eq.(2) 减去 fr/2，Rmax 处多出约 f·Rmax/2≈1.3 m/s。理想静止风暴上 ER11 峰风比 H1980/H08/H10 高 2.4/2.5/1.3 m/s，**只能解释 trial12 站点极值差 5–8 m/s 的一小部分**。ER11 原文的 Vmax 是边界层顶梯度风（原文 PDF 第 2、11 页）。**当前 ER11 格不是与 Holland 族同口径的地表风，trial11/12 中 ER11 的数字暂不作风场比较依据** |
| 10-18 | trial12 统一强度输入后的预试验二 | 风场的效应量仍达 6–8 m/s（14–20%），大于 2 倍模拟噪声（1.4–4.9 m/s）；路径集同量级（V700 压差口径下 STORM 与 IRIS 只差 4%）。描述性份额随风场集合和周期翻转：含 ER11 时 V100 风场占 33–51%，去掉 ER11 只剩 8–17%；V700 压差口径风场占 56–88%。ER11 比 Holland 族高 5–8 m/s 且与强度输入口径无关。H08 无法交叉；RAFT 年率查不到 |
| 10-18 | trial11 第 1 层预试验（迈阿密，3 路径集 × 4 风场 + H1980 内 3 种 B） | ln V 的描述性平方和份额（V50/V100/V700）：路径集 57/49/54%，风场 41/46/43%，交互 2/5/3%。**风场份额主要来自 ER11**（V100 在 STORM 上 52.7 m/s，其余三种 41.4–43.1）——ER11 用原生 Vmax、H08/H10 用压差，强度输入没统一，需拆开；换 B 模型影响 1–2%。RAFT 无合成年，按 HURDAT2 年率构造了 2873 年（假设）；环境气压统一 1010 hPa（假设）；每格只有一份目录，REML 不可辨识。**只是预试验，不作判断** |
| 10-18 | trial10 STORM 原代码评估 | 组件边界清楚，但气压与登陆衰减在同一循环里耦合，随机数流没有拆开，依赖 ERA5 月平均场和已停维护的 Basemap；全链 100 年未跑通。估计改造为第 2 层要 19–41 个工作日 |
| 10-18 | trial09 TCRM 有限修正（完成） | **闸门未通过**：生成步长 1 h→6 h 后，两种子 Δp≥40 hPa 年率 0.062（观测区间 0.05–0.33，落在下缘）、Δp≥10 hPa 年率 0.29（区间 0.23–0.64，内），但全部进入率 0.52（区间 0.92–1.54，外）；V100≈27.3 m/s，仍远低于 STORM 41.3、IRIS 36.4。原定位线索：拟合用的是 6 h 历史轨迹，生成却用 1 h 步长（AR(1) 时间支持不一致）；输入里的强压差尾在生成环节才丢失。只把生成步长改为 6 h 的 100 年短测：Δp≥40 hPa 年率 0.01→0.08（已进观测区间 0.05–0.33），进入率 0.32→0.39（仍低于 0.92–1.54）。两种子各 1 万年复检在跑 |
| 10-18 | trial08 TCRM 合理性闸门（完成） | **未通过**：两个种子都在迈阿密 250 km 内进入率约 0.33/年（观测 1.23，90% 区间 0.92–1.54），Δp≥40 hPa 的事件年率 0.0095（观测 0.18，区间 0.05–0.33），强风暴约少一个数量级；环境气压偏低（+5 hPa 只把 V100 从 21.6 提到 24.3）；预筛和 Vmax 代理已排除。另：STORM、IRIS 也各有指标落在观测区间外（进入率 0.50/0.25；IRIS 压差尾偏强），合成集之间本身差异很大 |
| 10-17 | trial08 TCRM 合理性闸门（进行中，初步） | 100 年初看：250 km 内 TCRM 进入率 0.32/年（观测 EBTRK 1.23/年，90% 区间 0.92–1.54）；压差中位/P90/P99 = 7.8/27.4/40.7 hPa，观测已知子集为 10.0/64.2/77.0 hPa——TCRM 风暴明显偏弱、偏少，是 V100 偏低的主要线索；H08 不读代理 Vmax；TCRM 与 Natural Earth 陆地掩膜在 66/548 个近岸节点不一致。1 万年双种子在跑，等完整结论 |
| 10-17 | trial07 第 2 层工程 | 两个种子各 1 万年整链跑通（每种子约 2.3 h、峰值内存约 2 GB，Colab 已停）。**但迈阿密 V100 只有约 21.5 m/s，远低于 STORM（约 41）和 IRIS（约 36），只有 35% 的年份有台风进入 400 km**——TCRM 合成气候是否合理未经检验，在通过合理性闸门前不能用作第 2 层底座。此外： | |
| 10-17 | trial06 检查点一最后一轮诊断（之后不再追） | 极端事件上两式 B 只差 8%（迈阿密）/14%（Wilmington），原文平均差约 18%；风眼壁到站点峰值再缩小 1–2 个百分点；登陆后 B 衰减影响 <0.35 个百分点。**检查点一记为"方向复现、量级未复现"**；最主要的线索是差距在上游——STORM 极端风暴的 Δp、Rmax 分布使两式 B 差变小，即换风场子组件的效应依赖路径/强度集（A×W 交互），主因仍未定 |
| 10-17 | trial05 检查点一单因子诊断 | 换配套 Rmax 模型使 V700 降幅多 1.1–1.4 个百分点，B 截断几乎无影响，都不能补足差距；迈阿密极端事件两式 B 差（−0.15）小于 Wilmington（−0.24），是两站差异的线索。主因未定，检查点仍未通过 |
| 10-17 | trial04 检查点一：Vickery 2010 Fig.4 换 B 统计模型 | **只复现了方向**：V100 Wilmington −4.9%（原文 −9.4%）、迈阿密 −1.4%（原文 −6.8%）；V700 −5.1%/−2.3%（原文 −10.9%/−9.3%）。量级未复现，检查点未通过；原文数字 Lead 已核（PDF 第 6 页） |
| 10-17 | trial03 第 2 层平台选型 | 暂选 TCRM（G/T/I/D）+ CLIMADA 风场：唯一在公开输入、Colab 上跑通 100 年并能显式换种子的平台（生成 10,000 年外推约 2.4 h）；FAST 卡在 ERA5 输入和时钟种子，CHAZ 卡在 Python2 与缺输入；五组件独立开关、两个复现检查点均未通过。IRIS 环境气压 1005/1010/1015 hPa 使 V100 变 34.5/36.4/38.0 m/s，且大量路径中心气压不低于假设环境气压，须改用物理环境场 |
| 10-17 | Colab 小试 trial02：STORM 去二次衰减、IB 两种衰减、400 km 预筛、IRIS 接入 | 400 km 事件预筛逐年无变化、提速 2.19 倍；STORM 二次衰减已证实去掉；IRIS 接通（环境气压 1010 hPa 为假设）；第 1 层 32 组估计 2–4 个 Colab 会话 0.5–1 h（不含 W3/W4/L2 新实现）。仍只作接口评估 |
| 10-17 | Colab 小试 trial01：迈阿密，STORM/IBTrACS 扰动 × H1980/H08 | 流程跑通；单组风场 104–478 s，192 组串行约 15 h；STORM 衰减不可拔插、扰动伪年不独立、开阔地未定标——只证明可运行，不作判断 |
| 10-17 | 逐组件替换方差分解试验设计 v0（96 组全因子＋两个参照方差） | 设计草稿，未计算 |

## 参数来源表

# L29.6b Typhoon Track and Intensity Models (for Wind Engineering)

## Objective
Decompose typhoon hazard models into five components (genesis / track / intensity / landfall decay / wind field), perform variance decomposition via component-by-component replacement, and determine which stage contributes most to the uncertainty in design wind speeds.

## Current Status
In progress (basic work approved by Liang Hu on 10-16; Week 1 from 10-17 to 10-23, task brief). Restricted to literature, data reconnaissance, and experimental design, with no supercomputer runs.
- 10-17: Taxonomy table v0 and variance-decomposition experimental design v0 written (see table below).
- Running: litwiki card supplementation received (10-17, 33 cards, index; automated pre-check misjudged it as failed because the reply contained only a link, whereas the index content is complete and Lead spot-check of Vickery 2009 Table 2 confirmed accuracy, accepted); gemini-worker data and code reconnaissance received (10-17, automated pre-check misjudged it as failed due to reply truncation, whereas file content is complete and Lead spot-check of CLIMADA and TCRM confirmed accuracy, accepted); better Colab pilot trial returned (10-17, workflow connected, lessons recorded in Design Section 3b); Grok quick search returned (10-17, unverified leads whose judgment direction runs opposite to the kickoff card's suspicion, recorded in Design Sections 1a and 4a); Deep Research Step 2 returned (10-17); Lead verified Vickery 2009/2010 against original texts, see .
- litwiki received (10-17): 6 new cards, 3 cards revised; full texts for Huang 2021 and Wei 2023 remain unobtainable.
- trial02 received (10-17).
- Awaiting: L29.6 unified benchmark specification template (design v1 will be finalized per template upon arrival).
- **10-19 Liang Hu pointed out that the literature search on track/intensity models was severely incomplete**. Lead acknowledged: previously relied only on knowledge-base keywords and Deep Research leads without systematically inventorying Liang Hu's Zotero library. Zotero database inventoried: 196 core candidates, approx. 170 without cards (list); litwiki building cards in batches (track/genesis -> intensity -> decay -> full chain and design wind speed). All "pending card" entries and representative models in taxonomy table v0 will be redone as v1 based on the new cards, supplementing the precedent check; until then, the taxonomy table must not be treated as a complete review.
- 10-19 Georgiou 1985 dissertation is in Zotero (316-page OCR full text), so the earlier "abstract only" statement was incorrect; litwiki is redoing the card.
- 10-19 Web search: Grok quick search x 3 (limited value, treated as leads only); Deep Research Max Batch 1 (synthetic track/intensity/decay) returned with a new lead list (Nakajo STCM, WHITS, TCWiSE, TC-Diffusion, HurriCast, FPHLM, Bhowmik, Hu 2026, etc., all unverified), currently being verified and carded by litwiki; recent-year (2022-2026) Deep Research Max sent and awaiting return, while Grok quick search returned (leads merged into the list, including several entries with questionable identifiers); Batch 2 (full spectrum of track and intensity models, including forecasting/AI models) returned on 10-19 and merged into the same list (forecasting/theoretical category, valuable for model-family landscape and failure modes rather than design-wind-speed precedents). Georgiou card redone (taxonomy table addendum).
- 10-19 litwiki supplemental ticket (forecasting / theoretical / AI weather models) returned: added 21 cards (8 page-numbered, 13 bibliographic brief cards), correcting the Anthes 1982 DOI and FuXi year; the 15-44% in TC-Next refers to track error relative to TempestExtremes, not design wind speed. Remaining batches (Zotero card supplementation, synthetic track/intensity/decay lead verification) are still in progress.
- 10-19 Recent-year (2022-2026) supplemental search: Deep Research Max journal-by-journal scan returned with insufficient breadth (only a few new synthetic-hazard entries); switched to Crossref automated screening, pulling 1803 recent papers with typhoon/hurricane in the title, selecting 157, and sending 41 priority papers to litwiki for card creation. Descriptive variance shares after unification: across all three track catalogs, V100 is 85-91% track set and 7-9% wind field (pressure-deficit / native convention), and V700 is 83-96% track set; across STORM + IRIS only, V700 is 63-68% track set and 21-34% wind field. (2), adding approx. approx. 1.3 m/s at Rmax. On an idealized stationary storm, ER11 peak wind exceeds H1980/H08/H10 by 2.4/2.5/1.3 m/s, **explaining only a small fraction of the 5-8 m/s site extreme difference in trial12**. `Vmax` in the original ER11 paper is the gradient wind at the top of the boundary layer (original PDF pp. 2, 11). **The current ER11 cells are not surface winds under the same convention as the Holland family, so ER11 numbers in trial11/12 are not used as a basis for wind-field comparison for now** |

In a 100-year short test changing only the generation step to 6 h: Δp >= 40 hPa annual rate rose from 0.01 to 0.08 (entering the observed 0.05-0.33 interval), while entry rate rose from 0.32 to 0.39 (still below 0.92-1.54). Two-seed 10,000-year re-verification running |

Additionally, STORM and IRIS each have metrics falling outside observed intervals (entry rates 0.50/0.25; IRIS pressure-deficit tail biased high), showing substantial divergence among synthetic catalogs themselves |

Dual-seed 10,000-year runs in progress, awaiting full conclusions |

Remains for interface evaluation only |

# L29.6c 结构优化算法

## 目标
在公开标准基准、相同函数评估预算下比较代表性优化算法，判定'新元启发式算法'是否实质优于成熟方法；与 T4 共用风控高层算例。

## 子项目（Liang Hu 10-22「内容很多，后续应该再分几个子项目」）
| 编号 | 名称 | 状态 | 第一个里程碑（A197 回执，10-22） |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L29.6c1 | 箱梁颤振外形优化 | 在做（A197，Liang Hu 10-22 批） | **M1 文献结论草案已交（10-22）** ：已读全文 7 项均先建代理再优化，无同真实 CFD 次数的跨算法比较；单次 2D URANS 静力系数 32 核 4.5 h（Tinmitondé 2022 PDF p.7，Lead 已核）；验证断面改 Great Belt（Poulsen 1992）。下一步 10-28 基准设计＋B9，10-31 方法清单（须含 DRL、空间映射、NGO），11-04 计算方案；设计库预计超 200 SU，届时三审报批 |
| L29.6c2 | 高层截面外形优化 | 在做（A197，Liang Hu 10-22 批） | 评估手段表 v0，10-28；10-22 评估手段表 v0 已写入 Li 2021 同预算比较（已见一项，先验不对等） |
| L29.6c3 | TMD 参数与布置优化 | 在做（A197，Liang Hu 10-22 批） | **M1 已完成（10-22 上报）**：Yang 76 层 23 自由度定义冻结，未控与屋顶 TMD 示例均复算对上（峰值差 ≤0.105%、RMS ≤0.434%）；基准设计 v0.1，B9 存档；Welch 频域评估器未过 5% 判据已弃，改同定义粗步长时域（ 验收中）；下一步 P1 比较（Colab CPU，预计 <10 CU） |

L29.6c 本层保留：问题—方法矩阵与跨子项目汇总。

## L29.4a/b/c 并入计划（10-29， 已于 10-29 转入，编为 L29.6c6/c7/c8；已向三个子对话交代）
依据：Liang Hu 10-29「L29 线的研究（除 L29.7）通常目的不在于寻找新的算法，而是在于通过设定基准，比较现有的算法，识别其对工程实际的应用存在的缺陷，加以改进。现在看来，L29.4 应该取消，子项目合并到 L29.6c 中。」决策。移入前不动 L29.4 的页面、目录和状态；移入后各子项目已批方案、闸门、状态照旧，只改问题句的定位。

| 新编号 | 原编号与名称 | 并入后的定位（基准比较现有方法 → 找工程缺陷 → 改进） | 与 c1–c5 的接口 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L29.6c6 | L29.4a 风工程优化真实应用普查（M1、M2 已交，三审；建议结题（待 Liang Hu）不变） | 应用台账作为 L29.6c 各基准的"工程真实问题清单"：哪些优化问题在工程里真有人用、用的是哪类方法，决定 c1–c4 基准是否覆盖真实用法；不再单独出新结论 | 给 c1–c4 选问题与方法名单；给 c5 提供"工程上实际用的方法"先验 |
| L29.6c7 | L29.4b 优化走进工程的障碍与对策 | 把每条原因（结果不可解释、对输入/超参敏感、离散可建造性、计算代价、约束不完备等）改写成可在基准上量的"工程缺陷假设"，在 c1–c4 的同预算结果上逐条检验，能检验的给出改进办法 | 缺陷假设清单交 c1–c4 在基准设计里预注册；c3 已有证据（NM 停在 TMDI 边界假最优、GA 对超参敏感）可直接对应 |
| L29.6c8 | L29.4c 可靠度约束下可被接受的优化 | 在与 c4 共用的风控高层算例上，同预算比较现有做法（规范系数约束、RBDO、事后 β 配平等），找其工程缺陷（系统 β 失真、验算集不完备、离散可建造性），再改进；L29.4 NIST 60 层"事后配平"流程作为其中一个被比较做法 | 与 c4 共用算例和预算口径；c5 的选法规则覆盖可靠度约束问题 |

下一步： 移完后，在三个子项目对话里各发一条交代（问题句按上表改写、闸门不变），并在本页「子项目」表补三行；c6 维持「建议结题（待 Liang Hu）」。

## 当前状态
- **10-23 22:4x c3 P1 约束两档初判**（c3 Lead 程序复算；限本基准/本配置/默认超参，未）：行程 RMS 限 80%/60% 下四种闭式解全不可行；NM 200 次中位距 J* ≤0.004%，中位约 35 次达 J*×1.005；二进制 GA 6000 次中位 +0.05–0.11%、达标需 430–840 次；SLSQP 需归一。tight 档 NM 2/10 种子卡 +34.7%（新假说：紧约束下局部法稳健性）。0.001 s 复核显示贴边解超限 0.019%（评估器偏差），-09 按限值/1.0002 重跑定最终表。累计约 6.4 CU。“GA 多余”对外表述前须 
- **10-23 23:5x c3 P1 约束档定稿**（同文件 §5；证据，c3 Lead 按 hitting.csv 复算）：-09 按 s_max/1.0002 重跑后 16/16 代表解在 0.001 s、原限值下可行；新 J*′ 与原 J* 差 +0.007%（medium）/+0.010%（tight），初判数字不改。NM、归一 SLSQP 中位 25–35 次达 J*′×1.005；NM 多重启（总 200 次）把 tight 档单种子 +34.7% 尾部降到 +0.091%（事后检验，只作新假说的一次检验）。限本基准/本配置/默认超参。下一步 -10 等预算调参轮（≤2 CU）→ P2 TMDI。
- **10-24 07:3x c3 调参轮完成**（7 方法 × 10 组超参 × 3 种子，medium 档、1000 次预算，中位相对 J*；调参阶段数，非正式比较）：CMA-ES、NM 多重启、归一 SLSQP 默认即 ≈0；PSO、L-SHADE 调后到 0；实数 GA 最好 +0.118%、二进制 GA +0.123%，且对超参更敏感（0.1–3.1%）。实数 GA 第 0 组变异率 0.1≠原默认 0.025，原默认取前轮数据。已派 -10c 正式比较（两档 × 10 种子，选组按原规则与事后补的平局规则两种并列，正式用平局规则；CU 外推 >4.5 即停）。
- **10-24 c3 P1 调参轮初判**（c3 Lead 复算；本配置、未审）：7 方法各约 3 万次调参预算后，两种 GA 用满 6000 次中位仍 +0.004–0.16%；未调参 NM / 归一 SLSQP 200 次 +0.000%、25–37 次达标；同 200 次预算 GA 调后仍差 1–3%；调参对 GA 效果不稳定；L-SHADE 调参获益最大（约 150 次达标）。对 6c 第(3)问的含义（限本 2 维带约束问题）：按问题特征预选局部法比调优进化算法更省。待 -10d 0.001 s 复核 → P2 TMDI。保活工具两次故障（盯错进程名、8 h 上限退出不拉回）已请 c3 报平台。
- **10-24 20:3x c3 P1 六审裁决**（6 份有效均「有保留支持」；裁决，结论稿）：限屋顶单 TMD 只调 f、ζ、本基准——多重启 NM 或归一 SLSQP ≤200 次达已知最优；GA（默认版及仅在两档约束上调参版）用到 6000 次不优于它们。收窄：R=10 登记为对事先 R=30 的偏离；B9 第 2 条分项判定（SLSQP 按事先设定不成立）；百分数标明粗步长、相对已知最优；调参在 1000 次上做、迁移到 200/6000 次须注明；闭式解按模态质量比 +2.04%/+4.14%。**不得对外说「小维 TMD 调参 GA 多余」**（P2/P3 未做）。在做：-12 风荷载分段参照与最终表；-11c 查 P2 中固定 μ 时 TMDI 劣于 TMD（与 Giaralis 2017 相反）。

projects.digest:
# Structural Optimization Algorithms (Active)

This project evaluates whether novel metaheuristic optimization algorithms provide measurable performance gains over established mathematical and heuristic methods under equal function evaluation budgets on wind-engineering benchmarks. To address distinct engineering challenges, the project partitioned its work into five sub-projects covering bridge flutter aerodynamics, tall building cross-sections, tuned mass damper (TMD) damping systems, structural sizing, and algorithmic selection rules. On a benchmark tall building, the best method differed by problem: local methods (multi-restart Nelder-Mead, normalized SLSQP) for single-TMD tuning, normalized SLSQP for the TMDI case (where multi-restart Nelder-Mead stayed in a false optimum), and CMA-ES for multi-TMD placement, whereas binary genetic algorithms lagged across all tested single and multi-TMD setups even with extended evaluations. These algorithmic findings remain strictly empirical, diagnostic, and limited to the single benchmark building configuration without broader validation. At present, TMD parameter and placement investigations have concluded their preliminary benchmark testing, while aerodynamic shape optimization and member sizing sub-projects remain in preliminary literature and experimental design phases.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-23**: The PI ordered literature retrieval re-dispatches for blocked papers; a worker agent retrieved two of three Elsevier articles, while the other seven dispatched papers were not obtained.
- **2026-10-23**: In sub-project L29.6c3, single-TMD parameter optimization under 80% and 60% stroke RMS limits showed that four closed-form solutions were infeasible, while Nelder-Mead reached within 0.004% of the optimum in 200 evaluations compared to binary GA requiring 430 to 840 evaluations.
- **2026-10-24**: Retrieval retries for five non-Elsevier papers yielded zero full texts due to access restrictions and download failures; the seven missing papers were listed for interlibrary loan or manual download, and current conclusions do not depend on them.
- **2026-10-24**: Equal-budget hyperparameter tuning (approximately 30,000 evaluations per method) in L29.6c3 showed that tuned binary GA still lagged behind the optimum by 0.004% to 0.16% at 6000 evaluations, whereas un-tuned Nelder-Mead and normalized SLSQP reached the target within 25 to 37 evaluations.
- **2026-10-24**: Six independent reviewer models issued a "support with reservations" ruling on single-TMD parameter optimization, restricting claims to the benchmark building and single roof TMD without generalizing to higher dimensions.
- **2026-10-25**: Sub-project L29.6c3 evaluated tuned mass damper inerters (TMDI), identifying a true optimum without an inerter (beta=0) and a boundary false optimum 18% worse; normalized SLSQP found the true optimum in 10 out of 10 runs within 500 evaluations, while multi-restart Nelder-Mead remained trapped in the false optimum and binary GA lagged by 8.3% at 6000 evaluations.
- **2026-10-25**: Exhaustive baseline searches for two TMDs showed that placing both devices on the roof was optimal, and the computing cost rate was corrected to 0.16 CU/h, leading to a scaled-down evaluation protocol for four TMDs.
- **2026-10-26**: In multi-TMD placement trials at 2000 evaluations, CMA-ES achieved the lowest objective values across all tested cases, while binary GA lagged by 3.29% to 18.39%; a summary review by five responding reviewer models accepted the conclusions as problem-specific observations rather than universal selection rules.

## What the PI decided
- **2026-10-23**: Liang Hu instructed the team to re-dispatch literature retrieval for previously blocked papers using restored desktop and workstation channels under a ceiling of 100 papers per publisher per machine daily, halting immediately upon encountering verification captchas without retrying.
- **2026-10-24**: Liang Hu mandated that every project and sub-project surface its latest report to the very front of its conversation thread, accompanied by a precise list of pending items requiring PI decisions.

## Where it stands
Sub-projects L29.6c1, L29.6c2, L29.6c4, and L29.6c5 are completing literature syntheses, awaiting CFD unit cost quotes, and drafting benchmark problem formulations. In L29.6c3, initial numerical benchmarks and independent multi-model reviews across single TMD, TMDI, and multi-TMD configurations are finished, and the open item is the PI's decision on whether to release the narrowed conclusions externally.

# L29.6c1 Box-Girder Flutter Shape Optimization

## Objective
On 4-variable closed box-girder flutter shape optimization (Zheng 2023 type, maximizing critical flutter wind speed), using the number of true CFD evaluations as the budget, compare surrogate + infill, pre-built surrogate + gradient, multi-fidelity, direct gradient / direct search, CMA-ES / L-SHADE, etc., to answer "which class of method should be used when N <= 120 CFD evaluations, and can this be stated in advance".

## Current Status
- 10-22 Kickoff plan approved by Liang Hu, work started. Section 3 computation phase and any single job >=200 SU or exceeding 24 h will still be submitted separately for approval at that time.
- 10-22 First milestone completed: literature conclusion draft. Reported to L29.6c. 12 full texts obtained, litwiki upgraded the cards to full-text level (index), and draft supplemented.
- CFD line cost inquiry (2D URANS single-run cost, sent from L29.6c) queued, reply to be forwarded by L29.6c.

## Decisions Made
- Problem definition follows Zheng 2023, with the Cid Montoya joint problem used for reference only (kickoff plan Section 1).
- Boundary with L29.6d: flutter derivative surrogate accuracy belongs to 6d, cited read-only by this project; boundary with L29.6c5: overall framework for selecting/tuning methods belongs to c5, while this project provides expensive-end empirical tests.

## Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-22 | litwiki upgraded 12 full-text cards | 11 full-text studies still lack cross-algorithm comparisons under the same true budget; in the 2026 wind-fairing study, four metaphor-based algorithms converged to the same boundary point on the same surrogate; Group B has no term-by-term derivative numerical errors and no core-hours; G1 has relative dimensions only |
| 10-22 | literature obtained 12 full texts; Lead read A5 (Cid Montoya 2024 BBAA, PDF pp.1-3) | G1 section +-10% two shape variables; mode switching in full-bridge multi-mode flutter makes the feasible domain disconnected, causing SQP to miss the global optimum -> benchmark must include a multi-mode structural model tier |
| 10-22 | litwiki delivered 16 cards + Poulsen supplemental verification | 5 full texts, 11 abstract/bibliographic only; all 7 full-text studies lack cross-algorithm comparisons under the same budget; single static CFD run is on the order of 144 core-hours (Tinmitonde 2022 PDF p.7); Poulsen has 7 derivatives, incomplete geometry, and no mass/inertia -> validation changed to derivative level + same-parameter Uf (decision record) |
| 10-22 | litwiki delivered 7 cards (EGO, Kennedy-O'Hagan, Forrester, QST applicability scope, COBYLA preview, Great Belt/G1 bibliography) | Method cards usable; Great Belt and G1 original texts not obtained by litwiki. Lead retrieved Poulsen 1992 full text from desktop library; G1 still missing |
| 10-22 | : 609 papers, initial screening 208, Lead selected 16 papers for inclusion | All 4 keyword paths had 0 hits, snowballing only; 16 included papers pending card creation (resent on 10-22 01:51, queued) |
| 10-21 | Read matrix v1 and 13 cards, wrote kickoff plan | Existing public data are insufficient to build a 4D surrogate testbed (Zheng per-sample Uf not disclosed; Li 2022 has only 19 sections at a single wind speed) |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- Liang Hu to decide the evaluation route (recommended: (b) build in-house URANS design library + surrogate testbed + true CFD confirmation) and whether to contact the original authors (recommended: not for now).
- 10-28 Benchmark design and B9 prior prediction archiving; 10-31 method list; 11-04 computation plan (awaiting CFD cost inquiry).
- Benchmark design must specify the structural model: 2-DOF section vs. full-bridge multi-mode (A5: multi-mode flutter exhibits disconnected feasible domains due to mode switching, causing SQP to stall at a local optimum).

# L29.6c3 TMD Parameter and Placement Optimization (Active)

This sub-project of L29.6c (structural optimization algorithms, under L29 "Make the World a Better Place") asks whether genetic algorithms (GA), which are common in the literature for tuning and placing wind-induced vibration dampers, are needed when every method gets the same evaluation budget, or whether closed-form tuning, simplex, gradient or other evolutionary methods are enough. The Lead agent built a benchmark on the Yang 2004 76-storey wind-excited building. Worker agents reproduced its archived uncontrolled and roof-TMD responses (23-DOF reduced model) with peak errors of about 0.1%. Three problems were compared with 10 seeds each: P1, a single roof TMD (2 parameters, with and without stroke limits); P2, a TMDI; and P3, placement of 2 or 4 TMDs. P4 (life-cycle cost) was deferred. Within this one building, one 900 s crosswind record and these configurations, the GA as implemented here was never the best method in any case. The best-performing method differed by problem: local methods for P1, normalized SLSQP for P2, and CMA-ES for multi-TMD placement; this is an observation, not a selection rule. The CMA-ES advantage with 4 TMDs under the tight stroke limit is recorded as a new hypothesis that has not been checked on other buildings. Nothing has been released externally.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-22**: Start-up plan approved. The benchmark moved from the Liu 2020 tower (not recomputable from public data) to the Yang 2004 building.
- **2026-10-22**: A frequency-domain fast evaluator failed its pre-set accuracy criterion and was dropped. A coarse-step time-domain evaluator (0.0333 s) passed, with a maximum RMS difference of 0.114%.
- **2026-10-22 to 10-23**: Unconstrained P1 results: Nelder–Mead reached within 0.5% of the best value in a median of 29 evaluations, versus about 250 for binary GA. Closed-form tuning missed the best value by 2.04% (Warburton) and 4.14% (Den Hartog) when the modal mass ratio was used. Under the stroke limits, binary GA needed 430–840 evaluations.
- **2026-10-24**: An equal-budget tuning round did not change the P1 picture. Six independent reviewer models all gave "supported with reservations". Five of them opposed the broad claim that "GA is redundant for small-dimensional TMD tuning". The claim was narrowed and R=10 (planned R=30) was logged as a deviation. Splitting the wind record into three segments gave best values differing by 24–35%.
- **2026-10-24 to 10-25**: P2 checks found no modeling error. On this building, an inerter spanning 1–3 floors made performance worse. A false optimum at the upper inerter bound was 18% worse, and binary GA remained 8.3% off at 6000 evaluations.
- **2026-10-25 to 10-26**: In P3, the best layouts placed all or nearly all TMDs at the roof. With 4 TMDs and the tight limit, CMA-ES was 0.065% off at 2000 evaluations, against 18.4% for binary GA.
- **2026-10-26**: Five reviewer models gave "supported with reservations" on the combined summary. The Lead agent withdrew two significance claims, corrected two numbers and logged three further deviations.

## What the PI decided
- On 10-21 Liang Hu asked for optimization problems relevant to tall buildings and bridges to be chosen through a broad literature survey, for more method trials, and asked whether optimization methods can themselves be selected or tuned. On 10-22 he asked for the work to be split into sub-projects.
- Approved the start-up plan on 10-22.
- On 10-24 asked every project to put its latest report up front for his review.

## Where it stands
No computation is running. The revised summary has been reported to L29.6c. The PI still has to decide whether its narrowed external statement may be released. P4 remains deferred until L29.6c decides whether to do it.

# L29.6c5 Choosing and Tuning Optimization Methods (Active)

This sub-project responds to the PI's question of whether a suitable structural optimization method can be chosen, or the method itself optimized, in advance. It asks three things. Q1: can a method be picked from problem features (evaluation cost, dimension, discrete or continuous, smooth or noisy, gradient availability)? Q2: is hyperparameter tuning or automatic algorithm configuration worth it once its cost is counted? Q3: do rules learned on cheap problems (truss, TMD, member sizing) transfer to expensive aerodynamic shape problems? The criteria were fixed before any runs. A selection rule must close more of the gap between the single best method and the per-problem best method than twice the scatter, and tuning cost is charged against the same budget. The PI approved the start-up plan on 2026-10-22. So far only literature work has been done, with no computation. The literature draft found that algorithm selection by problem features has already been done in structural optimization, in a 2013 doctoral thesis on parametric steel bridges. No wind-engineering precedent was found in this search, so the novelty claim for Q1 was narrowed.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: The Lead agent wrote the start-up plan. It noted that the existing truss comparison of 12 methods has only 4 untuned problems, so a bank of about 20 to 30 problems drawn from sibling sub-projects is needed. It used an engineering tolerance of 1% (an assumption, also reported at 0.5% and 2%) and estimated later compute roughly.
- **2026-10-22**: The PI approved the plan. A quick literature search and 8 classic literature cards (selection, landscape analysis, tuning tools, benchmarking, efficient global optimization) were dispatched.
- **2026-10-22**: The cards showed that tuning budgets are counted in algorithm runs, not structural analyses, so feature probing, tuning and final optimization must be accounted for separately.
- **2026-10-22**: The 2013 thesis was checked against the original. It covered 474 bridge problems and 8 optimizers, and a random forest picked the best optimizer 74.7% of the time, against 40.0% and 36.0% for always using one fixed method. It did not compare methods under the same budget and did not hold out whole problem classes. The Lead agent decided Q1 continues, narrowed to six points that the thesis did not cover, including equal-budget comparison and counting selector and tuning costs.
- **2026-10-22**: A 2021 survey card confirmed that truss "new algorithm is better" tables often use unequal analysis budgets. Its best 10-bar truss solution, 5060.854 lb, matches this line's own earlier trial. One classic paper remained unobtainable.
- **2026-10-24**: Status: the literature draft and citation snowballing were done (pool of 1505 papers, 12 included). The draft has not yet been reviewed.

## What the PI decided
- Asked whether the optimization method itself can be selected or optimized (point 3 of the 10-21 critique), and said the work should be split into several sub-projects.
- Approved the start-up plan on 10-22.
- Asked every project to bring its latest report to the front for item-by-item reading (10-24).

## Where it stands
The next steps are an archived first-version selection rule by 10-28, the problem bank design by 10-31 (which needs callable models from c3 and c4), and the experimental design for a three-reviewer review on 11-04. Any later compute will be submitted separately for approval.

projects.digest:
# L29.4b Why Engineering Practice Uses Structural Optimization Rarely or Not at All (Active)

This sub-project asks why real engineering projects rarely use structural optimization, and how far each reason is justified versus habit. It covers different structure types (buildings, bridges, other structures, dampers and similar components) and optimization types (sizing, shape or aerodynamic form, topology, parameters), and for each reason it sketches a mathematical or reliability model. The Lead agent took the PI's five reasons (safety reserve optimized away, model error and load uncertainty, constructability, the code checking system, liability) and added six of its own, then built a literature base through quick searches, citation snowballing and full-text cards. Milestone M1, a reason framework with mechanism, literature (card and page) and in-house evidence for each of 11 reasons, was delivered on 2026-10-22. The in-house evidence comes from a single case, the lab's NIST 60-storey RC member-sizing optimization, and is described as inference. In that case, three reasons look stronger than "safety reserve optimized away": an incomplete check set, the optimizer's "winner's curse", and the lack of any basis for conventional design margins. No ratings of "how justified" versus "how much inertia" have been assigned yet; that is planned for M3.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: Sub-project opened from L29.4; the Lead agent submitted a start-up plan (0 SU in the next two weeks; small demonstrations of no more than 30 SU possibly in late November, to be requested separately).
- **2026-10-21**: Grok quick search checked: 11 of 13 DOIs found; two leads discarded. Deep Research step two judged poor; no conclusions adopted, 5 leads kept. Neither search found structural-engineering literature on optimizers exploiting unchecked failure modes ("not found in two searches", not "does not exist").
- **2026-10-21**: Lead agent checked Beck 2020 (redundancy must be kept when latent failure probability exceeds the target; proven only for a two-bar system) and Smith & Winkler 2006 (choosing the best of three unbiased estimates disappoints by 0.85 standard deviations on average).
- **2026-10-21**: Snowballing gave 2,559 candidates, 508 after screening, 38 judged highly relevant; 24 priority papers retrieved (22 full texts) and carded. A spot check confirmed a Queensferry Crossing study: adding a cable-loss constraint raised the optimal half-bridge cable count from 22 to 36 for 13.11% more cable steel (model comparison, not as-built).
- **2026-10-22**: Start-up plan approved; M1 reason framework v1 delivered. Single-case evidence: missing column-tension check gave a utilization of 3.98 for the optimized design versus 1.08 for the conventional design; all top 5 coarse-grid candidates exceeded the acceleration limit on the fine grid (coarse grid underestimated acceleration by 2–6%); two conventional practices differed by 8.0–11.4% in cost; optimized-versus-conventional reliability index differences were no more than 0.26.
- **2026-10-22**: Eser 2025 read: optimized designs of 5 built steel structures were 3.59%–40.52% lighter (mean 19.94%) than design-office solutions, with no reliability calculation and 2 office designs not satisfying constraints.
- **2026-10-24**: At the PI's request, an addendum was appended to the latest report summarizing progress.

## What the PI decided

# L29.4c Engineering-Acceptable Optimization Under a Given Reliability Constraint (Active)

This sub-project asks whether, and how, structural optimization can be built so that it meets a given reliability constraint and can be accepted in engineering practice: the form of the constraint (member or system level), where the target reliability comes from, how uncertainty enters, how to make the check set complete, discreteness and constructability, explainability and sign-off, and computational cost. By the PI's ordering it must wait for the L29.4a survey and the L29.4b reason analysis, so work so far is literature review and a framework skeleton, with no conclusions. A first literature synthesis (six judgments) went to three independent reviewer models; two found important omitted counter-evidence, and the Lead agent withdrew or narrowed several claims in version 2. The revised reading is that US and Chinese codes do provide an entry for reliability-based design, but acceptance stacks reliability justification, conventional factor floors, explanation of differences and independent review; it does not replace the code with one system reliability index. No specific acceptance clause for optimization results was found. No computation has been run (0 SU).

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: Sub-project opened from L29.4; start-up plan submitted (0 SU for two weeks; framework draft v0 due 11-04; a possible demonstration of about 50–100 SU to be requested separately later).
- **2026-10-21**: Grok quick search treated as leads only (abstract level). The Deep Research report was judged unreliable and not used, apart from two code leads.
- **2026-10-21**: The Lead agent checked original texts: the ASCE performance-based wind design prestandard requires reliability consistent with code targets plus independent peer review including reliability expertise; GB 50068-2018 §E.4.2 requires the reasons for clear differences from the "traditional method" to be analyzed and the result shown reasonable before use. ISO 2394:2015 body text was not obtained.
- **2026-10-21**: Literature synthesis v1 reviewed by three reviewer models: one "partly supports", one "supports with reservations", one "supports" with no must-fix items. The Lead agent verified the cited omissions and issued v2: added the prestandard's authority-approval limits, LRFD checks for elastic members and the 80% base overturning floor, the GB 50068 commentary caution, and an industry author's view that direct reliability analysis in building design is "highly impractical"; withdrew the claim that calibrating to the conventional design's reliability is "consistent with code calibration logic".
- **2026-10-22**: Start-up plan approved; framework v0 skeleton written with options and literature for seven design decisions, recommendations and the feasibility table left empty.
- **2026-10-22**: A citation snowball search was blocked by an exhausted shared OpenAlex quota; rerun scheduled.
- **2026-10-22**: Dixon et al. 2026 checked (single-span concrete footbridge, one case): member-by-member Eurocode optimization left every member compliant but dropped a damage-limit-state system reliability index from 3.2 to 0.6 ("system failure"); system-level optimization kept 2.7. Beck 2020 (two-bar parallel example): whether redundancy is kept depends on the chosen target reliability. A v3 addendum was written, not yet reviewed.

## What the PI decided
- Set the order: survey first (L29.4a), then reasons (L29.4b), then solutions (this sub-project).
- Computations marked "to be requested separately", and any job of about 200 SU or more or longer than 24 hours, need separate approval.
- On 10-24 asked every project to bring its latest report to the front for line-by-line review.

## Where it stands
As of 10-24 framework v0 is still a skeleton awaiting L29.4a and L29.4b; its full text is due 11-04. "Explainable and signable" remains a literature gap, and two references are still being retrieved. Nothing awaits the PI.

# Dynamics and CFD Surrogate Modeling (Active)

This project evaluates the performance boundaries and advantage regime of physics-informed neural operators (PINOs) against surrogate models structured across dimensionality reduction representations, regressors, physical constraints, and data fidelities under equivalent training budgets for interpolation and extrapolation. The research team conducted systematic literature surveys on aerodynamic surrogates and formulated empirical verification protocols using field monitoring datasets from three Norwegian bridges. Literature analyses indicated that although multiple surrogate algorithms have been compared on shared datasets, none of the papers checked so far aligned hyperparameter tuning budgets or tested models on unseen objects. Data screening confirmed that field measurements from all three bridges satisfy criteria for predicting bridge response from wind, though short-term wind forecasting requires tiered targets and partitioned validation sets due to non-continuous recording thresholds and storm sample clustering. At present, all findings remain exploratory and unvalidated by computational runs: the empirical test protocol has been finalized internally without external review, while a surrogate problem-method matrix is being prepared for review by three independent reviewer models.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-22**: The Lead agent verified full-scale field records for three Norwegian bridges, approving all three for wind-induced structural response modeling while restricting short-term wind forecasting targets based on available record lengths.
- **2026-10-22**: Literature screening across project branches identified multi-surrogate benchmarks on identical data, but paper audits confirmed that none aligned tuning budgets or evaluated out-of-distribution extrapolation.
- **2026-10-22**: Liang Hu ordered an immediate system-wide halt to literature downloads and snowballing due to publisher download limits, subsequently lifting the suspension with strict quota and access rules.
- **2026-10-23**: The Lead agent resumed literature retrieval and paper card creation under publisher constraints, extracting case studies on flutter, vortex-induced vibration, and hyperparameter tuning sensitivity.
- **2026-10-23**: A worker agent drafted the verification protocol for bridge wind speed and acceleration response, adopting four year-based cross-validation groups for Hardanger Bridge and copying 25.5 GB of raw data to long-term cluster storage.
- **2026-10-24**: Liang Hu instructed all sub-projects to bring forward their latest reports for sequential evaluation, after which platform guidance clarified that progress reports were only required for another project line.
- **2026-10-26**: The worker agent finalized the bridge wind and response verification protocol ahead of schedule, resolving sensor spacing and requiring at least 50 strong wind records per test group while deciding against external review prior to computation.

## What the PI decided
- On 2026-10-22, Liang Hu ordered an immediate suspension of literature downloads and snowballing across all branches after heavy downloads triggered publisher rate restrictions.
- On 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23, Liang Hu authorized the resumption of literature retrieval under strict protocols: prioritizing open-access sources, searching local repositories first, restricting downloads to 100 papers per publisher per day, and stopping immediately upon receiving captchas or 403 errors.
- On 2026-10-24, Liang Hu instructed all projects and sub-projects to present their latest progress reports at the front of each conversation for sequential review.

## Where it stands
The verification protocol for bridge-site wind speed and bridge response prediction is finalized, with the method inventory due on 2026-10-30 and initial benchmark runs planned for 2026-11-02 to measure single-training runtimes and estimate cluster compute allocations. Concurrently, the problem-method matrix for surrogate modeling is being prepared for delivery and review by three independent reviewers.

# L29.6d2 Wind-Induced Response Computation and the Role of PINO (Active)

This sub-project uses wind-induced structural response as a test problem: TPU wind loads applied to linear or hysteretic structural models, with ground truth computed by the line itself. It asks three things: whether a family of surrogate models is useful at all, where physics-informed neural operators (PINO) have an advantage, and whether hyperparameter tuning changes the ranking of methods. Ten method classes are planned, from exact modal superposition and statistical linearization to tree models, LSTM, PhyLSTM, DeepONet, FNO, SA-FNO and PINO. Each method is run with default settings and with an equal tuning budget. The decision terms and five predictions were written before any runs. Each method must first reproduce published numbers; the main target is a 2025 wind case with relative L2 errors of 0.1887 (FNO), 0.1770 (SA-FNO) and 0.3575 (DeepONet). The plan was approved on 2026-10-22. So far only literature and design work has been done, with no computation.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: The Lead agent wrote the start-up plan, with a resource ceiling of about 720 Colab compute units (about 135 A100 hours, an assumption-based upper bound) in three phases. It cut repetitions from 10 to 5 to control the budget. It raised one question for the PI: the planned "main structure yields" case conflicts with the PI's statement that tall buildings have never shown main-structure nonlinearity under wind, so it proposed a linear main structure with nonlinearity only in isolation layers or dampers.
- **2026-10-21**: Literature cards found only indirect evidence from other fields that tuning changes rankings, and no study testing ranking reversal for FNO, SA-FNO, DeepONet and PINO. No measured record of an isolation layer yielding under wind was found. The published wind dataset is about 31.55 GB preprocessed (162 GB raw), so reproduction was split into an earthquake case first, then the wind case.
- **2026-10-22**: The PI approved all pending plans in one batch. The Lead agent took the structural-tier proposal as approved with the plan and said the PI's view would prevail if different.
- **2026-10-22**: At the PI's line-wide request, the literature was snowballed again: a pool of 3490, 417 passing the keyword screen, 37 included after the Lead agent's own title screening. The Lead agent of the parent sub-project L29.6d re-ran the search in the same folder by mistake and overwrote the pool files; they were rebuilt with identical counts.
- **2026-10-22**: Full texts of 9 new cards were read. Same-data comparisons of several surrogates already exist (one tall building, one bridge), but none aligns tuning budgets. In one, LSTM beat FNO on top-floor displacement at the same sampling rate (normalized error 0.0800 vs 0.1634). A monitored isolated building showed an 8 to 10% temporary frequency drop in a typhoon, with no measured yielding, hysteresis or residual displacement. The isolation tier therefore remains an analysis scenario.
- **2026-10-23**: No blocked or deferred papers needed re-requesting. One conference chapter was left for interlibrary loan.

## What the PI decided
- Split L29.6d into three sub-projects. Problems must come from the wind literature, methods must start from those used for the problem, and PINO is judged by the same criteria with no presumed outcome.
- Approved the start-up plan in a batch approval of all current projects.
- Judged the literature scan insufficient and required all Leads with their own literature collections or recent searches to redo citation snowballing.

## Where it stands
Experimental design v1 is due 10-27, a three-reviewer review on 10-28, and a literature-level preliminary answer for L29.6d on 11-02. No computation will start before the PI has seen that answer, and each compute phase needs separate approval.

projects.goal:
Covers two problems in the problem–method matrix: P4 short-term bridge-site wind speed forecasting; and P10 predicting bridge response from measured wind (plus waves for floating bridges; candidate). Across both problems, answer "are all of these surrogate methods genuinely useful, and can they be selected or optimized?" Specifically address four questions:
- Q1: Which methods beat persistence forecasting
- Q2: How much of the advantage of decomposition-hybrid models stems from data leakage or mismatched comparison targets
- Q3: Does hyperparameter tuning alter the method ranking
- Q4: Can data-driven methods beat a quasi-steady physical scaling baseline (P10 only).

# L29.6d3 桥址风速与桥梁响应

## 目标
负责问题—方法矩阵里的两个问题：P4 桥址短期风速预测；P10 由实测风（浮桥另加浪）预测桥梁响应（候选）。在这两个问题上回答"这些代理方法真的都有用吗、能否选择或优化"。具体回答四个问题：
- Q1：哪些方法胜过持续性预报
- Q2：分解混合模型的优势有多少来自泄漏或对照目标不一致
- Q3：调参是否改变方法排序
- Q4：数据驱动方法能否胜过准定常物理缩放基线（仅 P10）。

projects.digest:
# Bridge-Site Wind Speed and Bridge Response (Active)

The project investigates whether data-driven surrogate models offer genuine predictive utility for bridge-site wind speed forecasting and structural response prediction, specifically testing whether they outperform persistence baselines and quasi-steady physical scaling while quantifying artificial gains from future-data leakage in decomposition methods. The Lead agent audited monitoring datasets from three Norwegian bridges, screened candidate literature, and finalized a benchmarking evaluation protocol. Data checks showed that the floating (pontoon) Bergsøysund Bridge records contain only 45.5 h of concurrent monitoring at wind speeds of 10 m/s or higher, which is insufficient for 10-to-60-minute ahead strong-wind forecasting and required shifting primary testing for that horizon to the Hardanger Bridge dataset, which has 612.7 h at 10 m/s or higher and 7,085 paired wind and acceleration records. Literature cards showed that earlier studies on measured wind speed had already compared full-series (leaking) and real-time decomposition, though not as a strict single-factor test, and that no reviewed study reported paired numerical errors of machine learning against a physical model on the same test set. The finalized protocol establishes year-based validation groups and sensor pairings; because Hardanger only records once wind exceeds 15 m/s, the 10-to-60-minute forecasts cover only storms already under way, not storm onset.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-22**: The Lead agent verified downloaded monitoring datasets for three bridges, noting that the Hardanger dataset contains 7,085 paired wind and acceleration records across 2013 to 2020, with 4,434 records at or above 10 m/s and 1,877 records at or above 15 m/s.
- **2026-10-22**: Finding only 45.5 h of strong-wind records for the pontoon bridge, the Lead agent designated Hardanger as the primary dataset for 10-to-60-minute forecasts, restricting scope to ongoing storms.
- **2026-10-22**: Liang Hu ruled the literature search coverage insufficient and ordered all leads to rerun snowball searches across their literature bases.
- **2026-10-22**: The Lead agent completed title screening across 685 candidate papers, selecting 68 papers to establish comparative baselines and analyze decomposition leakage.
- **2026-10-22**: Liang Hu lifted a literature download halt, ordering retrieval resumed under publisher rate limits after checking local files.
- **2026-10-23**: The Lead agent drafted the evaluation protocol, copied 25.5 GB of raw data to long-term storage, and restructured validation into four year-based groups because 69% of primary strong-wind data was concentrated in 2015 and 2016; this split was marked as a post-hoc change, with the original last-two-years test still reported alongside.
- **2026-10-23**: A full-text review of one study (a different bridge, one held-out typhoon) found that it plotted machine learning and finite element response curves together but gave no error value for the finite element model, so no paired numerical comparison was possible.
- **2026-10-26**: The Lead agent finalized the evaluation protocol ahead of schedule, setting sensor spacing for torsional response, defining cross-validation groups, and confirming that real-time decomposition is computationally feasible; it is applied only to horizons of 1 minute or longer, since persistence is judged nearly unbeatable at shorter horizons.

## What the PI decided
- Liang Hu ruled that the initial literature search was insufficient and ordered all project leads to rerun literature snowballing.
- Liang Hu lifted the literature download suspension, directing that paused retrieval resume within the day while requiring local repository checks first, prioritizing open access, and strictly following publisher rate limits without bypassing access blocks.
- Liang Hu ordered the resumption of document retrieval following workstation restoration, enforcing publisher-specific routing while excluding ASCE book chapters, SSRN preprints, and IABSE conference papers.

## Where it stands
The evaluation protocol is finalized, though sensor coordinate alignments must still be verified against documentation before torsional acceleration tables are generated. Next steps are delivering the surrogate modeling method inventory by 2026-10-30 and running initial benchmark tests on 2026-11-02 to measure training runtimes and estimate compute requirements.

# Research Trustworthiness: L29.7 Root Coordination (Active)

L29.7, part of the "Make the World a Better Place" line, began as a pilot on how design-wind-speed concepts drift from their original definitions, then was widened to test the PI's impression that wind-engineering papers published after about 2010 are much less reliable than earlier ones. A literature review (W1) found that the checked evidence neither confirms nor refutes that impression. A pre-registered test (W2) followed: Claude scorers, with author, journal and year masked, rated 343 papers from JWEIA, the ASCE Journal of Structural Engineering and Wind and Structures for two serious defects: two or more key parameters missing, or model-based conclusions without quantitative validation. The defect rate was 0.63 for 1995–2009 and 0.52 for 2010–2025; the journal- and type-adjusted difference was −9.1 percentage points (95% interval [−18.6, +0.1]), which excludes a "clear decline" of 15 points or more but cannot resolve smaller changes. The 15-point threshold was set by the Lead agent, not the PI, and limits apply: all scorers are Claude, they recognised the era of 338 of 343 papers despite masking, and a fake-year test showed them judging papers labelled as older about 10–13 points more leniently.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: Start-up plan submitted. The PI asked for a broader scope. W1 (two search reports, three-reviewer review) concluded the PI's view is neither confirmed nor refuted, and that Deep Research's claim that the decline is "mainly an illusion" also exceeds the evidence.
- **2026-10-21**: W2 design reviewed by three models and revised (larger sample, all years masked, fake-year test); one journal was dropped as a post hoc change.
- **2026-10-22**: Pilot: two scorer groups agreed on 18/20 papers but guessed the era 20/20; text-only input penalised a 1998 scan, so figures were added. All 18 concept cards drafted. Contamination test: Opus gave 0/20 wrong answers, Sonnet 2–3/20 (internal pilot, not reviewed).
- **2026-10-23**: W2 report reviewed by six models (five valid; one channel returned only an error). All five accepted "clear decline excluded"; the Lead agent completed missing sensitivity readings and withdrew a draft claim that post-2010 papers were slightly better.
- **2026-10-25**: Sub-projects L29.7a (knowledge trustworthiness), L29.7b (methods rule library) and L29.7c (rule compliance and effect testing) opened; library v0 holds 2 current rules and 3 drafts.
- **2026-10-27**: Planted-error blind-review trial (X3) pilot on 4 papers: all 3 planted errors detected, no false alarms on 8 neutral edits, but cost about 1.7 times the estimate, above the 1.5 stop line, so the full batch paused. Canon-first search reached 18/20 concept queries; missing concept words were added to two cards.
- **2026-10-28**: Suggestions from L22.8 added to a draft rule, including at least 4 independent attempts before reporting a negative result.

## What the PI decided
- 2026-10-21: the original scope was too small; the work should not rely only on his own judgment.
- 2026-10-22: stop all bulk literature downloading and snowball searches; lifted the same day under per-publisher limits.
- 2026-10-24/25: broaden L29.7 from knowledge to research trustworthiness, maintain a methods rule library, create L29.7a/b/c, and require all lines to cite rules marked "current".
- 2026-10-26: approve X3 and L29.7d, sending only open-license papers to external reviewer models and piloting 4 papers first; L29.7d's red-team packages join the same review round.

## Where it stands
X3 is re-testing 2 papers with a single adjudicator before a combined review planned for 11-02 to 11-06; the PI is asked to decide by 11-01 how to proceed if the DeepSeek reviewer channel stays down. L29.7a's formal error-rate test is set for 11-01 to 11-03, and the canon-first acceptance rerun is pending.

# L29.7a Trustworthiness of Knowledge (Active)

This sub-project continues an earlier pilot that the PI approved, using local material only, with no downloads and no computation. On 2026-10-25 the Lead agent wrote the first 14 entries of a claim ledger, drawn from two reviewed L29.3 manuscripts: 10 judged unfounded or distorted (for example, that a 700-year return period means one 700-year storm), 3 partly founded (for example, "700-year = 50-year × 1.6" holds only under one wind-speed ratio model), and 1 still open (whether PBWD design is as safe as current codes). Three of the entries are errors this lab once wrote and later withdrew, kept to stop reuse. It also filled concept-card gaps from original sources, such as the ASCE open-terrain z0 = 0.03 m, while leaving the Eurocode and Chinese code z0 values and the ASCE 7-05 importance factor values open because no local source was available.

# L29.7b Methods Rulebook (Exploring)

L29.7b builds a shared rulebook of method and acceptance rules that every research line must cite when a rule is marked "current". The PI approved the sub-project on 2026-10-25 with no compute and no downloads, and the expansion plan served as its start-up plan. On the same day the Lead agent read the source rules from several lines and filed a v0 library: one file per rule, with a header, a change log and short self-test questions. Each rule taken from another line was sent back to that line's Lead agent to check that the library text was faithful to the original. By the end of the day five rules were current: replication acceptance format, extreme-event evaluation criteria, statistical stationarity criteria, checking classic benchmark tables, and figure acceptance. Two remained drafts: grid convergence index (GCI) validity conditions, three of whose clauses have no literature support yet, and four "anti-self-deception" rules that still await testing in L29.7c. The work was document-only.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI approved the sub-project (zero compute, no downloads). The Lead agent filed v0 with 5 rules (2 current, 3 drafts) and asked four line Leads to confirm.
- **2026-10-25**: The L22 replication line found 6 points of its original text missing from the library version. All were restored and the rule moved to v1.1, with no change to its meaning.
- **2026-10-25**: The L31.9c owner confirmed the evaluation-criteria summary. Two items (block bootstrap, mandatory sample size) are marked as line requirements with no literature basis.
- **2026-10-25**: The Fluent line asked for corrections to the stationarity rule (period scatter of about 14.6%, not 14 to 17%; a threshold for calling an effect resolvable). It also estimated, assuming independent periods, that sampling noise could be about 9% against a 2% threshold, and supplied literature sources for GCI validity. The cavity benchmark rule became current v1.0 and a GCI draft was written.
- **2026-10-25**: The CFD line confirmed the turbulence clause of the stationarity rule, which became current v1.0: periodic-shedding signals use one clause, broadband turbulence the other. Which clause applies to periodic signals with strong low-frequency modulation stays open. Passing the check means only that no drift was detected, not that the signal is proven stationary.
- **2026-10-25**: A figure-acceptance rule was drafted from CFD figure decisions. After CFD's two required edits it became current v1.0. Its use for wind-tunnel and field figures is a library extension that the original line never validated.
- **2026-10-26**: The parent Lead agent passed on two candidate rules that await the PI's approval: "skill score is not physical reliability", and acceptance checks for ML flow-field surrogates. Until approval they may only be listed in a "to be incorporated" table, with no rule text.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the sub-project with no compute and no downloads. The expansion plan counts as its start-up plan.
- Approved that rules marked "current" must be cited by all lines, and that major changes need the PI's decision.

## Where it stands
The library holds 5 current rules and 2 drafts. Next the Lead agent will draft rules for L29 topic-page headers and for "look up parameters before assuming them", select numerical self-test questions, and take in rules handed over from L22.8, with a target around 11-07.

# L29.7c Rule Compliance Audits and Effect Testing (Active)

This sub-project of the research-credibility effort (L29.7, under the "Make the World a Better Place" line) checks whether the lab's shared method rules are actually followed and whether they work. It has two parts: a monthly audit of about 10 decision records or reports from other lines, and effect tests of the rules, chiefly "X3", a blind test in which errors are planted in published papers to see whether the lab's checklist scorer and its six-model review panel catch them. Before any audit, the Lead agent froze a baseline snapshot of 1,357 decision records (1,373 changed since 10-01, minus its own line) with hashes, and wrote a first-round audit plan limited to two rules: replication acceptance (R-REP-01) and extreme-event evaluation (R-EVAL-01). After the PI approved X3, a pilot on 4 CC BY papers (3 with planted errors, 1 control) found that reviewers caught all three planted errors and none of the neutral wording edits was flagged as a fatal or major problem. The pilot used only 3 planted errors, so these counts are descriptive only and do not show that the review process is reliable overall. Cost came to about 1.7 times the estimate, above the pre-set 1.5 times stop line, so the full batch is paused pending a cheaper re-test on 2 papers.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Sub-project opened read-only after the PI approved the expansion plan. Lead agent froze the baseline snapshot and drafted the audit method (sample by rule, judge citation and actual compliance separately, blind double-scoring).
- **2026-10-25**: First-round audit plan v1 fixed at 17:10: five-level judgment words with operational definitions, 9 check items for R-REP-01 and 5 for R-EVAL-01, random seed 20261116, about 5 files per rule. Sampling set for 11-16, results 11-18.
- **2026-10-26**: PI approved the X3 pilot with two conditions. Lead agent counted only plain CC BY as open (no-derivatives licenses excluded), finding just 5 eligible papers in the scored set.
- **2026-10-26**: Pilot planted errors: two key wind-tunnel parameters deleted; a text value (5.4% changed to 8.4%) contradicting a table; a conclusion rewritten as a proven causal claim; plus 2 neutral edits per paper. The answer key was hashed and moved out of reviewers' reach.
- **2026-10-26**: Reviews returned. Detection: 6/6, 6/6, and 5/5 valid opinions (one reviewer channel could not read the file and was counted as a channel failure). The checklist scorers agreed on all 4 papers and caught the deleted parameters, but not the changed number, which is outside their checklist.
- **2026-10-27**: An independent instance without the answer key wrote verdicts; all three planted errors entered "must fix". A second independent scorer agreed with the Lead agent on all 24 reviews. Total cost about 1.7 times the estimate, so the full batch stopped.
- **2026-10-27**: The L29.7 Lead agent accepted the stop: re-test 2 papers with a single-instance verdict; fix the anonymisation step (one paper still showed author identifiers); keep the reviewer-substitution cap.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the sub-project as part of the L29.7 expansion (10-25).
- Approved the X3 pilot (10-26) with two fixed conditions: send only openly licensed papers to external reviewers, filling gaps with internal reports reported separately; and run a 4-paper pilot (3 planted, 1 control) before scaling up.

## Where it stands
The full X3 batch is paused until a 2-paper re-test stays within 1.5 times the cost estimate, the anonymisation rule is fixed, and the DeepSeek reviewer channel is restored (to be checked 11-01). The first compliance audit is scheduled for 11-16, with results on 11-18.

# Physical Corroboration and Adversarial Testing of Research Conclusions (Active)

L29.7d asks how the lab should decide whether a research result is correct and how to handle claims that extrapolate beyond what has been validated. Following the PI's analysis of how experimental, field-measurement and computational-method papers are usually validated, the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan that sets minimum thresholds for five research types (any missing threshold means failure), a three-level verdict (pass, conditional with an extrapolation statement, fail) and a graded extrapolation statement with four levels from E0 (inside the validated range) to E3 (no basis). After the PI approved the plan on 10-26, the Lead agent drafted validation standard v0 and a seed library of common pitfalls, and agreed with the sister sub-project L29.7c to contribute eight deliberately flawed test packages to a joint blind review. Literature cards were added to support the extrapolation rules; two web quick-search reports were used only as leads after checks against originals found several misstatements. The standard is a draft and has not yet been tried on existing conclusions or reviewed.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: Project opened; the PI asked that validation standards follow research type, with failure when standards are not met and extrapolation treated as a hard problem.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan submitted: thresholds in four columns (internal checks, external comparison, beyond current knowledge, minimum threshold), six evidence levels, a rule that evidence sharing the same inflow, mesh, training data or model family counts once, and a trial on three existing lab conclusions with an 80% agreement target between the Lead agent and an independent assessor.
- **2026-10-26**: The PI approved the plan and its four proposals. The Lead agent wrote standard v0 and a pitfall library with 13 sourced entries.
- **2026-10-26**: Joint testing with L29.7c agreed: eight packages in four new error classes (unfaithful definitions, physically impossible results, out-of-range extrapolation, counterfeit evidence), two each; materials due 10-31, joint review 11-02 to 11-04, statistics 11-05 to 11-06. L29.7c's six amendments were adopted.
- **2026-10-26**: Literature cards added. Checks against originals corrected four misstatements in a web quick-search report, for example on a rectangular-cylinder benchmark comparison, where the original reports scatter in fluctuating quantities for all turbulence treatments rather than failure of one model class. Cards supported rules such as reporting model discrepancy with predictions, judging validation per output quantity, and not assuming sharp-edged bluff bodies are Reynolds-number independent. The pitfall library reached 15 entries, 14 with sources.

## What the PI decided
- Validation criteria are set by research type (experiment, field measurement, computational method); failing them means the result fails, and extrapolation needs separate treatment.
- Approved the plan; the "missing threshold means failure" rule is not applied retroactively to existing conclusions, only to new ones and to conclusions given to the PI or published.
- Extrapolation level E3 may never be written as a conclusion, only as "to be tested"; a Lean formal-proof pilot only selects a topic and estimates cost within two weeks.
- The red-team packages are merged into L29.7c's blind review batch rather than reviewed separately.

## Where it stands
Next steps are a consistency checklist and assumption ledger (10-29 to 10-31), the eight flawed packages and pitfall library by 10-31, trials on three existing conclusions, and standard v1 for review on 11-08. The formal Deep Research step has not been done because the service returned an error; it will be re-sent once fixed.

# L30.1 Wind Tunnel Test Automation (Active)

This line asks how far wind tunnel pressure testing should be automated when the lab has no tunnel of its own and depends on outside facilities. A two-step literature review and three independent reviewer models, who all gave "support with reservations", led the Lead agent to recommend not pursuing full automation now. That is a project decision, not a claim that it cannot be done. The first target was a software-only "digital chain" from a parameter table to model geometry, print files, tap and channel tables, test matrix and automated quality checks. Two literature gaps were kept narrow: no robotic whole-model change or automatic tube connection was found for pressure or load testing in civil tunnels, and no same-geometry printed versus machined building-model Cp comparison was found within the checked range. After the PI approved a start, the digital-chain prototype (L30.1d) and a facility-independent interface and safety specification (L30.1a) were built and tested only on synthetic "virtual wind tunnel" data. These results show that the software and data flow work; they say nothing about the safety or measurement quality of any real facility.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16**: Status-and-roadmap page delivered after three reviews; automation graded L0 to L5, phases A to D. Four sub-projects created but not started.
- **2026-10-19**: All work paused under the PI's new planning rule; start-up plan submitted, recommending only L30.1d.
- **2026-10-20**: Read-only draft of 24 automation-interface items prepared for a planned test facility in another line.
- **2026-10-22**: Citation snowballing gave a pool of 564 papers, 116 after screening, 12 relevant groups. Printed-tap studies checked so far (airfoils, cylinders, tubing) were not controlled same-geometry comparisons, so the gap statement was narrowed, not removed.
- **2026-10-24**: PI approved opening L30.1d. Checkpoints met early: M11 channel table matched the existing one in 728/728 cells; M11 and CAARC 1:400 each produced five outputs with one command. STEP files were not delivered because the CAD library exceeded the 1 GB dependency limit.
- **2026-10-25**: Shared data specification v1.3 frozen after a three-reviewer review (10 must-fix items addressed).
- **2026-10-26**: Three virtual tunnels (one 80-tap set, public time series plus simulated tubing at 70/45/55 Hz, noise, blockage) passed the partner line's validator. A deliberately drifted station was flagged. The source model has a different section ratio, and records of 32.8 s were looped to 300 s, so no peak estimates are possible.
- **2026-10-26**: L30.1a interface and safety spec v0 and v1: 37 pre-registered dry-run and fault-injection cases passed, plus 7 new cases. It was kept as a draft and not frozen because the partner line does not need it yet.
- **2026-10-27**: The new validator and the official CAARC tap layout (289 taps) arrived early; spec v1.4 was dispatched.

## What the PI decided
- Create all sub-projects for upcoming presentations, but do not start work on them yet (10-16).
- Projects without an approved plan stop, summarize, and wait for approval (10-19).
- Open only L30.1d, with the line making its own simple geometry (10-24).
- The planned facility will likely not be ready in time and is not a civil-engineering tunnel. The partner tunnel will be chosen later; for now, use data from several virtual tunnels and "only build the framework". L30.1a was then approved on that basis (10-26).

## Where it stands
L30.1d is producing spec v1.4, due 11-02, which will go to three reviewers before freezing. L30.1a is paused until the PI selects a real partner tunnel, and L30.1b and L30.1c stay paused. Superseded intermediate outputs are scheduled for cleanup under the standing authorization from 11-01.

# L30.1d Offline Digital-Chain Prototype for Wind-Tunnel Pressure Models (Exploring)

This sub-project builds an offline "digital chain" for pressure-model wind-tunnel testing. From one parameter table, a single command should generate five matched products: parametric geometry, a print file with pressure-tap passages, a tap and channel table, a test matrix, and an automatic quality-control report on synthetic pressure data. Examples: a 60×60 mm section prism (M11) and CAARC at 1:400. The specification is shared with the wind-tunnel comparison line (L30.3). The regenerated M11 channel table matches the existing one cell for cell (728/728). STEP files were not delivered because the CAD library needed 1.7 GB, over the 1 GB limit. All geometry is demonstration only. Specification v1.3 was frozen after a three-reviewer round. The PI then asked for a framework fed by several virtual wind tunnels, and three synthetic tunnels were run through the chain. v1.4 is not yet frozen.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16**: The sub-project was held at "not started" pending a start order.
- **2026-10-24**: The PI approved the plan, with two changes: build simple geometry in-house and share the specification with L30.3. The worker agent delivered checkpoint 1 (spec draft and the M11 channel table, 728/728 cells matching) and checkpoint 2 (parameter-driven code; CAARC with 80 taps, of which 40 rest on assumed rings). The worker agent found that the 1980 CAARC reference paper itself prints 183.88 m for 600 ft (182.88 m).
- **2026-10-24**: Checkpoint 3 was first submitted incomplete. The Lead agent rejected the early stop. The second version produced hollow shells with through-wall taps and base outlets. Hoses are routed logically, not as solids.
- **2026-10-25**: Three independent reviewer models reviewed specification v1.1: two supported it with reservations and one did not support freezing as is. Ten must-fix items were found, including a channel-order conflict with the L30.3 validator and paths that could let dead or non-finite channels pass QC. All were fixed, and v1.3 was frozen with 27 tests passing.
- **2026-10-26**: The PI asked to use data from several virtual tunnels and to build only the framework for now. Public TPU time series were mapped onto the 80 CAARC taps, with per-facility characteristics added for three virtual tunnels. All three passed the L30.3 schema check, which is a single-file format check only, not measured-data certification. The source record is 32.8 s looped to 300 s and cannot be used for peak estimates. A worker agent found the validator could accept synthetic data posing as measured, and L30.3 agreed to add a mandatory submission-mode field.
- **2026-10-27**: CAARC was switched to the formal 289-tap layout (81 roof taps, roof data proxied from side walls). Two frozen v1.3 files had been overwritten in place during development; they were restored byte-exact into snapshot folders. Of three independent reviewer models, two did not support freezing v1.4 as is and one supported it with reservations, giving nine must-fix items: four in the L30.3 validator and five in this line's code. This line's five were fixed the same evening.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the start order: geometry is built in-house, and the specification is shared with the comparison line L30.3.
- On 10-26: the candidate physical tunnel is unlikely to be ready in time and is not a civil-engineering tunnel. For now, use data from several virtual wind tunnels and only build the framework.

## Where it stands
Specification v1.4 will be frozen once L30.3's validator v5.3 (due by 10-31) is out and the three virtual-tunnel files re-run correctly under it: format-only and synthetic in demo mode, and failing in production mode. v1.3 remains in force meanwhile. Roof routing, hose solids and measured validation remain undone.

# L30.1a Partner Wind Tunnel Interface and Safety Specification (Paused)

This sub-project of the wind tunnel automation line was set up to write, with a future partner wind tunnel, a programmable control interface and safety-interlock scheme, plus a pressure comparison of printed versus machined models; external contact is reserved for the PI. It sat idle until 10-26, when the PI approved a facility-independent version using virtual wind tunnels as the test case. A worker agent wrote an interface and safety specification (setpoint and status read/write, unified time base, control logs, a state machine, data output mapped onto the already frozen data specification, and four interlock layers: hardware emergency stop, facility local interlock, interface whitelist and script self-check, with continuous human supervision and final stop authority for the operator over the first two layers). A virtual-tunnel reference implementation then passed all 37 preregistered dry-run cases across three virtual tunnels, including fault injection, and the Lead agent independently reproduced the result. This shows only that the synthetic software flow is correct; it is not a safety or measurement-quality certification of any real facility, and whitelist limits and error codes are engineering inference.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16**: Sub-project created as "not started", waiting for a partner wind tunnel; no work done.
- **2026-10-24**: Status report: paused awaiting a partner tunnel; the PI to choose the facility.
- **2026-10-26**: The PI approved a facility-independent framework built on virtual tunnels. Specification v0 and a test plan with criteria fixed in advance were delivered and accepted ahead of the 11-02 deadline.
- **2026-10-26**: Reference implementation: 37 of 37 cases passed, with out-of-range setpoints, emergency stops, time-base loss, missing logs, local interlocks and stale status all blocked or isolated and logged; inputs unchanged.
- **2026-10-26**: Specification v1 clarified emergency-stop event logging, external reset permission and log-break recovery; the original 37 cases showed no regression and 7 new cases passed. The comparison line (L30.3) said it will not use this specification for now, so v1 stays a draft, not reviewed or frozen.

## What the PI decided
- Said the candidate facility would likely not be ready in time and is not a civil-engineering tunnel; the partner will be chosen later, and for now the work should use data from several virtual tunnels and "only build the framework".
- External contact with any facility is made by the PI.

## Where it stands
No tasks are running. Remaining work, including the printed-versus-machined comparison and replacing the virtual stub with a real facility adapter and limits, waits for the PI to choose a partner wind tunnel.

# L30.1c Feasibility Study of Robotic Model Changing (Paused)

This sub-project is a long-term feasibility argument on whether a robot arm could swap whole wind tunnel models and connect pressure tubes automatically, covering feasibility, cost and safety. Its scope is a written assessment only, with no prototype or procurement. The basis recorded so far is that two literature searches found no precedent for robotic model changing or automatic tube connection in pressure and load testing in civil wind tunnels; the closest found was a 2015 conference paper in which a robot arm assembled building models in a wind tunnel and measured wind. The Lead agent's plan for after the start: search the knowledge base and run a two-step literature review on automatic model changing in aeronautical and automotive tunnels and collaborative robot safety, write the assessment in three parts (feasibility, cost in three tiers with sources or marked estimates, safety), then send it to three reviewer models. No research has been done.
