# L31.9f Impact of Internal Climate Variability on Extreme Winds and Design Wind Speeds

## Objective
Evaluate the impact of natural variability modes (ENSO, PDO/IPO, NAO, AMO, IOD, MJO, etc.) on near-surface extreme winds and design wind speeds across hazard types, structured across three scales: single-year (phase stratification), multi-year (decadal modulation, storm clustering), and design reference period (estimation bias and apparent non-stationarity in finite records). Source: Point (4) of Liang Hu's five comments on 10-25 (for exact wording see).

## Current Status
- 10-25 Kickoff plan written:, awaiting Liang Hu's approval. No computation dispatched and no Colab sessions opened prior to approval.
- 10-25 Web quick search sent (Grok 402 circuit breaker triggered, automatically switched to Gemini web quick search), task brief.
- Knowledge base status: searched across 8 phrasing variants and local full-text pages, finding almost no direct cards on "variability -> near-surface extreme wind"; 12 existing related cards are listed in Section 4 of the plan.

- 10-25 Second quick search returned (substituting for DR); Lead verified two papers against original texts (Chen & Duan 2018, Jagger & Elsner 2006) and one online (Wohland 2021), finding fabricated numbers in the quick search and treating it as leads only.

## Decisions Made
- Quantified objects and operational definitions of decision terms across the three scales finalized before starting work (Section 1 of the plan; 5% threshold is an assumption of this project). Decision.
- Boundaries: model capability belongs to L31.9e, trends belong to L31.9b, conversion conventions belong to L31.9a/d, and station-level bottlenecks belong to L31.9c; evaluation methodology cites L31.9c evaluation criteria rules v1.

## Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10-25 | First web quick search (Gemini, Grok circuit-broken) | Approx. 60 leads, 48/60 DOIs exist; at least 2 misattributions (DOI for Jeong 2008 is actually Fast 2008; DOI for Oderiz 2020 is actually Patra 2020), "[full text]" labels unreliable | |
| 10-25 | Deep Research Step 2 | **Not done**: rolling 30-day quota 90/90 exhausted; sent second web quick search instead (task brief) | - |
| 10-25 | (24 verified seed DOIs + 10 search queries, from 1990 onward) | 4062 unique papers (5000 cap truncated 1281 seed citations, mainly d4PDF forward citations); 2 queries returned 0 hits and needed rephrasing; Lead selected 39 papers by title, : 4 already held locally, 35 confirmed absent; card creation delegated to litwiki (queued) | |

| 10-25 | Second web quick search (substitute for exhausted DR quota) | 14/18 DOIs exist, but with multiple author-DOI mismatches (Doney, Lau, Or, Feser, etc.); Shantou 38.5/40.8/36.2 m/s attributed to Chen & Duan 2018 is absent from the original text (which only has Fig. 9 and "La Nina exceeds El Nino by more than 8%"); "false alarm rate 18-24%" attributed to Wohland 2021 is absent from the original text (which states: significant trends occur 45% of the time in control runs; 20-year internal variability is an order of magnitude larger than forced change) | |
| 10-25 | litwiki card creation | Among 39 papers, 9 full-text page-numbered cards (Group A 4 papers, Group B 5 papers) and 30 abstract/bibliographic-only cards; AMS all-channel circuit breaker triggered that day, and MDPI excluded per Liang Hu's rule. Continuation delegated (queued) | |

Ruling; supplemental card delegation sent to litwiki | |

F1/F2 upgraded to v1.1: added ocean grid-point sub-period evidence (ERA-40 approx. 10-year sub-period 100-year wind speeds differ significantly from the full record in storm-track regions, consistent with decadal NAO phase); F2-5 gaps (1) and (3) still hold after re-verification | |

# L31.1 登陆台风内边界层（课题 1）

## 开题卡（10-16 v1，未做研究）
**核心科学问题**：台风登陆时，海上平衡边界层越过海岸进入粗糙陆面，内边界层（IBL）从海岸向内陆长出：在离岸多远、多高的范围里，风廓线、湍流度和阵风因子还"带着海上记忆"？规范里按暴露类别和上风距离来判风剖面的做法（ASCE 7 暴露过渡规则，条文待核）在台风条件下是否成立？台风的强旋转、超梯度风和非平稳性会不会让 IBL 的增长规律和良态风不同？

**现有认识与空白**
- 库内有：登陆台风中 ASOS 10 m 风与 WSR-88D VAD 廓线的对比（17 个台风、7 个站，考虑了粗糙度暴露的标准化）： p.1, 3–7；登陆飓风近地阵风因子随粗糙度类别和径向位置的变化： p.4–10；沿海台风竖向廓线观测：；台风边界层分高度模型（Kepert 2010 Part I/II，Snaiki & Wu 2017）：（10 张卡）。
- 10-16 补卡（litwiki，前缀，页码见各卡，PDF 页与期刊页已分栏）。
 - 内边界层理论：Garratt 1990 IBL 综述 `CCSQBC2J_*`；Garratt 1994 `TPFDXT2B_*`（§6.3、Fig.16 在 PDF p.20–21/期刊 p.108–109）。
 - 登陆过渡：Powell 1982 Frederic 登陆边界层转变 `P2X3QPNY_*`；登陆期间飓风边界层转变 `8WDH8J8V_*`（JAS 2020）；Kepert 2002 登陆影响（会议短文，无期刊页）`4DXCV6LE_*`；内核边界层理想化模拟 `4VSXZ2VX_*`。
 - 观测：Harvey 登陆眼墙观测 `GFXNLY5E_*`；登陆近地最大风 `3JNGWVQY_*`；GPS 下投探空风廓线 `UMJLAEGX_*`；高风速海面拖曳系数降低 `HKB46DW7_*`。
 - 数据来源：Ma 2026 `Z4VTJBVX_*` 是 arXiv 预印本（廓线重建网络），**不是** HRD 数据集原文；引用数据时以数据 README 为准。
- 空白（初判，待精读核实）：经典 IBL 理论（Garratt）基于定常的良态风；台风登陆把"海陆突变"和"风暴径向结构/衰减"叠在一起，现有登陆研究多为个例，缺少工程可用的 fetch–风速比–阵风因子关系。精读后修订本条。

**切入点与可用数据/工具**（只读引用）
- HRD 下投探空廓线 7,524 条（10–300 m，2001–2022，海上近核心）：（README 注明不是陆上廓线，部分 10 m 值为赋值）。用作"海上上游廓线"。
- 登陆 ASOS 配对：10 次登陆、29 个站，H08 风场带海陆粗糙度切换：，v1 结果为持续风偏差 +9.9%、阵风中位绝对误差 11.2%，67 个站次中 34 个截尾（项目页 10-14 行）。（10-16 更正：事件表和 v1 配对仍在本地，TACC 归档里只有；已复制到。）
- 台风风场残差诊断（H08 外圈偏高约 2.5 m/s、1 RMW 以内偏低）：。
- 旧 WRF 台风算例（未审计）：Isabel 2003 四重嵌套、香港 2018-09-16 WRF–OpenFOAM：见。

**第一步最小实验**（0 SU，工作站 小脚本）
- 输入：下投探空按"相对最大风半径（RMW）的径向位置 × 强度"合成海上平均廓线；ASOS 登陆站按"离海岸距离（上风向陆上 fetch）"分组的平均风与阵风因子。
- 做法：算陆/海风速比和阵风因子随 fetch 的变化，与经典 IBL 增长律及规范暴露过渡规则对比。
- 输出：fetch–风速比–阵风因子图，以及"规范规则 vs 台风实测"偏差表。
- 判据：若在 fetch 小于数公里时，偏差超过 ASOS 本身的不确定度（10-16 修订：±10% 在 E69U739F 里查不到，改用数据自身 bootstrap 95% CI 与同站对比），课题成立，进入第二步：WRF/CM1 登陆 LES 或半理想化算例，需 Liang Hu 定先后后再申请机时。

**预计工作量**：第一步约 5 人-日、0 SU、0 Colab。第二步（登陆 LES）约 15 人-日，CRC 单节点若干天或 TACC 约 300–800 SU，开算前按规则送审。

## 未决与下一步
- **10-20 ASOS 阵风口径更正（情报转告，事件线/CM1 线已核原件）**：IEM 1 分钟 gust_sknt 按传感器区分——超声站（SW ≥2.7A，Vaisala 425/IFWS，多数站 2007–2009 换装）为该分钟最高滑动 3 s 平均（截断整节），杯式站为离散 5 s；本页之前写的"5 s/2 min"不准确。依据 （ASOS SW 2.7A Release Note §3.3/§3.4、TIN 02-30A 原件）与 （HOMR 逐站换装日）。对本线的影响（Lead 判断，未送审）：
 - L31.1-11 定稿（同站按风向比，非台风 2010–2024）：同站内传感器基本不变，比较里相互抵消，**结论方向不受影响**；口径名称改为"按站 3 s（超声）/2 min"。残余：2010 年后仍有换装或 2022–2023 再换 AWMT702-HT 的站，需按日期核。
 - 扩样本（2004–2024 台风，GF 1.223 vs 约 1.29、同站 9 对 8 正）：311 个站次中 65 个在 2009 年及以前（分钟数 18.7%），可能是杯式 5 s；跨站分档和跨年份的同站对比可能被传感器混杂，**标"待传感器复核"**，不作定论。
 - 与 ASCE 3 s 阵风因子的对比：超声站本来就是 3 s，解读要改（不再假设"5 s 偏低"）。
 - 处理：恢复后第一步按 HOMR 逐站逐日标传感器类型，重算"只用超声时段"与"加传感器固定效应"两种敏感性（工作站 小脚本，0 SU），结论用三种读法并列。
1. 站内固定效应 2010–2024 已完成，结论送审 （6 位）。平均风/阵风：固定站网配对不可行；改查野外测风塔离岸剖面数据（Gemini）。若无公开数据，平均风这一半只能靠第二步数值模拟（需 Liang Hu 定先后后申请机时）。决策。
2. 换海上参照：同事件近岸 NDBC/C-MAN 实测，替代 H08，判平均风与 3 s 阵风的净影响。
3. 文献已补（litwiki，10-17 回，索引）：
 - 推算结果：10 m 风速计在 fetch 约 70–210 m 时进入内边界层，约 2 km 时 90% 调整完。ASCE 的 183 m 大致对应"刚进入内边界层"，不是"调整完"。0.2–0.5 km 正处在过渡层，和实测 GF 偏低一致。
 - 最近先例：Miller 等 2015（FCMP）。只有一个站（Irene T1），覆盖海→沙滩 0–300 m，Iu 和 GF 随离岸距离增大（PDF 第 20–22 页 / 期刊第 148–150 页，Lead 已开原文核对）；另有粗糙地表→开阔地 0–2.5 km，约 ≥1 km 才平衡，方向相反，不可套用。
 - 本课题的增量：用多站 ASOS 覆盖海→陆 0.2–5 km，并直接和规范的过渡规则对照。
 - 仍缺 Schroeder & Smith 2003（原文在未挂载的 I: 盘）、ESDU 82026、Wieringa 1992、Cook 1985。
4. 按风速分档、剔除对流阵风后复核 GF。
5. 两站特例的风险：SPG、NEW 都是伸进水里的小机场，扩样本前不下结论。

## Liang Hu 注

> **页码更正（10-26，L31.1e 发现、Lead 用 pdftotext 复核）**：ASCE 7-22 §26.7.3 D 类条文跨印刷 274–275：PDF 336 = 印刷 274，「600 ft (183 m) or 20 times」句在 PDF 337 / 印刷 275。本页及 旧记录里的「PDF 336 / 印刷 275」配对有误，以此为准。

# L31.1 Landfalling Typhoon Internal Boundary Layer (Topic 1)

## Current Status
**10-22 Citation snowballing (full re-snowballing per Liang Hu's instruction)**: pool (4799 papers, initial screen 1416, 434 from snowballing alone). Lead screened 6 papers for card creation (items 12-17 in checklist), focusing on a sea-land transition mean wind profile model (2023) and a step-roughness-change LES (2002), which can be directly compared against the land/sea wind ratio of 0.968→0.840 from the step-2 40 m LES. Conclusions unchanged for now, to be compared once cards return.
> 10-22 Cards returned: the sea-land transition mean wind profile model (2023, full text) only gives prescribed fetches of 0.2/2/20 km and tabulated marine/transition mean winds (PDF p.12 / journal p.424) without distance-resolved land/sea wind ratios, so it cannot be directly compared against 0.968→0.840 on this line; the remaining 5 papers have bibliographic entries only. Conclusion unchanged.

In progress. Review (6 reviewers) has ruled: **original wording not established, established after narrowing**.
- Revised conclusion (L31.1-11 finalized numbers): Within the same station, wind directions with an upwind overland fetch of 0.18-2 km have a gust factor (IEM gust / 2 min mean) ~0.03-0.04 lower than wind directions with fetch ≥5 km (non-typhoon; 0.030-0.032 when the long-fetch side is restricted to open terrain, 0.037-0.039 across all long-fetch sectors; station + event bootstrap CIs are all <0); the difference is no longer significant by 2-5 km. The order of magnitude is compatible with an internal boundary layer adjustment scale of ~2 km at 10 m height. Typhoon periods show the same direction, but the interaction term is not significant.
- This is an observational association, not causality; it does not involve modifications to ASCE 7 exposure classifications or design loads.
- FCMP (core): Same-tower comparable data cover only 4 towers across 3 storms with very wide CIs, neither independently replicating nor refuting the result; qualified pairs on the short-fetch side with synchronous marine reference are 0. **Observational pathway concluded**; mean wind and design gust can only rely on step-2 landfall LES/WRF, pending Liang Hu's decision.
- Mean-wind half (historical record): Fixed station networks are infeasible. Verified by Gemini, the only qualified public dataset is the FCMP wind towers (DesignSafe PRJ-3195 / PRJ-2034, 13 hurricanes from 1999-2008, 36 tower deployments, two levels at 5 m and 10 m, 1 Hz, with coordinates; spot-checked by Lead). StickNet measurement height is only 2.25 m with no public time series; no wind-tower time series could be found for Idalia, Laura, Michael, or Harvey. Assigned to core (L31.1-12, queued after) to cross-check gust factors and estimate mean-wind ratios using FCMP.
- Revisions and robustness checks required by the ruling have been completed (core).

- Step-2 preparation (upper level, 10-17, revocable): plan . Run CM1 with periodic sea strip + land strip, reusing L31.2's typhoon boundary layer configuration. G0 passed: for code modifications see; Lead verified that `use_avg_sfc=false` when `testcase=6`, so land-strip z0 is not averaged out. Short-test job submitted and registered, still queued at 10-17 05:18 (ComputeOps); Lead scheduled an 8 h fallback follow-up. At 10-17 13:19, found that a same-source short test in L31.2 failed immediately upon starting due to `ppnode=36` mismatching 48 cores; while our job was still queued, Lead changed the namelist to `ppnode=48` prior to startup (original retained) and scheduled another 6 h follow-up. After starting at 13:20, the job aborted during initialization due to a missing land-use table in the run directory (although the exit-code file wrote 0), producing no results. Lead verified that land-strip z0 is set after reading the table, so supplying the table does not alter the design. Assigned core to resubmit in a fresh root after supplying the table (L31.1-14b): job completed the full 600 s (finished at 16:45). Measured 1.99 s wall-clock per model second, dt 0.5 s; land-strip ust 1.46 vs sea-strip 1.11 m/s. Extrapolation: ~12 h on a single cluster node per 40 m case; ~95 h for a 20 m case, requiring supercomputer allocation (~190 SU, indicative). Reported to upper level. On 10-17, upper level cleared two 40 m cases (z0 0.03 primary / 0.3 sensitivity), assigned to core (L31.1-15): two new run roots, 3D frames every 1800 s, post-processing on the cluster, outputting results per frozen criteria. Submitted two jobs at 10-17 16:58 (z0 0.03 and z0 0.3), resource request, registered, queued; each case includes an automatic stop guard if output exceeds 20 GB or group free space drops below 300 GB. Credibility-gate heights adjusted to 30-210 m matching tower points (α, U(30)/U(110)) prior to generating results. 10-18: Both cases completed the full 21600 s (log ended normally, ~12 h wall-clock each, ~14.5 GB output each); post-processing jobs wrote the tower window summary at 09:33, and tower-point criteria are out (verified by Lead): credibility gate passed; for z0=0.03, 10 m land/sea wind ratios at 0.2/0.5/1/2/5/8 km are 0.968/0.948/0.923/0.895/0.854/0.840 (provisional), and for z0=0.3 they are 0.87/0.80/0.73/0.68/0.61/0.60; GF increases by ~0.03 inland from the coast (z0=0.03). 3D gate and δ(x) are out (. Answering the gust question requires 20 m, pending Liang Hu's decision. On 10-18, upper level requested a cost short test for the 20 m option first: for geometry check see (sea strip 7.0 km + land strip 4.52 km, nx=128, ny=576; reference profile is ~2% low when the sea strip is 5 km); short test completed (L31.1-18): A (vertical 20 m) 3.69 s per model second, dt 0.333 s, 6 h extrapolated to 22.1 h (single cluster node, ~44 SU indicative); B (vertical 10 m) 4.63 s per model second, 6 h extrapolated to 27.8 h; land-strip 10 m ust 1.36 / sea-strip 1.03 m/s, znt 0.030 / 0.002 m. Reported to upper level. Upper level conditionally cleared A after review: 7 mandatory revisions. Frozen criteria and geometry (10-18 11:10, prior to any 20 m production results); preparation of the new run root and resolved-fraction pre-check assigned to core L31.1-19, with no submission if the pre-check fails. 10-18 11:4x: new root compiled, not submitted; measured frames insufficient, Lead similarity estimate gives A at 10 m ≈0.72 (20 m interface value alone ~0.6), 30 m ≈0.77, 50 m ≈0.84, so under the frozen criteria A will likely fail the 0.80 threshold at 10/30 m; on 10-18, upper level chose "still run A, narrowing the objective to a mean-wind resolution gate" (narrowed after viewing the pre-check, not original plan; Revision 1 of frozen document): test convergence between 40 m and 20 m for 10/30/50 m R_U to close the "provisional" label on the 40 m case's 10 m mean-wind ratio; evaluate gust factor only at heights passing the 0.80 gate, recording "uninterpretable" at 10/30 m if they fail the gate. Perform restart-append test and L31.2 frame measurement first before production (core L31.1-21), submitting only if conditions are met. 10-18 12:1x: restart-append test passed (: 150→300 s, 200 integer seconds across 24 tower-point ranks continuous without duplication, prior frames not overwritten; frame-number continuation across the next 3D frame was not tested, so production does not rely on restart by default, keeping it only as a fallback if 22 h exceeds 24 h); L31.2 20 m frames had not yet reached 3600 s (~13:15), resolved-fraction measurement not yet performed, run not submitted; Lead scheduled a follow-up in 80 minutes to assign core the measurement and submission check. Restart-append not yet actually tested. 20 m case pending Liang Hu's decision, to be sent afterward to 14:2x: four-frame marine pre-check (L31.1-22) gave resolved fractions at 10/30/50/70/110 m of 0.781 (upper interface alone 0.640) / 0.768 / 0.842 / 0.875 / 0.905, meeting the frozen submission condition (50 m ≥0.75, 10/30 m below 0.80); production run submitted (registered, h_rt 24 h, continuous run). Note that the pre-check uses a pure marine z0 sample, so land-strip fractions must be measured post-production; no R_U/GF values will be reported before results are complete.

## Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10-16 | Data retrieval: B1B4 event table / v1 pairing (local read-only copy); IEM re-fetched 67 station-storm ASOS 1-min records with wind direction | 60 station-storms had data, 52 had ≥20 kt minutes | |
| 10-16 | Computed upwind overland fetch along 5° rays per station (WorldCover 2021) | 38 stations; no station had a sector <0.2 km | |
| 10-16 | GF (5 s/2 min) binned by fetch, using sector medians as units | 0.2-0.5 km: 1.22 (CI 1.20-1.24); >5 km: 1.33-1.37; within-station difference 0.07-0.25; sensitivity checks (30 kt, water criterion 0.5/3 km) preserved direction |, |
| 10-16 | Wind speed ratio = observed / H08 open-water equivalent | 0.55-1.33, no fetch trend; H08 errors swamp the expected ~14% deceleration | |
| 10-16 | Dropsonde marine profile composite (r/RMW × intensity) | α(20-150 m) 0.04-0.11; median z0 1.7e-3 m, spanning two orders of magnitude; few samples near RMW |, |
| 10-17 | Expanded sample (core): 2004-2024 landfalls ≥64 kt, 41 storms, 78 stations, 2,330 sectors; paired with NDBC/C-MAN marine references | 0.2-0.5 km: GF 1.223 (7 stations); ≥5 km: ~1.29; 8 of 9 within-station pairs positive, mean difference 0.106; unchanged after removing convective proxy; land/sea ratio ~0.7 in both bins, inconclusive | |
| 10-17 | Lead check for local roughness confounding (station-clustered bootstrap) | Short-fetch effect −0.016 (CI −0.066 to +0.034), not significant; consistent direction within z0 bins, but only 4-5 stations per bin | |
| 10-17 | Within-station fixed effects (core), 2020-2024 strong-wind days, 20 stations | Non-typhoon short − long is −0.054 (CI −0.073 to −0.038); typhoon interaction −0.052, CI crosses zero when switching to 200 km threshold; bot's z0 control including water pixels rendered the effect insignificant | |
| 10-17 | Lead verification: switched to z0 control using land pixels only | Non-typhoon short − long is −0.058 (CI −0.073 to −0.035); −0.048 after adding far ring (CI −0.086 to −0.012); negative at 14 of 18 stations |, |
| 10-17 | Within-station fixed effects extended to 2010-2024 (core), 20 stations, 200/300 km × three z0 controls | Non-typhoon short − long is −0.041 to −0.049 (all CIs <0); typhoon short − long is −0.057 to −0.078 (all CIs <0); interaction −0.015 to −0.032 (all CIs cross zero); leave-one-station-out does not change sign |, |
| 10-17 | Synchronous shoreline reference pairing for mean wind / gust (core) | Among 80 stations, only 3 geometric pairs exist (EYW←NQX, NAK←tplm2, PIE←SPG), and strictly qualified open-water exposure after auditing the reference stations is 0, **unestimable**; in ASCE 7-22 Table 26.10-1 (PDF p. 338 / print p. 277, verified by Lead), Kz at 30 ft is 0.98 for Exposure C and 1.16 for Exposure D, giving an equivalent velocity ratio of 0.919 | |
| 10-17 | Sent for review (6 reviewers) + Lead supplementary calculation | 4 supported with reservations, 2 did not support original wording. Supplementary calculation: short bin changed to 0.183-1 km, excluding NYG gives −0.044 [−0.059, −0.034]; equal station weighting −0.048 [−0.068, −0.027]; distance gradient −0.046 / −0.041 / −0.037 / −0.007 (0.18-0.5 / 0.5-1 / 1-2 / 2-5 km). Ruling: established after narrowing |, |
| 10-17 | Revisions per ruling (core): specification fix, event-level bootstrap, same-sample z0 control, long-fetch side restricted to open terrain, convective filtering, gust duration, distance gradient | Non-typhoon −0.037 to −0.039; open-terrain long-fetch side −0.030 to −0.032 (10 stations); gradient vanishes by 2-5 km; interaction not significant; post-2010 gusts are mostly 3 s (14/21 stations upgraded sensors in 2003-2009) | |
| 10-17 | FCMP wind-tower cross-check + marine reference (core) | 40 tower deployments; same-tower short − long covers only 4 towers, 3 s/10 min is −0.016 [−0.32, +0.29], inconclusive; cross-tower descriptive <0.18 km is 1.34 vs ≥5 km 1.55; qualified short-fetch marine reference pairs are 0 | |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- **10-20 ASOS gust specification correction (forwarded by intelligence, original documents verified by event/CM1 lines)**: IEM 1-minute `gust_sknt` differs by sensor type: ultrasonic stations (SW ≥2.7A, Vaisala 425/IFWS, most stations upgraded in 2007-2009) report the highest running 3 s mean within the minute (truncated to whole knots), whereas cup stations report discrete 5 s gusts; "5 s/2 min" written earlier on this page was inaccurate. Based on (ASOS SW 2.7A Release Note §3.3/§3.4, TIN 02-30A original text) and (HOMR station-by-station sensor upgrade dates). Impact on this line (Lead judgment, not reviewed):
 - L31.1-11 finalized results (within-station comparison across wind directions, non-typhoon 2010-2024): sensors within a given station remained largely unchanged, canceling out in within-station comparisons, so **the direction of the conclusion is unaffected**; specification label updated to "station-native 3 s (ultrasonic) / 2 min". Residual check: stations upgraded after 2010 or further replaced with AWMT702-HT in 2022-2023 need date-by-date verification.
 - Expanded sample (2004-2024 typhoons, GF 1.223 vs ~1.29, 8 of 9 within-station pairs positive): 65 of 311 station-storms occurred in 2009 or earlier (18.7% of minutes) and may be cup-anemometer 5 s gusts; cross-station binning and multi-year within-station comparisons may be confounded by sensor upgrades, so **mark as "pending sensor verification"** and do not treat as final.
 - Comparison with ASCE 3 s gust factor: since ultrasonic stations are natively 3 s, the interpretation must be revised (no longer assuming "5 s underestimates 3 s").
 - Action: as the first step upon resumption, label sensor types by station and date per HOMR, recomputing two sensitivity analyses ("ultrasonic periods only" and "adding sensor fixed effects", small workstation script, 0 SU), and present all three readings side by side.
1. Within-station fixed effects for 2010-2024 completed, conclusion sent for review (6 reviewers). Mean wind / gust: fixed station-network pairing is infeasible; switched to searching for field wind-tower offshore profile datasets (Gemini). If no public data exist, the mean-wind half can only rely on step-2 numerical simulations (requiring Liang Hu to set priority before requesting compute time). Decision .
2. Alternative marine reference: use co-event nearshore NDBC/C-MAN measurements in place of H08 to evaluate net effects on mean wind and 3 s gust.
3. Literature supplemented (litwiki, returned 10-17, index):
 - Analytical estimate: a 10 m anemometer enters the internal boundary layer at a fetch of ~70-210 m and reaches 90% adjustment at ~2 km. ASCE's 183 m roughly corresponds to "just entering the internal boundary layer" rather than "fully adjusted". Fetches of 0.2-0.5 km sit squarely in the transition zone, consistent with the lower measured GF.
 - Closest precedent: Miller et al. 2015 (FCMP). Covers only a single station (Irene T1) across sea→beach 0-300 m, where Iu and GF increase with distance inland (PDF pp. 20-22 / journal pp. 148-150, verified in original text by Lead); also includes rough terrain → open terrain 0-2.5 km reaching equilibrium around ≥1 km, which is in the opposite direction and not transferable.
 - Increment of this topic: using multi-station ASOS to cover sea→land 0.2-5 km and directly comparing against code transition rules.
 - Still missing Schroeder & Smith 2003 (original text on unmounted drive), ESDU 82026, Wieringa 1992, and Cook 1985.
4. Re-verify GF after stratifying by wind speed and filtering out convective gusts.
5. Risk of two-station special cases: both SPG and NEW are small airports jutting into the water; draw no conclusions before expanding the sample.

# L31.1a Observed Features of Landfalling Typhoon Boundary Layers (Active)

This sub-project derives 10 m turbulence intensity (TI) and spectra below 0.5 Hz from local tower records of 13 storms, binned by upwind land distance. The PI approved the start-up plan on 2026-10-26; the Lead agent fixed pre-registered criteria before any results, and a worker agent ran the analysis on a workstation with no supercomputer time. Of 2587 valid 10-minute windows, 2270 passed the stationarity test. The same-tower nearshore versus offshore TI comparison was undecidable (3 tower deployments, 2 storms, interval spanning 0). Across towers, TI was 0.126 within 0.18 km of water and 0.194 beyond 5 km, a description only. Nearshore integral scale was about 0.65–0.68 times offshore, which formally meets the frozen criterion but is treated as a weak lead, with post hoc fitting bands and only 2–3 storms. Limits: no tower-wake removal, distance from a 2021 land-cover proxy, and 1 Hz sampling biasing TI low; no causal or design-load interpretation.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: The PI approved the plan; criteria fixed and analysis assigned to a worker agent.

# L31.1b Idealized Land-Surface Simulation and Data Assimilation (Active)

L31.1b, part of the landfalling-typhoon inner boundary layer work, tests whether refining the CM1 large-eddy simulation grid from 20 m to 10 m gives enough resolved turbulence near the ground to explain observed gust factors. The run starts from the 20 m production field at 14400 s, interpolated onto the finer grid. The PI approved the start-up plan on 2026-10-26: short tests of at most 50 SU within two weeks, production (about 180 SU) to go to review and then back to the PI, and data assimilation to be written as a plan only. Before any 10 m results, the Lead agent fixed three outcomes for the first short test, based on a resolved-turbulence fraction of 0.80 at 10 m and 30 m: "likely to pass", "fail" or "no verdict". Production convergence was provisionally defined as gust factors at 10 m and 20 m grids differing by no more than 0.02. After three failed setup attempts, the fourth attempt ran a 600-second test (0 SU). At 10 m height the resolved fraction was 0.50 to 0.69, below the threshold, and some sites were still rising, so it was recorded as "not stationary, no verdict" (alternative reading: "fail"). A 1800-second extension was running at the last update.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: The PI approved the plan. The Lead agent froze the design and criteria and dispatched the first test to a worker agent on a single cluster node, with an output cap of 20 GB because group storage was below 600 GB.
- **2026-10-26**: Attempt T1 stopped at the interpolation self-check (1.95% mean-wind difference at 10 m against a 1% limit). After a near-ground fix, T1b failed at 30 m (1.25%). The Lead agent judged this mostly an artifact of linear back-interpolation and switched wind interpolation to log-height. This was recorded as a post-hoc amendment, with the original reading kept alongside.
- **2026-10-26**: T1c passed the check (at most 0.44%; the original linear reading gave 2.1% and 2.7% at 10 m) but stopped because a land-use table file was missing. T1d added the missing file and started integrating.
- **2026-10-27**: T1d completed 600 model seconds: about 72 s wall-clock per model second, timestep about 0.24 s, memory about 39 GB. Extrapolated production cost was about 108 cluster node-hours. Resolved fractions were 0.78 to 0.83 at 30 m (3 of 5 sites passed) and 0.84 to 0.89 at 50 m (all passed). One required output frame was missing.
- **2026-10-27**: The Lead agent extended the run to 1800 s (about 36 node-hours, 0 SU), with criteria fixed in advance. If it is stable but still fails, the result will be reported to the PI as stuck, not extended again.
- **2026-10-27**: T1e stopped because its storage check did not work on compute nodes. T1f was blocked when a combined preflight-and-submit command left a false submission record. After the platform cleared the record, T1f started at 11:10, and a planned duplicate run was cancelled.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the start-up plan: short tests of at most 50 SU, production to be reviewed and reported separately, and assimilation as a written plan only.

## Where it stands
T1f was running and expected to finish around the evening of 10-28. If it passes, a production plan goes to three reviewers. If it fails or remains unstable, the Lead agent will file a stuck report for the PI. Failed run directories are to be cleaned from 11-03 under the standing authorization.

# L31.1c Complex Land Surfaces and Scale Coupling (Active)

This sub-project of L31.1 (internal boundary layer of landfalling typhoons) links the PI's earlier typhoon-scale land-sea roughness-contrast model (chapter 9 of his dissertation, published in JWEIA 2026; 2 km grid) to local internal-boundary-layer estimates 0.2–5 km inland, using zero-compute engineering models compared with the line's LES. Criteria were fixed before results and are based on the line's own data, without literature basis: a land/sea mean-wind-ratio difference of 0.02 or more between two inflow choices counts as substantial, and engineering model versus LES within 0.03 counts as compatible. A first run with an upstream profile read from a paper figure found differences below 0.02 at all 30 grid points, but only for that profile and an assumed 20° angle. The PI's final-version paper cases could not be found on his desktop; an older 2024-01 run was retrieved instead. Using its Case001 (Vmax 25, B 0.6, not a paper case, flow validation only), the model's real sea-side profile changed the land/sea ratio by up to about 0.06–0.10, so the earlier "small effect" finding does not generalize. Agreement with LES depends strongly on which internal-boundary-layer height definition is used. No result is a design-load conclusion.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: Plan approved by the PI; work started at zero compute. A worker agent was assigned upstream conditions, a method comparison table, a zero-compute linkage case and a parameter-source table.
- **2026-10-26**: First linkage result: all 30 points below 0.02 under the figure-read profile and 20° angle, but some points exceed it at 40° or with ±2 m/s reading error. Engineering model versus LES: 13–14 of 30 compatible with the preset Deaves definition, 24 of 30 with the Elliott definition added after the fact.
- **2026-10-26**: The first request for the PI's model files was interrupted by a service restart and resent. Code, the chapter and older 2024-01 results were retrieved; the final paper-case results were not found anywhere on the desktop.
- **2026-10-26**: Flow validation on Case001: 12 of 30 points (Deaves) and 21 of 30 (Elliott) differ by 0.02 or more; 18 and 14 points respectively are within 0.03 of LES. The coastline node choice was ambiguous, so this is a demonstration only.
- **2026-10-26**: The Lead agent asked L31.1 to release a single-node rerun of the paper's Case1 at 9 coastline positions (1 benchmark case of at most 4 hours, then all 9 within 24 hours), to be checked first against the paper's figures and table.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the startup plan, with zero compute for this two-week phase.

## Where it stands
Waiting for L31.1 to release the paper-case rerun; once run, results must reproduce the published figures before linkage continues. The Lead agent noted that if the PI remembers where the 2026-06 revision figures were computed, the rerun could be avoided.

# L31.1e Sea-to-Land Transition Clauses in Wind Codes (Active)

This sub-project of L31.1 (landfalling typhoon internal boundary layer) checks, against the original code texts, how wind codes treat the transition from sea to land roughness, and maps each clause to what the line's observations and simulations can and cannot test. A worker agent extracted clauses with separate PDF and printed page numbers and built a comparison table; version 1 covered 33 clauses, 23 checked against the original text. Key findings: the claim that ASCE 7 "always" assigns Exposure D on hurricane coasts from 7-10 onward does not hold, since D requires an upwind water fetch above max(5000 ft, 20h) and a site within max(600 ft, 20h) of the shore; Eurocode Annex A.2 gives a 2 km / 1 km rule but only as an informative recommended procedure; and some codes do treat mean wind and gusts or turbulence separately. Several codes (AS/NZS 1170.2:2021, IEC 61400-1 4th edition, AIJ 2015, the adopted AASHTO version) were not available anywhere in the center and remain marked "original not checked". Version 2 was accepted as the two-week stage deliverable; its five improvement ideas are research suggestions only, not design values.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: Startup plan approved by the PI; work started at zero compute cost.
- **2026-10-26**: Table v1 delivered; the Lead agent spot-checked page numbers and corrected the line's own earlier ASCE 7-22 page reference.
- **2026-10-26**: The design-load line supplied ASCE 7-16 and EN 1991-1-4; table v2 was commissioned and then accepted, with ASCE 7 evolution, Eurocode Annex A.2, AASHTO (draft only) and two scanned figures rechecked.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the startup plan, whose stop-loss rule is that codes missing locally are not downloaded from publishers but marked as unchecked.

## Where it stands
Table v2 is final and reported to L31.1, readable by L31.5. Quantitative tests of the code transition rules wait for turbulence and gust results from L31.1a and L31.1b; no new work is assigned until then.

# L31.2 台风微气象特征对风工程的影响（课题 2）

## 开题卡（10-16 v1，未做研究）
**核心科学问题**：雨带、边界层滚涡（roll vortices）、mesovortices、台风诱发雷暴和龙卷，这些是公里级和百米级的结构。现行风工程把台风风场当作"平均风场加平稳湍流"，用 10 分钟平均风、阵风因子和谱来描述。这些结构在多大程度上改变工程关心的量？包括：极值阵风及其持续时间、风速竖向廓线（低空急流、负切变）、空间相关性、非平稳性、风向突变。哪一种结构对哪一类结构（低矮房屋/围护、高层、桥梁、输电线）最要紧？

**现有认识与空白**
- 库内有：飓风阵风因子的局限讨论；季风、雷暴与台风阵风因子对比；登陆阵风因子 p.7–10（按径向位置分组）；雷暴阵风锋雷达观测 （非台风）。
- 10-16 补卡（litwiki，前缀，页码见各卡）。
 - 滚涡观测与理论：滚涡普遍存在的观测证据 `H8P6WYI8_*`；为何滚涡普遍 `YLYWIEGS_*`；内流产生滚涡 `KXQKKJRC_*`；滚涡对湍流通量的影响 `5K8YNM2C_*`；滚涡雷达观测 Wurman & Winslow 1998 `IVIK7T2W_*`（**仅摘要**）。
 - LES：台风边界层湍流模拟与参数化 `5CSTHEFP_*`；飓风滚涡 LES `IXGCAWJU_*`；用 LES 定义谱 `9EQGPXLZ_*`；Ito 2017 近地相干结构 `Z9SNS4GV_*`；Worsnop 2017 阵风与切变 `CY2GGGNN_*`（期刊 p.6413–6415）。
 - mesovortex 与龙卷尺度涡：小尺度涡增强地面风 `4R8BQWPX_*`；龙卷尺度涡普遍存在 `VFAW4KKB_*`（PNAS 2018）；Stern & Bryan 2018 模拟下投探空 `HN4Z6G5P_*`（期刊 p.3901–3910）。
 - 台风龙卷：Edwards 2012 综述 `FS8WW5GV_*`（现有副本正文只有 33 页）。
- 空白（初判，待精读核实）：气象界对滚涡和小尺度涡已有观测和 LES（如上），Worsnop 2017 已开始把 LES 转成阵风和切变量。但系统地给出工程参数（持续时间、空间尺度、发生概率）并接到规范阵风因子和廓线，仍缺。精读后修订本条。

**切入点与可用数据/工具**（只读引用）
- HRD 下投探空 7,524 条：。可以看单条廓线偏离平均廓线的统计，以及低空急流和负切变出现的频率。
- CM1 对流/下击暴流 LES 能力和运行根（Moore 2024 40 例等）：（CRC）。可以改做半理想化台风边界层 LES。
- CM1 31 m LES"模拟塔"取 3 s 阵风的方法：。
- 雷达与 Mesonet 事件流水线（雷暴，非台风）：。
- 平台上**没有**台风 LES、台风雷达档案和台风龙卷数据集，这是本课题起点最低的地方。

**第一步最小实验**（0 SU）
- (a) 现象 → 工程量对照表：每种现象列出典型尺度、持续时间、风速增量、发生位置和频率，以及影响哪个工程量、现行规范是否覆盖。依据全部来自补来的卡片，带页码。
- (b) 下投探空诊断：统计单条廓线的低空急流高度、负切变比例和廓线离散度，按 RMW 径向位置和强度分组。判断"用平均廓线设计"会漏掉多少。
- 判据：如果某种现象造成的阵风或廓线偏差超过规范阵风因子或廓线不确定带，且发生概率不可忽略，列为第二步算例对象。第二步是 CM1 半理想化台风边界层 LES，研究滚涡和 mesovortex 产生的阵风；需 Liang Hu 定先后，开算前送审。

**预计工作量**：第一步约 8 人-日、0 SU。第二步 LES 约 20 人-日，CRC 单节点 1–2 周或 TACC 约 500–1500 SU（估计，以短测为准）。

**参数/文献来源**
| 参数 | 取值 | 查过 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 各现象尺度/持续时间 | 待定 | 已有卡 |
| LES 网格/域 | 基线 5.12×5.12×2.98 km、128³、dx 40 m；细网格候选 20 m（假设） | 见 参数来源表 |

**和别的项目的边界**：雷暴与下击暴流在 PETW SP2 CM1 线；本课题只做台风内部的微气象。台风龙卷的统计如果需要事件库，向 SP1 事件线提跨线请求。

## 当前状态
- **10-25 L31.4a4 对齐**：v0 已交。缺项已派 L31.2b（11-06 前交）；雨带下沉部分由 L31.2f 文献图谱补。10-25 v1 已 --report 总控；**v2 已于 10-25 提前交**：TSV/MV 同定义静压降与风向变化率查不到（给 4 个替代量）；雨带阵风锋爬升时间与出流峰高 13 篇全文均无，确认文献空白。10-25 晚并入 L31.2b 补充 v2（Isabel 20° 空间偏转、He 2016 急流高度）；L31.2b 把 Rammasun 写成'作者归因于 TSV'，Lead 核 Feng 2021 PDF p.2–3 原文为'may be…hard to know'，已发进 L31.2b 更正。再并入 Hugo EVM 450 m 飞行层 6 s/0.5 km 内转 45°、82→25 m/s（Marks 2008 PDF p.4，Lead 核原文）。
- **10-25 Liang Hu 要求重划子项目**（原话见）：草案 待 Liang Hu 定；文献补课已启动（10 个现象 Grok 快查）。
- **最新报告（10-25）**：。TCHAT B 档已训完 5 万步，2025 测试评估在跑；B 档上限追认为 33 CU。
- **10-22 口径更正**：数据包 RMW 单位疑为海里，r/RMW 分组被放大约 1.85 倍。原"强台风 r/RMW 1.25–4 外核急流/负切变"改读为"**强台风距中心约 15–60 km（眼墙及其外侧）**"：负切变 40–48%，急流鼻 22–33%；60 km 外降到 18%/2%。主口径改为绝对距离。见。
**10-22 引文滚雪球**：池 （1936，初筛 1069，只由滚雪球 492）。筛出 6 篇建卡（清单第 6–11 号），其中两篇专做台风边界层 LES 对水平分辨率的敏感性（2021、2023），与本线「条带波长随网格缩小、不收敛」直接相关，也关系 10 m 网格（TACC ≥200 SU）是否值得；暂不改结论，卡回后对照。
> 10-22 卡回（索引）：两篇全文与本线 LES 现象一致——Liu 等 2023（卡 06_L31_2，300→20 m 五档网格，12×12 km 域）：100 m 与 20 m 的总动量通量、总 TKE 差一般 <20%，但滚涡形态与局地极值未收敛（PDF pp.11、13）；2021 文（卡 07_L31_2）：166→55 m 时滚涡波长由 >2000 m 缩到约 800–1200 m（PDF p.9），作者明言是分辨率敏感、不是收敛（PDF p.15）。对本线：「阵风因子对网格不敏感、条带波长随网格缩小」与文献同型；文献到 20 m 仍未见滚涡收敛，10 m 网格方案（TACC ≥200 SU，待 Liang Hu）立项时须写明这一先例，不能预期 10 m 就收敛。
> 10-22 全文核：Liu 2021（111→37 m 最大近地风变化有限，未分析滚涡波长）、Chen 2021（O(10) m 判据针对亚格点湍能占比）都不能当滚涡波长或阵风收敛的证据；本线判断不变。

在做。10-19 LES 第一阶段（40 m、20 m、5.12/10.24 km 共 4 个 6 h 算例）完成，Lead 小结：
- **稳健**：近地 3 s/10 min 阵风因子对网格和域长都不敏感（10 m 约 1.25–1.26，90 m 约 1.15–1.16）。

- **未回答**：滚涡是否出现、阵风是否集中在高速条带。
- 再往下需要 10 m 网格（约为 20 m 的 8 倍，CRC 单节点约 6 天，只能上 TACC 多节点，估计 ≥200 SU），属于大计算，**按 Liang Hu 定的"不开大计算"停在这里**，已 --report 总控请 Liang Hu 定。期间不再提交 LES 作业。

## 子项目

# L31.2 Wind Structures Associated with Typhoons and Hurricanes: From Meteorology to Wind Engineering (Exploring)

Project L31.2 investigates how typhoon and hurricane wind structures affect gusts, duration, profiles, and structural loads. The team built a phenomenon-to-engineering mapping table from 17 literature cards, diagnosed 7,524 dropsonde profiles from 116 storms, ran four 6 h idealized CM1 boundary-layer large-eddy simulations (LES) across 5.12 km and 10.24 km domains at 40 m and 20 m grids, tested AI wind reconstruction in L31.2a, and reorganized L31.2 into phenomenon-specific sub-projects (L31.2a-L31.2i). After 50 m smoothing and regrouping by absolute radius (after a suspected radius-of-maximum-wind unit issue), significant negative shear and low-level jet noses occurred in 40%-48% and 22%-33% of profiles at 15-60 km in intense storms (>=50 m/s), versus 18% and 2% at 60-120 km. In the single 40 km outer-core CM1 LES setup (no eyewall updrafts), 3 s/10 min gust factors remained stable (medians 1.25-1.26 at 10 m and 1.15-1.16 at 90 m), whereas 90 m streak wavelengths (1.68 km at 40 m vs. 0.88 km at 20 m) and cross-wind correlation scales (68 m vs. 41 m) were grid-dependent and unvalidated. In L31.2a, ERA5 underestimated peak winds relative to (assimilated) dropsondes by 27-39 m/s at 15-60 km in intense storms, a four-storm physics-constrained reconstruction test was inconclusive, and a 47,500-step shortened TCHAT model was inconclusive on the 2025 set (median peak bias -2.5 m/s vs. about -6.2 m/s for ERA5, tied strong-wind area errors of 1.0, and 24-27 m/s underestimation at 0-30 km); L31.2b is approved and active, while startup plans for L31.2c-L31.2i await PI approval.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16**: Sub-project L31.2 opened after PI approval; the Lead agent dispatched the 17-card mapping table, 7,524-profile diagnosis, and CM1 LES scoping.
- **2026-10-17**: Dropsonde smoothing (50 m) and ASCE 7-22 Exposure D comparisons highlighted intense-storm jets and negative shear, and the first 6 h CM1 LES (40 m grid, 5.12 km domain) completed.
- **2026-10-18**: Expanding the 40 m CM1 LES domain to 10.24 km preserved 10 m gust factor medians (1.25 vs. 1.26) but shifted 90 m wavelengths from 1.68 km to 2.08 km.
- **2026-10-19**: Refining the 5.12 km CM1 LES to a 20 m grid confirmed stable gust factors (1.255 at 10 m) but grid-dependent wavelengths (0.88 km at 90 m); the PI issued a pause order and approved a near-surface wind topic with R23.3.
- **2026-10-21**: Following PI approval, the Lead agent opened L31.2a for AI wind reconstruction and downscaling.
- **2026-10-22**: L31.2a found 27-39 m/s peak wind underestimation in ERA5 for intense storms; after a suspected radius unit issue, the Lead agent regrouped dropsonde results by absolute distance (high-incidence zone 15-60 km).
- **2026-10-25**: The PI reviewed a progress report and directed restructuring into phenomenon-specific sub-projects; the Lead agent opened L31.2b and answered requests from L31.4a4 and L31.8e; that evening the 47,500-step TCHAT test was judged inconclusive.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2a closed shortened TCHAT testing after two cloud CPU evaluation reruns of the 50,000-step weights were stopped by slow data download, and the Lead agent opened L31.2c-L31.2i.

## What the PI decided
- Approved baseline work without large computations (2026-10-16), paused unapproved work and accepted that a probabilistic AI weather model suits track and strong-wind extent but not design peak winds (2026-10-19), and authorized L31.2a to plan then execute (2026-10-21).
- Grouped eyewall/outer-eyewall jets, negative shear, near-surface gusts, and mesovortices into L31.2b, and assigned rolls, tornadoes, tornado-scale vortices, thunderstorms, rainbands, eyewall replacement, rapid intensification, and landfall to a meteorology-to-wind-engineering workflow (2026-10-25).
- Instructed proceeding with restructuring, requesting higher concurrency, and creating L31.2c-L31.2i (2026-10-25 to 2026-10-26).

## Where it stands
Sub-projects L31.2b-L31.2i are open (landfall merged into L31.1); literature maps exist for rolls, tornado-scale vortices, associated tornadoes and landfall, while L31.2f-L31.2i write their own. Startup plans for L31.2c-L31.2i await PI decisions, alongside a proposed R16.4 shared typhoon simulation and full TCHAT retraining. Next, the Lead agent retrieves pending papers one at a time for the sub-projects.

# L31.2a AI Reconstruction and Downscaling of Near-Surface Typhoon Winds (Active)

This sub-project of L31.2 asks whether AI downscaling can recover near-surface tropical cyclone winds that coarse reanalysis misses, using NOAA HRD dropsondes as the reference. Experiment E1 compared ERA5 with 7,524 dropsondes from 116 storms: at 100 m the overall median bias was small, but in intense storms ERA5 was far too weak 15 to 60 km from the center (median bias −27 to −39 m/s). All comparisons are against assimilated observations, not independent validation. E2 tested a lightweight "interpolation plus physical constraint" reconstruction against HAFS analyses used as model truth; its primary reading was not decidable and the configuration was stopped under a pre-set stop rule, not as a negative result. A shortened retraining of the TCHAT network with HAFS as target (option B) was tested on 2025 storms: TCHAT reduced the peak-wind bias but tied the baselines on strong-wind area error, so the frozen criterion returned "not decidable". Option B is now closed at the 47,500-step checkpoint; experiment E3 waits for a data application.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-21**: Sub-project opened under L31.2 at the PI's request.
- **2026-10-22**: E1 completed after one failed submission. The Lead agent also found the dataset's radius of maximum wind values implausibly small and switched to grouping by absolute distance; L31.2 agreed.
- **2026-10-22**: A worker agent found full HWind data available only commercially; HAFS analyses are public, so E2 adopted HAFS as "model truth".
- **2026-10-23**: E2 finished on the third submission, after two runs failed on code errors. Real-location reading: not decidable. Alternative synthetic flight-track reading: 0/4 storms better than interpolation on both measures and only 1/4 better on peak error, triggering the stop rule.
- **2026-10-23**: E1b on 71 pairs from 4 storms (10 m, descriptive): median peak bias −2.0 m/s for HAFS versus −22.3 m/s for ERA5. A NOAA report excerpted by a worker agent (not checked by the Lead) states HAFS assimilates dropsondes, so HAFS is used only as a reference ceiling.
- **2026-10-23**: Proxy timing projected original TCHAT retraining at about 189 CU, far over the 30 CU plan limit. The L31.2 Lead agent chose no full retraining for now and approved a 50,000-step shortened run.
- **2026-10-23 to 10-24**: Google Drive authorization was revoked and data building paused until the PI reauthorized on 10-24.
- **2026-10-25**: Training data built (train 1,276, validation 204, test 624). Training reached 25k steps after a one-line fix to the author code. On validation storms Idalia and Milton, median peak bias was −10.73 m/s for TCHAT versus −26.58 m/s for ERA5 bilinear, so training continued. A built-in budget timer stopped it at 49,000 steps (last full checkpoint 47,500).
- **2026-10-25**: 2025 test (11 storms, 116 windows, 584 pairs): peak bias median −2.5 m/s (TCHAT) versus about −5.9 to −6.3 m/s (ERA5 baselines); area error 1.0 for all. Verdict "not decidable". TCHAT still underestimated intense storms near the center (−17.7 m/s at 0 to 15 km, n=55).
- **2026-10-25 to 10-26**: Three attempts to test the true 50k weights gave no result (a missing input file, then a slow CPU, then a slow data server); option B was closed at about 34.3 CU against a 35.3 CU limit set by the L31.2 Lead agent.

## What the PI decided
- Asked for this sub-project to be opened under L31.2 and allowed plans approved that day to proceed without a further approval round.
- Ordered a pause on new literature downloads (10-22), which the sub-project followed.

## Where it stands
Option B is closed with a "not decidable" verdict at 47,500 steps; any claim that TCHAT beats the baselines would first go to a six-reviewer check. Pending: the PI's decision on full retraining and approval of the ensemble data application needed for E3.

# Near-Surface Winds in the Eyewall Region: Low-Level Jets, Negative Shear, Gusts and Mesovortices (Not started)

L31.2b, split from L31.2 (typhoon micrometeorology), studies the low-level jet, near-surface negative shear, near-surface gusts and eyewall mesovortices about 15–60 km from the center of a typhoon or hurricane. The aim is to trace them from meteorological mechanism to engineering wind characteristics and then to effects on typical structures. The work is planned in four parts: b1 jets and negative shear, b2 gusts and non-stationarity, b3 mesovortices, and b4 structural effects. On 2026-10-25 the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan that reuses earlier, read-only results. Dropsondes in strong typhoons showed significant negative shear in 48% of profiles and a jet nose in 33% at 15–30 km from the center, and 40% and 22% at 30–60 km. LES gave a gust factor of about 1.26 at 10 m and 1.15 at 90 m. The plan is still awaiting approval, so the work so far has been literature only. The literature map found that the engineering side is thin, and the claimed gaps were narrowed once more papers had been read.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The sub-project was opened on the PI's instruction. The Lead agent submitted plan v1. It proposes two weeks of dropsonde re-analysis and three extra LES cases, about 8 node-hours with a cap of 20, with the b3 simulation design written but not run.
- **2026-10-25**: For a request from L31.4a4, the Lead agent compiled vortex pressure drops, wind-direction changes and jet heights, all from source pages. The existing CM1 LES has a weak jet at 870–890 m, about 3% above gradient wind. That setup has no eyewall updraft, so its jet strength is not representative of the eyewall region (an inference from the literature, not tested). A pressure drop measured during Typhoon Rammasun was first attributed to a small vortex; this was corrected the same day to "possibly related, cannot be confirmed".
- **2026-10-25**: The WRF line said a full-physics typhoon nested down to LES is technically feasible but must be built from scratch. Its cost is extrapolated, not measured, at roughly 10² to 10³ SU and needs a 30-minute short test first. The Lead agent proposed Harvey 2017 as the event.
- **2026-10-25**: In a Gemini web search report, about half of the specific numbers did not match the original papers when checked. The report was used only to find leads.
- **2026-10-25**: Literature cards were built: 46 of 47 core papers have full-text cards. Literature map v1 was written by the Lead agent itself.
- **2026-10-25**: The v1 claim that no one had computed building loads under jet profiles was retracted. Huang 2026, a rigid 180 m CAARC wind tunnel model under a jet-like inflow, reported a drag coefficient rising from 1.244 to 1.427 (+14.7%) when both cases are normalized by roof-height wind speed; the authors note the comparison may reverse with 10 m normalization, and only rigid-model pressures were measured. Map v2 narrows the structural gap to flexible response, jet peaks in the upper part of the building or above the roof, combined effects, and low-rise buildings and bridges.

## What the PI decided
- On 2026-10-25, combined the eyewall jet, negative shear and gust work with mesovortices into one sub-project, which may be split further later.
- Endorsed the method: simulation, then combination with observations or reanalysis, then wind characteristics, then structural effects. The PI also said the literature coverage was "very insufficient" and asked the Lead agent to continue.

## Where it stands
The literature phase is finished: 68 papers have cards, 65 of them full-text. Four items are pending the PI: approval of the plan, high-rise buildings and wind turbines as the first structures for b4, deferring any split of b1–b4, and whether to ask the WRF line to open a sub-project for a shared simulation case.

# L31.2c Boundary-Layer Rolls in Tropical Cyclones (Exploring)

Reported roll spacings range from 0.3 km to 2.4 km across platforms and heights, and wind engineering has not studied rolls as a separate load source. In the line's own CM1 large-eddy simulations, near-ground gust factors were robust to grid (about 1.26 at 10 m, about 1.15 at 90 m), but streak spacing at 90 m changed from 1.68 km on the 40 m grid to 0.88 km on the 20 m grid, so it has not converged. On 2026-10-26 the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan that does not refine the grid yet; no new computation has been run. It plans to reanalyse existing output for frequency-dependent cross-wind coherence as a candidate grid-independent engineering quantity, and to compare roll spacing at the same height across radar, mobile radar, SAR and simulation for one of three hurricanes.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable, ruled out a 10 m grid for now (TACC, at least 200 SU), and set long-span bridges plus transmission lines as structures.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons, each through the full procedure.

## Where it stands
Only plan approval by the PI remains (up to 8 CRC node-hours over two weeks). The grid question will be reported again after the reanalysis, in about two weeks.

# L31.2d Tornado-Scale Vortices in Tropical Cyclones (Exploring)

The sub-project studies sub-kilometre tornado-scale vortices (TSV) at the inner eyewall of typhoons and hurricanes, and the short extreme gusts, wind direction shifts and static pressure drops they cause near the ground; independent tornadoes are out of scope. On 2026-10-26 the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan; no computation has been run. Planned first steps, with no supercomputer or Colab time: fix criteria, then a kinematic model of a translating vortex tested for consistency with the Harvey 2017 observations (a 9 s enhancement and a gust factor of about 1.7), which is a consistency check, not independent validation; and a metadata-only inventory of five observation datasets. The Lead agent checked that Harvey is not among the 13 storms in the local tower data, and that one dropsonde product cannot identify TSV hits.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon, from literature and mechanism to effects on typical structures.
- **2026-10-26**: Sub-project opened as plan-only; start-up plan written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable and chose transmission towers and lines as the second structure type, shared with L31.2c.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons, each through the full procedure; scarce literature often signals an opportunity.

## Where it stands
Awaiting the PI on plan approval, the shared full-physics typhoon to LES simulation base, and contacting authors for data.

# L31.2e Tornadoes Accompanying Tropical Cyclones (Exploring)

The question is whether tornadoes that accompany typhoons and hurricanes differ from inland tornadoes, in ways worth treating separately in engineering, on the quantities used by ASCE 7-22 Chapter 32. On 2026-10-26 the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan; no computation has been run. While writing it, it found that a 1991 composite sounding for tropical-cyclone tornado environments gives CAPE of about 253 J/kg versus 2542 J/kg for Great Plains supercells, and 0–1 km shear of 14.8 m/s versus 9.0 m/s. A keyword search of Chapter 32 found no separate treatment of tropical-cyclone tornadoes, which still needs a full reading. The plan defines "different", "negligible" and "no verdict" before any run, resamples by whole storm, and returns "no verdict" below 30 effective storms.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable and ruled that idealised CM1 runs stay in this sub-project, with a separate experiment plan and short test first.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons, each through the full procedure from literature to structural effects.

## Where it stands
Awaiting the PI's approval of the two-week part (up to 2 CRC node-hours or 0.5 CU): tornado database statistics against hurricane tracks and ERA5 background winds. Low-rise houses and transmission towers are the proposed structures.

# L31.2f Thunderstorms and Convective Downdrafts in Tropical Cyclones (Exploring)

The sub-project studies convective downdrafts and outflows embedded in typhoons and hurricanes and their near-ground wind. On 2026-10-26 the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan and literature map v1 (not reviewed); no computation has been run. The map finds meteorological knowledge mainly from airborne radar or smoothed surface data, while the wind-engineering side is thin: mean gust factors are 1.52 in both stratiform and convective regions, and none of the 16 full-text papers read gives near-ground wind rise time or outflow peak height. Unsourced figures from a quick search are marked as not to be used. The planned first step matches convective rainband passages in tower records (13 hurricanes, 40 tower deployments, 1 Hz) with radar reflectivity, stopping if fewer than 10 events can be judged. Because the towers measured wind only, results can say "rainband passage", not "caused by downdrafts".

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan and literature map v1 written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable, chose low-rise houses plus transmission lines, and assigned the shared tower-radar matching table to this sub-project.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons, each through the full procedure.

## Where it stands
Awaiting the PI's approval (up to 5 CRC node-hours and 30 GB temporary storage over two weeks).

# L31.2g Spiral Rainbands (Exploring)

The sub-project asks whether near-ground wind during rainband passage differs from wind between rainbands, how wind profiles differ inside and outside bands, how often and how long a site is swept by bands in one storm, and what this means for structures. Its starting point is a 2016 study where gust factors were about 1.52 for all precipitation types, while about 75% of segments rejected as non-stationary lay near outer rainbands; the Lead agent's view, not yet reviewed, is that the difference may lie in non-stationarity. On 2026-10-26 it wrote a start-up plan; no computation has been run. The two-week plan uses local tower records from 13 hurricanes and dropsondes, and stops at description with fewer than 20 identifiable passages.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable, chose low-rise roofs plus wind turbines, and moved radar matching to a shared table produced by L31.2f.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons, each through the full procedure.

## Where it stands
Only the PI's approval of the plan remains. About 17 journal papers are still to be retrieved, and simulation depends on a shared modeling base not yet decided.

# L31.2h Eyewall Replacement (Exploring)

The sub-project asks how eyewall replacement cycles, well studied in meteorology but generally not treated in codes or engineering typhoon wind models, change wind loads. The literature it cites reports, over 24 replacements, an average duration of about 36 hours, hurricane-force wind radius at flight level growing from 94 km to over 150 km, and a 28% rise in total kinetic energy; none of the 15 full-text cards gives near-ground gust factors, spectra, coherence or structural response. A quoted gust factor of 1.45–1.75 from a quick search has no traceable source and is barred. On 2026-10-26 the Lead agent wrote a start-up plan; no computation has been run. The plan uses local dropsonde profiles (for example 205 for Rita 2005) and a parametric double-eyewall wind field, returning "no verdict" with fewer than 30 profiles or 3 storms.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable, set the order exposure, profile, gust, and chose curtain-wall glass as the first structure.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons; scarce literature often signals an opportunity.

## Where it stands
Awaiting the PI's approval of the plan (0 SU for two weeks). Six journal papers remain to be retrieved.

projects.title: L31.2i Rapid Intensification
projects.digest:
# L31.2i Rapid Intensification (Exploring)

The sub-project asks how the near-ground wind field changes during rapid intensification (RI) of typhoons and hurricanes. The Lead agent read about 25 full-text cards: the meteorological literature agrees on inner-core changes such as rapid contraction of the radius of maximum wind and supergradient wind up to about 2 km, but no card gives pressures, loads or structural response, and the only near-ground RI record is one station with a gust factor of 2.1 and a wind-direction shift of about 30°. On 2026-10-26 it wrote a start-up plan; no computation has been run. Planned steps: label 7,524 existing dropsondes as RI or steady stage and compare profiles at equal intensity and radius (0 SU), and small axisymmetric CM1 idealised runs (up to 6 CRC node-hours). The Lead agent left tower data out of the near-term plan because the towers in the typical pre-landfall RI case were not on the eyewall path.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI set a common procedure for each typhoon-related phenomenon.
- **2026-10-26**: Start-up plan written and reported to L31.2.
- **2026-10-26**: L31.2 reviewed the plan as approvable and chose offshore wind turbines plus low-rise building envelopes.
- **2026-10-27**: Two more papers read; neither gives near-ground or 10 m wind or engineering quantities.

## What the PI decided
- Study only phenomena that accompany typhoons, each through the full procedure.

## Where it stands
Awaiting the PI's approval of the plan.

projects.title: L31.3 Equivalence of inflow generation methods
projects.report:
# L31.3 入流生成方法等效性与适用性（课题 3）

## 开题卡（10-16 v1，未做研究）
**核心科学问题**：CFD 入流生成方法很多，包括前驱/回收（precursor/recycling）、合成湍流（SEM/DFSEM、DFM、DSRFG、CDRFG、NSRFG、DFSR 等）、LBM 体力注入。当它们给出同样的目标统计量（平均风廓线、湍流度、积分尺度、谱、相干）时，作用在建筑上的风压是否等价？"等价"要匹配到哪几阶统计量才够：只要一点统计就行，还是必须匹配两点相干、相位结构、散度和压力脉动？哪种方法在什么条件下（网格、雷诺数、域长、求解器）会失真？

**现有认识与空白**
- 库内有：DSRFG 原文（满足散度为零、可处理各向异性） p.1, 7, 14；谱方法合成湍流的系统化改进，指出不同入流会在入口产生显著的虚假压力脉动 p.6, 9, 22；平衡边界层合成湍流；壁湍流合成入流；结构风工程 LES 入流方法中文综述 p.1；LBM 合成湍流生成器 PDF p.3, 6, 14。
- 10-17 补卡（litwiki，索引；我抽查了 Yan & Li、Yu 等两张卡）：
 - Yan & Li 2015：同一 CAARC 上 RFG、VM、DSRFG、recycling 四类入口比到 Cp 均值与 rms，未报峰值；每工况只统计 10 s 模型时长（EFV5P3MS，PDF pp. 6, 11–14 / 期刊 pp. 163, 168–171）。
 - Yu, Yang & Xie 2018（NSRFG 原文）：同 CAARC 比 NSRFG 与 CDRFG 的 Cp 均值/rms 与底矩，同属 RFG 族；LES 只分析 20 s（YF9ABFIY，PDF pp. 7, 9–11 / 期刊 pp. 306, 308–310）。
 - CDRFG 原文（Aboshosha 2015）同楼对照的是底矩谱与响应，不是表面 Cp（YY8AZK4Z，PDF pp. 10–11, 14 / 期刊 pp. 207–208, 211）。
 - Zhang 2022（IRCDRFG vs CDRFG，6EK4MSBA）、Deng 2023（MNSRFG vs NSRFG）同族升级，只比均值/rms；Mansouri 2022 学位论文跨族筛选，只有 SEM-G 做了峰值。
 - 文献库未找到"2015 年后、跨方法族、同一建筑、均值/rms/峰值三量都对照"的完整原文（Waleson 2026 未取得全文）。
- 空白（初判，补卡后加强，仍待综述核实）：大多数方法论文只在自己的算例上与目标统计比较，跨方法、同一基准、一直比到建筑风压峰值的系统比较很少；也没有一套公认的"等价判据"。

**切入点与可用数据/工具**（只读引用，都在别的项目）
- CAARC LES L1（DFSEM，TACC），已诊断多进程 DFSEM 缺陷和入口分区造成的 Iu 亏损 41–47%：；运行根；CAARC DFSR（CRC）；风洞目标数据 TFCA（Zenodo 18702221）。
- Silsoe 空域验收与沿程积分尺度：、。
- LBM 合成入流（FluidX3D 体力区）：、；LBM 前驱域：。
- 平台上**没有** DSRFG/CDRFG/NSRFG 代码，也没有统一的入流比较工具。
- 分工（10-16 已与更好世界对齐）：CFD 入流的等效性和基准由本课题主责；面向结构分析的风速时程随机模拟（SRM/AR/POD/小波/演变谱）的谱系和基准归更好世界 6a；更好世界谱系图里的 CFD 入流一支只读引用本课题结论。合成生成器出口统计检验归本课题；两边比较指标统一口径。

> 10-17 更正（盘点结果，见指标表 v1 第 0 节）：Silsoe 上 OpenFOAM 用数字滤波入口而非 DFSEM，LBM 体力注入是同族 Xie–Castro 数字滤波（非同一实现）；CAARC 尚无尺度解析建筑算例。下面第一步按现有数据改为"CAARC 入口生成保真度 + Silsoe 同生成器不同注入方式"。

**第一步最小实验**（0 SU，只读已有结果）
- 输入：CFD 线和 DWT 已有的空域/建筑算例结果，覆盖 DFSEM（OpenFOAM）、DFSR（OpenFOAM）、LBM 体力注入，目标都是 Silsoe 或 CAARC。
- 输出：统一指标表，分两部分。(1) 入口和沿程各站的 U、Iu、Lu、谱和相干的衰减，以及入口虚假压力脉动；(2) 建筑 Cp 的均值、rms、峰值相对风洞的误差。
- 判据：如果各方法入口统计误差都小于 10%，但建筑 Cp 峰值误差差异超过 20%，就说明"一点统计匹配不够"，课题成立。第二步是自建离线生成器检验（DSRFG/CDRFG/DFSR 同目标，只看生成场，Colab 或 CRC 小作业），然后做受控的同网格三方法建筑算例，开算前送审。

**预计工作量**：第一步约 5 人-日、0 SU。第二步离线检验约 5 人-日、Colab 约 10 计算单元。第三步受控建筑算例，TACC 约 600–1500 SU，需审。

**参数/文献来源**
| 参数 | 取值 | 查过 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CAARC Iu 亏损 | 41–47% | — |
| 生成器最高无量纲频率 | fmax≤H/(4h)，h 为最大网格间距；fmin 取实测下限 | litwiki 10-22 |
| 等价判据阈值 10%/20% | 假设 | 库内无；补卡委托中 |
| Silsoe 入流目标 U_H/Iu/Iv/Iw | 6 m/s / 0.195/0.15/0.08 | CFD 线设计文件 |
| Silsoe 目标 Lu/Lv/Lw | 16.4/6.24/6.24 m | CFD 线设计文件 |
| CAARC 入流目标 | C05 Cobra 探针 8 高度全应力张量与 Lux/Lvx/Lwx | CFD 线 |
| 峰值估计器 | epochal 10 段、BLUE 拟合 Gumbel、段长 T/10 的 78% 分位（μ+1.3925β） | litwiki 10-17 补卡 |
| 谱估计器、相干拟合、积分尺度算法 | 见口径 v1.1 第 0 节、A4–A6 | — |

## 已定决定
- 2026-10-16 与更好世界 6a 分工 → 
- 2026-10-22 L29.5b Silsoe RANS 对表（只读引用 A4 校准，须按原定义）→ 
- 2026-10-21 与更好世界 L29.5（UQ）边界对齐 → 

- 10-22 M3 DFSEM：原生 BC 种子固定 123456，授权隔离改造仅加 seed 入口，seed=123456 须与原生逐位一致等四条烟测闸门过后才提交 6234/6235/6236 → [决策](../)

# L31.3 Equivalence and Applicability of Inflow Generation Methods (Topic 3)

## Decisions Made
- 2026-10-16 Division of labor with Make the World a Better Place 6a →
- 2026-10-22 Alignment with L29.5b on Silsoe RANS (read-only citation of A4 calibration, must follow original definition) →
- 2026-10-21 Boundary alignment with Make the World a Better Place L29.5 (UQ) →

- 10-22 M3 DFSEM: native BC seed fixed at 123456; authorized isolated modification adds only a seed entry point, and production runs may be submitted only after passing four smoke-test gates including bitwise agreement with the native code at seed=123456 →
## Current Status
**10-22 Citation snowballing (requested by Liang Hu on 10-22)**: pool (406 non-seed papers initially screened), from which the Lead selected 5 papers absent from our library and sent them to LitWiki for card creation. Does not alter the preliminary judgment that "studies comparing across method families on the same building down to peak values are rare" (the newly added cross-family comparison Bazdidi-Tehrani 2016 does not compare peak values; based on abstract, pending card verification). Added one item to the plan: Step 3 building cases will set the maximum frequency of each generator according to the mesh cutoff frequency and check for spurious pressure in an empty domain (Mansouri 2022 abstract states that without truncation, peak pressure errors can exceed 100%, pending card verification). 10-22 Cards returned (index): full text was verified only for Castro 2017 (comparing velocity coherence and base-moment spectra across closely related RFG methods on the same building, without comparing surface Cp, PDF pp.10-14 / journal pp.220-224), while the other 4 papers had abstracts only; whether Bazdidi-Tehrani 2016 reports surface pressures and the setup corresponding to >100% in Mansouri 2022 remained unverified. 10-22 Full texts of two open-access papers verified: Mansouri 2022 (card, full_text_verified): for the TTU building at 90°, h=H/16, fmin=0.1, fmax=10, the error in the roof minimum peak pressure is approx. 100% and the side-wall error is >600% (resolvable upper limit on this mesh is 4, which fmax exceeds), with the error denominator unspecified; the authors recommend fmax≤H/(4h) (where h is maximum grid spacing and dimensionless f=nH/U_H) and setting fmin to the measured lower bound (PDF pp.2, 5-6, 8, 10); spurious pressures appear at the building location in an empty domain, whereas mean Cp is insensitive to fmax and cannot substitute for peak pressure diagnostics. Chen 2022: C-CDRFG amplifies inlet turbulence intensity by the ratio between target and measured locations, with a CAARC inflow fetch of 3H, and the reported "91%" refers to base-moment matching rather than surface Cp (PDF pp.5-6, 11-13). **Step 3 plan addendum**: set the maximum frequency of each generator to fmax≤H/(4h) (per Mansouri 2022 PDF pp.2, 10), and inspect velocity spectra, spurious pressure, and peak pressure at the building location. Bazdidi-Tehrani 2016 and Chen 2024 remain abstract-only.
> 10-22 Full-text verification: Bazdidi-Tehrani 2016 compares flow fields and dispersion only, without reporting surface Cp (card), further supporting the finding that "cross-family studies on the same building comparing down to peak Cp are rare". Chen 2024 (card): under the same synthetic inflow, without pressure correction the four-face average NMAE of surface Cp standard deviation is 108%, dropping to 11.6% with inlet mass correction and 16.3% with divergence correction; the NMAE for mean Cp is <5% in all groups, while for peak Cp it is 12.0% uncorrected and approx. 5-6.7% after correction, showing that spurious pressure from synthetic inflow primarily corrupts fluctuating and peak values rather than the mean, matching the pattern seen in the CFD line's Silsoe DDES ("mean Cp passes, fluctuating Cp fails, high frequencies stronger closer to the inlet") (a lead only, not a conclusion). Added one rule to the Step 3 plan: apply inlet mass correction or divergence correction uniformly across all generators and verify spurious pressure in an empty domain.

**10-21**: Basis v1.3 frozen (review plus supplemental review, 4 reviews total from Gemini and GPT-6, not sent to a third provider and reported to the platform; see ruling at). **Blind retest of xLu passed all 6 cells** (M1e, seeds starting from 2070000, approx. 0.03 CU; actually finished before the first task was interrupted, with criteria verbatim identical to the frozen draft; see correction in the decision log). M1 self-check released (43 carried-over cells + 6 retested cells, not counted as a single complete blind verification pass), **M2 released**, and minimal DFSR trial submitted on cluster with a 2 SU cap: third submission (v3) **completed**: single-seed DFSR mean wind speed error <0.1%, turbulence intensity generally 4-13% low, coherence 1-13% weak, generation cost 77 s per million point-steps. **M3** (pre-registration): statistics across three DFSR seeds and pooled A6 completed (10-21, pooled Ĉ u_y 10.84/10.99/11.02 vs. target 10). No progress on the remaining methods on 10-21; on 10-22 the primary cluster connection dropped, so DFM, CDRFG, NSRFG, DSRFG, and Saad were re-dispatched to Colab using offline Python (cap 20 CU), while DFSEM waited for cluster recovery. GenIC had been mislisted as DFM in plan v0 and was corrected (it is actually SEM). The same batch of 2a data was handed over to R16.7e for blind structural response computation.

**10-22 12:00**: DFM, CDRFG, NSRFG, and DSRFG each completed three seeds on Colab; Saad ran a short smoke test only as a reference. Three issues were identified: (1) several vertical A6 fits for CDRFG and DFM hit the upper bound of 100, meaning near-zero coherence, which serves as a diagnostic flag rather than a physical conclusion; (2) DFSR statistics were evaluated at z=1.70833 whereas the Colab methods were evaluated at z=1.625, creating a location mismatch; (3) the corrected NSRFG run (default1000) was still being collected. A wrap-up task was dispatched to core: recompute at a unified point location, classify A6 boundary hits (inherent method limitation / implementation bug / improper fitting frequency band, citing original page numbers in all cases), and report after finalizing . Total Colab cap 20 CU.

**10-22 afternoon**: M3 wrap-up acceptance. For the five-method comparison at the unified location, see . Single-point statistics (U, I) are very close across methods, with DFM I running 5-10% high; coherence differs substantially, with only DFSR staying within approx. 10% of the target on all three items. Implementation bugs in CDRFG and DSRFG were fixed post-hoc (drawing modal directions independently at each height). NSRFG coherence was an order of magnitude too strong and DSRFG xLu was approx. 4x too large, so core was dispatched to diagnose both (≤4 CU). By evening both diagnoses were complete and attributed to (a), i.e., inherent properties of the parameter mapping under this configuration: measured NSRFG coherence nearly coincided with the theoretical formula because the original parameter c was set directly to Davenport C; random temporal frequencies in DSRFG prevented the autocorrelation from crossing zero, inflating the integral length scale. M3 was complete except for DFSEM. Once the cluster recovered at 10-22 14:18, core was immediately dispatched to run three DFSEM seeds on the cluster within the 50 SU total M3 cap, saving results separately as aligned summary v5. Anomalous turbulence intensity in v5 was traced to (b): the 5 m normal grid thickness of the inlet utility clamped the eddy size. After fixing and saving as v6, I matched the target; overly weak coherence was attributed to (a) due to compactly supported eddies; kurtosis of 6.5 was noted as a remaining gap. **By late 10-22, the M3 descriptive comparison across all six methods was complete**: single-point statistics are largely consistent, whereas spatial coherence is the primary discriminator; each method maps target coherence into its internal parameters differently, which serves as the entry point for 2b. For summary, see .

**10-23**:
- **2a structural read-back**: R16.7e ran an initialization-method regression using our frozen code. Because this was not an independent implementation, it counts as a sensitivity check on initialization rather than an independent blind run. For peak base bending moment from Cz 5→20, r₅=(P20-P5)/P5 is -19.2% under zero initial conditions vs. -20.6% under static-equilibrium initialization; under the r₁₀ basis reported in 2a, the values are -21.4% / -23.1%. The Cz effect on top acceleration RMS emerges only under static initialization, with r₁₀ = -37.1% (-0.3% under zero initial conditions, swamped by startup transients), so acceleration numbers in 2a must switch to static initialization.
- **2b draft v0**: . Defines five equivalence levels E0-E4 evaluated via derived cross-spectral operators and reachable sets. Returned: within the explored parameter domain, NSRFG **found no** calibration simultaneously satisfying 10/10/5 (u_z and w_z vary in the same direction; this does not "prove unreachability"); the 2a static-initialization addendum has been archived.
- **10-24**: The CFD line established that unphysical high-frequency pressure on Silsoe is linked to inlet net mass-flux fluctuations: without projection, the DFSR inlet is 3.1x the baseline, dropping to 0.07-0.08x after net mass-flux projection (under this configuration, not claimed as the sole cause). Recorded in metrics table v3 and the 2b draft as direct evidence for Level E3.
- **10-25**: Wrote progress and plan report covering P1-P7 through the 11-02 two-week summary. Dispatched core (queued): recompute six-method inlet discrete divergence aligned with A9, incorporating Saad's discrete divergence criterion into Level E3. After core encountered unknown_execution twice, the Lead attached a keepalive to recover results for the four Colab methods: D* is 4.8 for DFM, 3.4 for CDRFG, 2.1 for NSRFG, and 1.7 for DSRFG. Even methods claiming divergence-free behavior in the original papers have non-zero divergence on a discrete grid under Taylor's frozen-turbulence hypothesis, though a reference scale is not yet established. See summary at . Dispatched Round 2: compute DFSR and DFSEM on the cluster, and add the gradient ratio R across all six methods (marked as a post-hoc addition).
- **10-25 Five comments from Liang Hu** (verbatim at): insufficient literature; examine formula-level equivalence, input equivalence, and the relationship to stationary Gaussian methods in L29.6a; engineering equivalence (irrotational, divergence-free, wind pressure, wind speed, wind force); fast computation; non-stationary (thunderstorm) inflow and ramp-down phase. Also requested reorganizing into subprojects. Drafted restructured kickoff plan v2 split into L31.3a-e:, pending approval. Prior to approval, work is restricted to literature and theory: Gemini quick search and snowballing have been dispatched, while E3 wrap-up jobs proceed as scheduled.
- **10-26 L31.3d fast computation M-d content complete (reported by subproject)**: cost table v1.4b. Descriptive under the present configuration and hardware, not yet submitted for review: Colab T4 CPU single-threaded E2 (s / 10⁶ point-steps) is 0.119 for NSRFG, 0.610 for CDRFG, 2.67 for DSRFG, and 10.3 for DFM, while GPU is 12-31x faster with pointwise agreement between CDRFG GPU and CPU; modal reduction and 1/4 cyclic replay both trade accuracy for speed (distinguishable in 70-119 of 186 metrics), whereas FFT grid projection and DFM GPU convolution yielded no speedup; on the same cluster node relative to CDRFG: DFSEM is ≤2.2x (upper bound including disk I/O) and DFSR is approx. 69x (including setup). Resource usage: approx. 3.37 CU on Colab and approx. 1.5 core-hours on cluster. Will be submitted jointly for 6-reviewer review before entering synthesis/manuscript.
- **10-25 evening, Literature**:
 - Gemini quick search located 41 of 50 DOIs, with mismatched entries removed.
 - Snowball literature pool reached 4160 papers (truncated); Lead selected 45 papers as Batch 2.
 - Availability: 28 of 36 papers in Batch 1 and 24 of 45 papers in Batch 2 are already available locally.
 - Both batches have been dispatched to litwiki for nine-field formula-level intensive reading cards.
 - Non-stationary thematic snowballing completed: pool of 1241 papers, from which the Lead screened 37 papers as Batch 3 (36 available locally) and dispatched them to litwiki.
 - The three batches total 118 papers, with 88 available locally.
 - **Batch 3 (non-stationary) returned** at 10-25 17:18, completed first by litwiki. The 37 cards verified key pages only rather than page-by-page intensive reading. Summary table: . Preliminary finding: none of the 37 papers provides a non-stationary turbulence field that can be used directly as an LES inlet and has been independently validated against a real thunderstorm ramp-down phase. Algorithmic methods (Li & Kareem, wavelets, Hilbert, time-frequency SRM) are mostly validated against seismic motions or synthetic targets; physical-analog methods (impinging jets, wall jets, LES) generate flow fields inside the computational domain rather than serving directly as inlets, and are validated only up to mean profiles or local metrics. This defines the gap for L31.3e; **Batch 1 (36 papers) returned** (late 10-25): all nine-field cards built, index, review taxonomy and formula comparison, . Lead spot-checked the Smirnov card, which met quality standards; cards remain at "initial verification" rather than page-by-page final sign-off. Batch 2 is proceeding in parallel across three blocks. **r2A method comparison (16 papers) returned** (key-page verification). Reading: controlled studies swapping only the inflow generator on the same building to compare wind pressures or forces are scarce, with only Yan & Li 2015 on CAARC (RFG/VM/DSRFG/recycling) coming close. Most others compare a "new method against wind tunnel", such as NSRFG vs. CDRFG, MNSRFG, and MINSRFG, reporting base-moment RMS errors of 1%-19% relative to wind tunnel; others examine sensitivity to inlet parameters and mesh resolution (Chew 2025, Wong 2026 calibration, Mansouri 2022 mesh cutoff frequency fLES=H/(4h)). This underscores the need for the controlled discrimination experiments in L31.3c. **r2B divergence-free and bridges (16 papers) returned**, directly usable for b:
 - On the structural wind engineering side: Li & Kareem 1993 (DFT plus digital filter), the two 1993 SRM randomization schemes, and the 2004 direct comparison of SRM/AR/ARMA all stop at multi-point time histories without addressing spatial divergence-free conditions
 - On the inflow side: most enforce divergence-free conditions in the continuous sense (orthogonal spectral modes, DFSEM vortex cores, vorton vorticity), whereas discrete divergence-free enforcement appears only in the 2025 WES paper using Hodge-projection post-processing
 - The POD + digital filter and POD + VAR pathways sit squarely between the AR/POD methods of L29.6a and inflow generation.
 - **r2C machine learning and non-stationary methods (13 papers) returned**. All 118 cards across the three batches are now complete, with the index integrated into v2 by the Lead. The two papers closest to the non-stationary gap are:
 - 2026 JFS: jet w(t) configured with a ramp-down phase in a joint LES with ABL, validated against WindEEE wind speeds but not building pressures
 - 2026 Eng Struct: LES of a downburst superposed on an ABL, computing building aerodynamic forces, though ramp-down pressure performance requires separate verification.
 - Both are physical-analog jets rather than synthetic inlets. Non-stationary SEM (2011) modifies only local scales without an event-level U(t). A "non-stationary synthetic inflow directly usable as an LES inlet and validated against a real thunderstorm ramp-down phase" has still not been found.
- **10-25 18:40 E3 six-method divergence complete** (cluster + Colab): the gradient ratio R across five methods lies between 0.53 and 0.61, matching the "three mutually uncorrelated terms" reference value √3/3≈0.577, with no distinction between continuously divergence-free DFSEM and non-divergence-free DFSR; only NSRFG gives 0.41. Reading: the Taylor divergence proxy on the inlet plane lacks discriminative power on a 0.25 m grid, where DFSEM eddies span only 1-2 grid spacings. Divergence evaluation will instead be performed on the CFD solver mesh under L31.3c. See details at . In Batch 2, non-stationary SEM (2011) and the 2026 LES of a downburst superposed on an ABL still need to be examined.
 - **Deep Research quota 90/90 exhausted, not run**, reported to Liang Hu. Fluctuating Cp has still not been delivered, as the CFD line is calibrating the scales generated by DFSR. See decision at .

**10-20 14:3x**: Cluster connection restored. Run in parallel while M1 awaited review: dispatched core to launch the 2a small coherence experiment (C₀=10, from Eq. 18 on PDF p.6 / print p.624, structural design example value; three tiers 5/10/20 × 64 seeds, ≤5 SU), and prepared M2 DFSR (compilation, configuration, experiment card, and pre-check all completed; run root prepared, not to be submitted until M1 passes). Round 1 of 2a aborted before structural response: generator QA code filtered out all frequency bins on distant point pairs at C=10, yielding NaN for the mean; authorized fixing the QA code only (thresholds and criteria unchanged) and resubmitting under run root v2 (reusing the resource request).
