Dispatched on 10-20: M1 statistical script and self-check (core bot, ≤2 SU); broad search for recent literature and code (Grok quick search followed by Deep Research); supplemental cards on Tony Saad's work (litwiki). Quotas for both tiers were exhausted (Grok 402, Deep Research 60/60) and reported to the platform; Lead conducted Round 1 self-search and built cards for matching items (three-family index; every card notes "equivalence with SRM not discussed in original text", with no off-the-shelf derivation of theoretical equivalence in our database). Saad supplemental cards returned (2017 AIAA J, 2016 Comment, 2018 GPU; index), prompting the addition of a "solver-mesh discrete divergence" diagnostic to the offline verification (basis v1.2 candidate). M1: code written, but because the primary cluster connection was down from 10-20 07:25, the full self-check was routed to Colab: **failed under frozen criteria** (σ/I 3.5-4.6% low, two S1 plates flagged, one plate stress at 2.16 SE; xLu/A5/u-coherence/B3 passed); preliminarily attributed to unadjusted generator bandwidth truncation in the self-check ground truth and multiple-testing false alarms. # L31.3b Formula-Level Equivalence of Inflow Generation Methods (Active)

This sub-project of L31.3 asks, at the level of formulas, how synthetic inflow generation methods relate to one another and to the stationary Gaussian methods of L29.6a, and tries to trace each phenomenon seen in the line's M3 batch test to a specific formula term. The Lead agent wrote draft v1 itself, checked by a read-only verification script and original-paper pages; no new wind fields were generated. Draft findings, valid only for this line's inflow configuration: random-wave methods with bounded wavenumber ranges cannot exactly reproduce Davenport coherence, while Cauchy-distributed wavenumbers can; NSRFG gives identical coherence for all three velocity components; the digital filter method has frequency-independent coherence and an actual integral scale of (2/π)L (predicted 0.343 m, M3 measured 0.34 m); DFSEM coherence vanishes beyond a finite separation; and the M3 DSRFG implementation differs from the original equation, so its M3 coherence numbers describe the line's code, not the method. A worker agent's theory check confirmed the DSRFG point and showed that one draft explanation (for CDRFG component differences) was wrong; it was corrected. The draft is unreviewed.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: Draft v1 written; 8 of 14 M3 phenomena mapped to formula terms, 3 partly, 3 unexplained. M3 files left untouched; corrections kept in a side note.
- **2026-10-26**: A worker agent's theory-only calculation confirmed the DSRFG code deviation (theory 4.54 / 12.86 / 6.47 vs. M3 4.52 / 12.84 / 6.28) and corrected the CDRFG explanation; 9 of 14 phenomena now mapped.
- **2026-10-26**: Four new literature cards were read and merged. The DFSR coherence gap of about 7% was reclassified from a code error to a mismatch between the generation reference speed (13.73 m/s, which has a Davenport 1961 source) and the evaluation's two-point mean speed. A divergence-free versus Davenport compatibility point remains a hypothesis.
- **2026-10-26**: A platform reminder asking for a startup plan was judged a false alarm, since the sub-project inherits the L31.3 approval.

## What the PI decided
- Assigned this sub-project mainly to the Lead agent, with a deliverable due 11-02; it inherits the PI's L31.3 approval and shared budget.

## Where it stands
A follow-up on 10-29 is to read two remaining papers and finish the open derivations for draft v2; review by six reviewer models is planned for 10-31 and delivery for 11-02.

# Fast Computation of Synthetic Inflow Generators (Active)

L31.3d is one of five sub-projects of L31.3 (equivalence of inflow generation methods). It asks what each inflow generator costs on uniform hardware and whether accelerated versions (GPU, FFT, pre-generation, fewer modes) change the generated statistics in a distinguishable way, judged with the line's v1.3 criteria. Existing cost figures from an earlier stage were not comparable because they came from different machines, so a worker agent first wrote a pre-registration and ran a smoke test, then timed four Python generators on one Colab T4 machine and two OpenFOAM-native methods on the cluster. In this configuration, GPU versions were 12-31 times faster, and the CDRFG GPU version matched the CPU version point by point; reducing the number of modes gave speed-ups with distinguishable statistical differences, while FFT synthesis and a GPU convolution for DFM were not faster. A point-indexing error found mid-way invalidated one batch of statistics, which were recomputed, and a zero-difference control then showed 0 of 186 comparisons distinguishable. The results are descriptive, for this configuration and hardware only, and have not been sent for review.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-26**: Sub-project started under the approval inherited from L31.3 (Colab budget of at most 5 CU, milestone 11-05). The Lead agent split the work into pre-registration plus smoke test first, full runs after checking.
- **2026-10-26**: Pre-registration and smoke test accepted (about 0.03 CU). Because some generators synthesise a whole block on the first frame, the Lead agent changed timing to a regression of total time on step count (slope = cost per step, intercept = setup).
- **2026-10-26**: First full stage: same-machine cost table for NSRFG, CDRFG, DSRFG and DFM; CDRFG GPU about 30 times faster than CPU; FFT synthesis on GPU 2.6 times slower.
- **2026-10-26**: A worker agent found that sampling points had y and z swapped when arrays were flattened. Affected statistics, including a first zero-difference control, were withdrawn and recomputed. After the fix, CDRFG with 50% / 24% of modes was 1.5 / 2.0 times faster, with 72 / 119 of 186 statistics distinguishable; NSRFG with 500 modes was about 1.17 times faster with 74 distinguishable, and 250 modes was slower.
- **2026-10-26**: A cluster job for the OpenFOAM methods exited without output; the cause was confirmed as a strict-mode shell setting when loading the environment, and the rerun finished normally. DFSEM cost 3.45 (an upper bound, including per-frame text output); DFSR about 107.9 from a single run length including initialisation (about 69 times CDRFG on the same node).
- **2026-10-26**: At the overall project's request, the cost table was annotated: the DSRFG figures come from an earlier implementation that deviates from the original formulation, and DFSR used a constant reference speed in its coherence function.
- **2026-10-26**: The Lead agent issued the milestone cost table early and decided not to measure a per-step DFSR slope or DFSEM cost without output, since the upper bounds already fix the order of magnitude.

## What the PI decided
- The PI set this sub-project's scope (uniform-hardware cost table and statistical comparison of accelerated versions) with a Colab limit of 5 CU and an 11-05 milestone; about 3.37 CU were used.

## Where it stands
The milestone cost table and acceleration conclusions are complete and no jobs are running. Before these results enter the L31.3 synthesis or a paper, they must go through a six-reviewer check, to be scheduled by the overall project.

# L31.3e Non-Stationary Turbulent Inflow

## Objective
Answer Liang Hu's question 5: what numerical algorithms and physical-like methods exist for non-stationary (thunderstorm) turbulence; how do they differ from real non-stationary turbulence; and can they be used as building inflow, especially during the ramp-down phase. Deliverables: method feasibility table, and a pilot test of the first algorithm on the THUNDERR ramp-down phase (M-e, 11-08). Budget: Colab ≤5 CU (L31.3 total ≤10 CU); cross-communicating with L29.6a4.

## Current Status
10-26: L31.3e-06 (StickNet pilot) paused at data retrieval: EOL requires an account or email web order. Placing an order constitutes an external action under Liang Hu's identity and has been reported to the coordinating conversation for Liang Hu's confirmation; proceed per original card once confirmed. New computations paused for the remaining parts.

## Decisions Made
- 10-26 M-e conclusion draft established after review revisions → 
- 10-26 L31.3e-01 judged H1 inconclusive, D1 circular, switched to L31.3e-02 → supplemented in the same decision document
- 10-26 First pilot compares stationary, uniformly modulated, and fully evolutionary spectrum SRMs, evaluating single-point statistics only, coherence not evaluated → 

## Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Sentence Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-26 | Method feasibility table v0 (37+13 cards in library) | Existing non-stationary approaches usable as building LES inflow fall into only two categories: "time-varying mean + stationary turbulence generator" and physical-like methods; no paper in the library isolates the ramp-down phase to compare generation errors against measurements |
| 10-26 | Feasibility table v1 (Grok quick-search verification) | Consistent with v0: no mature method yet varies both turbulence variance and spectrum over time for synthetic inflow, and no work separately evaluates the ramp-down phase (not found, rather than proven nonexistent); added Haines & Taylor 2019, categorized as physical-like (divergence-free synthetic inflow applied at the nozzle, not at a building inflow plane); incomplete DOIs discarded |
| 10-26 | L31.3e-01 Three SRMs on THUNDERR ramp-down phase | Admitted 47/99, test 6 records (4 events). Stationary generator fails to reproduce ramp-down σ(t) (e_σ 0.34-3.46). The 6/6 D1 pass for uniform modulation is due to feeding each record's own σ(t) as input, which is a circular test and not counted as evidence. Low- and mid-frequency band energies are indistinguishable in 4/6; gust peak factor, high-frequency band, skewness, and kurtosis are all 3/6, inconclusive. Median r_T is 0.97, spectral shape in this sample does not vary with time. H1 inconclusive. Colab ~0.01 CU |
| 10-26 | L31.3e-02 σ(t) prediction (non-circular; 20 records, 10 events) | Under three prescriptions, constant σ (P0), pre-peak turbulence intensity of the same record (P1), and training-set turbulence intensity (P2), D1 fails to reproduce at the event level across all three (0/10, 1/10, 0/10), H1′ not established; median e_σ is 0.33/0.29/0.45, while the sampling lower bound given true σ is ~0.05-0.11; record-level gust peak factor is indistinguishable in 16-18/20. ~0.005 CU |
| 10-26 | L31.3e-03 σ envelope model + peak gust (20 records, 10 events) | For power-law β=0.66 and envelope with dū/dt term, event-level D1 is 1/10 for both, H-A not established. When ū(t) is given correctly, event-level error of ramp-down peak gust: constant turbulence intensity 5.5-5.7%, envelope 1.9-2.5%, oracle 1.0%; constant mean + constant σ is −15.9% (two effects not separated). Lead recomputation: in 15/20 records, peak gust occurs in the first 10% of the ramp-down phase, so G1 does not represent the interior of the ramp-down phase |
| 10-26 | L31.3e-04 Leave-one-event-out (47 records, 21 events) | Oracle indistinguishable in 21/21, resolving-power gate passed; P0-P4 are 0, 1, 0, 3, 1/21, Wilson upper bounds 0.155-0.346, all below 2/3, judged "not reproduced with resolving power" (in-sample); D1 cannot detect uniform σ biases within ±10%, but can detect at −20%/+25%; e_σ ratio 3.6-5.1. Colab ~0.03 CU. Verified by Lead |

## 开题卡（10-16 v1，未做研究）
**核心科学问题**：分离区和角部的风压是强非高斯的（偏度大、峰度高，负压尾部长）。CFD（LES/LBM）、随机模拟（Hermite/变换类、矩匹配）和 AI 生成模型分别能不能复现这种尾部特征和峰值统计？幕墙（尤其玻璃）的强度和累积损伤对持续时间敏感，用规范的等效静压（峰值系数乘以平均或 rms）设计幕墙，与按真实非高斯时程算出的失效概率差多少？非高斯性对幕墙设计结论有没有可见影响？

**现有认识与空白**
- 库内有：非平稳、非高斯随机过程模拟算法 p.1–15。结构线的"压力–响应相容"编译页提到峰值因子：。
- 10-16 补卡（litwiki，前缀，PDF 页与期刊页已分栏）。
 - 非高斯模拟：Gurley & Kareem 1998 相关非高斯压力场模拟 `M6YFPBWH_*`；多项式变换加 POD 生成大跨屋盖非高斯荷载 `X3B57QFZ_*`。
 - 峰值估计：Winterstein 1988 Hermite 极值 `XX4QUV6S_*`；Sadek & Simiu 2002 `9XZRXTEV_*`；Peng 等 2014 峰值方法比较 `UJS3XV63_*DGQC6QDE_*`；非高斯峰值不确定性解析法 `ZNURE73L_*`。
 - LES 峰压可信度：LES 与风洞对照加 UQ `JTGXK9HM_*`；高层建筑 LES 峰压质量评估 `ER29ZKGI_*`。
 - 玻璃持续时间：Gavanski & Kopp 2011 `C3XBMEKX_*`。原文认为设计气旋中心约 30–50 min 的时段造成主要玻璃损伤，3 s 阵风假定可能低估玻璃设计荷载（PDF p.1、7/期刊 p.1603、1609）。
- 空白（据上修订，待精读核实）：
 - "持续时间效应让 3 s 等效荷载可能低估玻璃荷载"已有先例（Gavanski & Kopp 2011，低矮建筑风洞压力），本课题**不重复这一点**。
 - 仍空着的是：(1) 风压的**非高斯尾部特征**本身（偏度、峰度、方法误差）对玻璃/幕墙损伤等效荷载的影响，尤其是高层幕墙角区；(2) CFD、随机模拟、AI 三类方法复现的尾部，用于幕墙损伤评估时是否够用。
 - 台风幕墙破坏现场调查还没有可核原文。
 - 第一步实验 (3) 改为：在 Gavanski–Kopp 的持续时间框架上，单独分离出非高斯性的贡献，比如"同 rms 高斯替代时程 vs 原时程"的损伤等效荷载比。

**切入点与可用数据/工具**（只读引用）

**第一步最小实验**（0 SU，工作站 或 Colab 小规模）
- 输入：CAARC 风洞测点 Cp(t)；LBM Silsoe Cp(t) 作为 CFD 对照。

| 10-17 | CAARC M2 CC-2050 0°/45°/90° 共 1032 个测点、LBM Silsoe 40 个测点的偏度/峰度分类 | 强非高斯集中在 0° 侧面后缘（偏度到 −0.96，峰度到 5.65），45° 几乎都是近高斯；LBM Silsoe 只有 1/40 达到强非高斯，屋顶前缘接近高斯（缺实测高阶矩，未下判断） |

## 未决与下一步
- **审查 裁决（10-17）**：第一步**只按判据二**做内部探索性过闸（高斯假定 −22.5%，按原文实现的 Sadek–Simiu −2.8%）。裁决：（文末有更正：Lead 复核时的 "82/135" 是 Lead 自己的脚本错误，已作废）。
- **补正后的判据一（core，按 35 个轨道计）**：50% 分位基本在 15% 内（正压 4/0/3，吸力 2/0/0），规范式峰值略偏低；90% 分位吸力侧 21/23/17 个轨道偏保守。两个分位都与 Gavanski–Kopp 同向。非高斯贡献随所用的量而变，不下普遍结论。报告：。
- **第二步方案已定（10-17，core）**：。顺序：G0 文献与数据 → G1 随机单点小试 → G2 扩到 M2 全风向 → G3 AI 短测 → G4 接收 CFD 时程。门槛开算前预注册（均为假设）；全程约 9–14 人日、0 SU，G3 另需 43–130 个 A100 计算单元。
 - **G1 已止损（10-17，core）**：「训练风向插值 + 单点 Hermite」在留出风向上谱前置闸门只过 12/27（要求 80%），初步判不够用。均值、rms、偏度、峰度全过；BLUE 50%/90% 各过 25/27，高斯负对照只过 16/27、18/27。留出风向里没有一个强非高斯点，所以主问题没被检验。报告：。
 - **G1b 已止损（core）**：给定前 60 s 统计时，单点 Hermite 在强非高斯组的检验段谱过 10/30，BLUE 50% 过 16/30、90% 过 22/30，正压 R_dmg 中位 1.25–1.30。报告：。
 - **Lead 核查**：同样的门槛套在实测前半 vs 后半上，谱也只过 11/30，强组峰度 23/30、R_dmg(s=10) 19/30。这几项门槛比数据自身的抽样波动还严，判不出方法好坏。超出噪声的真实失败是 BLUE 50%（实测两半之间 25/30，Hermite 16/30）和正压短尾一侧的损伤高估约 25%。
 - **G1c 已止损（core）**：报告。两种边际正好互补：
 - Hermite：主导长尾（吸力）BLUE50/90 29–30/30，短尾（正压）BLUE50 17/30，损伤高估约 25–30%。
 - 双尾 PPCC：短尾 BLUE50 30/30，R_dmg 28/30；但长尾 BLUE50/90 降到 21/30，峰度群体闸门也不过。
 - 经验 CDF 参照全部通过，说明"平移过程 + 谱校正"的框架够用，瓶颈在各尾的边际模型。
 - **G1d 按预注册未过，随机单点路线止损、不再加方法**（core，报告）。新样本是强非高斯 40 例。没过的两条：
 - 主导尾 BLUE50 为 36/40，低于同批 Hermite 的 38/40，违反"不低于 Hermite"
 - 正压 R_dmg 误差 q90 为 0.28–0.31，超过 0.20。但实测两半之间本身就有 0.25–0.29，经验 CDF 也一样。
 - 组合法的正压 R_dmg 中位偏差 +4% 至 +7%（Hermite 为 +23% 至 +27%）；吸力侧 q90 为 0.133，低于噪声 0.151。
 - **审查 裁决（10-17）**：。
 - 止损成立。
 - "失败在噪声附近、限制主要是记录长度"撤回：组合边际的实现有方差转移缺陷，主导 BLUE 系统高估约 8–11%；经验 CDF 的 R_dmg 按构造等于半段差；"两半至少一半通过"抬高了通过数；G1c 预注册的冻结证据不足。
 - 随机单点路线的初步结论：**在已测试的实现下，只给目标点的均值、rms、谱、偏度、峰度不够，需要目标点的经验边际或实测时程。** 只对本轮实现成立。
 - **第二步现状**：G2 不启动（方案要求 G1 先过）。AI（G3）暂缓：只以低阶统计为条件的 AI 会撞上同一堵墙，等先回答"有目标点数据时，生成模型还能多带来什么"（延长重现期、多样本、空间相关场），再定是否值得花 Colab。CFD（G4）等别线的 CAARC 时程过闸。
 - 今后评分统一：两半误差中位 + 逐半报告 + 按风向→轨道分层的 bootstrap 区间；噪声基线与正式评分同口径。
 - G3（AI）继续暂缓：条件生成也面临同样的跨风向插值问题，等 G1b 的结果再定。
 - G0 AI 文献已回（litwiki，索引）：
 - 唯一直接先例是 Liu 等 2025 的条件 WGAN（卡）。它用稀疏测点重建高层建筑 400 个测点的风压时程，只做了时间留出，没有独立风向或独立建筑；比较了偏度和峰度，但高峰度处低估；Fig.18 的稀有负压尖峰仍有误差（PDF p.15–16 / 期刊 p.2821–2822）；没有块极值分布、重现期或损伤检验。
 - Kim 2021 的 GAIN（VIBMBDWP）没有评估极值；Chen–Kopp–Surry 2002 的 ANN（7HLM4JFR）只比较了同一段时程的最大、最小 Cp（PDF p.15–17 / 期刊 p.603–605）。
 - 2019–2026 年没有查到扩散模型或流模型生成风压时程并评估极值的文献（不是穷尽证明）。
 - 对 G3 的含义：按风向留出、按 BLUE 尾部和损伤等效荷载来检验，正好补这个空白；Liu 2025 用的是东京工艺大学开放风洞库，可作 CAARC 之外的第二数据源（下载前先查大小）。
 - 已给 、留言（只告知）：等它们的 CAARC 时程过闸后，只读取用。
 - G3（AI，Colab）等 G1 结果出来再决定开不开。
- 已知缺口：斜风向的镜像未经验证；点压未做面积平均；Silsoe 缺实测高阶矩。

### 第三周计划（已完成，存档）

### 第二周计划（已完成，存档）
1. 修正方法：Sadek–Simiu 短尾改用正态；加入 HPM（UJS3XV63）和修正 Gamma（DGQC6QDE）；Gumbel 改用 Lieblein BLUE；做分半检验，去掉自证成分。
2. 取齐 M2 CC-2050 其余 9 个风向，以及 M4（1:200）C05 的 0°/45°/90°（逐个取、算完即删），检验结论随风向和模型比例是否稳定。
3. 足尺设计风暴（Gavanski–Kopp 5 h 设计气旋）：算"时程损伤等效荷载 vs 规范式峰值 × 3 s"，补上首步判据的第二条；加内压敏感性。
4. CFD 一侧：Silsoe 缺实测高阶矩，LBM 尾部问题改在 CAARC 上做（风洞 M4 vs 将来的 CAARC LES 同口径比较）；Ong 2020 的数值偏度、峰度图（PDF p.7–11）只作位置线索；CAARC L2 建筑 LES 出 Cp(t) 后做同口径比较（已给 留言，只读）。
5. 第一步收尾时，若要给出"非高斯性对幕墙设计有可见影响"这类结论，先 

## Liang Hu 注

## 已定决定
- 2026-10-22 与更好世界 L29.6a2 边界对齐：模拟方法普查、实现、误差/速度基准归 L29.6a2；幕墙影响、跨风向插值、R_dmg 归本课题 →
projects.brief: 你前面做了很多工作和调研，但这个问题还是没有解决。这里面有好些问题：（1）风压值该如何取？可以通过试验或者CFD，但是CFD风压计算不易（CFD线我们是否在考虑这个问题？），且这些与实测结果对比如何？对于高层建筑，其来流和周边流场可能还有一定复杂性，比如临近建筑带来的channeling effect，还有特征湍流，尾流，雷暴或者龙卷这类特征风；另外建筑还可能渐进破坏，例如破坏后内压和外形会发生变化等因素；（2）风压的极值如何得到（或者说，其概率特征该如何分析？这因其为非高斯，包含谱（甚至高阶谱），分布函数，极值估计，相关函数等内容？这些概率特征并且受到时程的平稳、非平稳性影响，该如何考虑？概率特征与风速参数之间的关系如何？）：（3）在已知风压（时程或频域）的前提下，一块玻璃幕墙的响应特征如何计算？如何判断其是否失效？可靠性如何判定？（4）这些研究是否可以拓展用于低层建筑？以上这些问题，请仔细考虑，并根据文献重新合理设置本项目的子项目。

# L31.4 Non-Gaussian Wind Pressure Simulation and Curtain Wall Design (Topic 4)

## Current Status
**10-22 citation snowballing**: pool (1978, initial screening 437, snowball-only 115). Selected 6 papers for card creation (items 18-23 on the list); focused on verifying whether "Surface Pressure Extremes: A Hybrid Data and Simulation Approach" (2016) is a precedent for this line's conclusion that "empirical marginals or measured time histories are required": if so, the conclusion of the stochastic single-point route must be rewritten to align with the precedent.
> 10-22 card returned: the abstract of 2016 "Surface Pressure Extremes: A Hybrid Data and Simulation Approach" indeed contains the precedent of "target PDF + PSD with inverse Johnson synthesis", which belongs to the same family as our G1d composite method; how the empirical marginal is constructed remains unverified (no full text). The conclusion of the stochastic single-point route is kept unchanged for now, but this work must be listed as a precedent when writing the report; high-order scale-resolving simulation of tall-building extreme loads (full text) serves as the CFD-side reference.
> 10-22 full-text verification: the 2016 "hybrid data and simulation approach" fits a Johnson marginal using the first four moments + an AR Gaussian core (PDF pp. 3-5), rather than a point-by-point empirical marginal: falling into the category judged by our G1 series as "giving moments alone is insufficient", so our conclusion that "empirical marginals or measured time histories are required" is not preempted by the precedent.

In progress (Liang Hu's 10-16 23:3x reply: "create all and carry out basic work"). Week 1 completed on 10-17 at 00:30 (0 SU): report, experimental design. The Step 1 criterion of "peak methods differing by > 15%" is preliminarily met; "time-history damage vs. code equivalent static pressure" awaits Step 2 full-scale storms. No conclusions drawn. litwiki returned (10-17): original Silsoe measurement papers (Richards & Hoxey 2012, Ong 2020) **do not** have skewness, kurtosis, or peak factors on the same basis (card), so "whether LBM tails are insufficient" cannot be judged at present; BLUE coefficients have been added to the library and written into scripts. Week 2 task brief completed (10-17 02:44), and Week 3 completed; review ruled on (Criterion 2 passed the gate, C3/C4 withdrawn); corrections completed (10-17).

## Tried and Results
| Date | What Was Done | One-Sentence Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10-17 | Skewness/kurtosis classification across 1032 taps on CAARC M2 CC-2050 at 0°/45°/90° and 40 taps on LBM Silsoe | Strongly non-Gaussian taps concentrate near the side trailing edge at 0° (skewness down to -0.96, kurtosis up to 5.65), while 45° is almost entirely near-Gaussian; only 1/40 taps on LBM Silsoe reaches strong non-Gaussianity, with the roof leading edge remaining near-Gaussian (missing measured higher-order moments, no judgment made) |
| 10-17 | Comparison of four peak estimators against empirical peaks across 101 strongly non-Gaussian taps | Gaussian assumption -19%, Hermite (original W88 coefficients) +18%, shifted Gamma +3%, block Gumbel +1% (shares the same record as empirical, containing self-validation); median inter-method difference is 18%-21% |
| 10-17 | Glass damage-equivalent load ratio R_NG between spectrum-matched Gaussian surrogates and original time histories (s = 10/13/16) | Median across strongly non-Gaussian taps is 1.22 (s = 10) / 1.34 (s = 16), maximum 1.86; damage amplification approximately equals peak amplification (ratio 0.93-1.01) |
| 10-17 | Week 2 (core): method corrections and split-half testing, M2 11 wind directions, M4 45°/90°, 5 h design cyclone | Out-of-sample (366 half-records): Gaussian -22.5%, Winterstein +16.4%, HPM +10.7%, modified Gamma +7.1%, Sadek-Simiu -0.1%, BLUE Gumbel -0.1%; storm p_eq(3 s) / code-formula peak median is 1.02-1.08 at the 50th percentile and 0.86-0.92 at the 90th percentile (direction vs. Gavanski-Kopp pending verification); half-duration truncation per wind direction and 160 taps dropped due to sign flips prevented judging the 15% gate |
| 10-17 | Week 3 (core): biaxial symmetry mirroring to complete 360° wind directions, two-tailed integration across 344 taps, original time history vs. Gaussian surrogate in storms | Primary scenario 1/8, GCpi=0, 135 corner taps: median p_eq(3 s) / BLUE 50% peak is 0.98-1.10 (mostly <15%); ratio to BLUE 90% peak is 0.81-0.94, with 89-95 of 135 taps on the suction side deviating by >15% (code formula is on the conservative side); median R_NG is 0.83-0.98 (non-Gaussianity does not make "measured peak × 3 s" unsafe); agrees in direction with Gavanski-Kopp at the 90th percentile (PDF p. 5 / journal p. 1607) |
| 10-17 | Step 1 correction (core): removed window locking, added 240 permutations, variable window lengths, orbit deduplication, independent orientation selection across 10 surrogates, and Sadek-Simiu implemented per original paper | Criterion 1: 50th percentile mostly within 15%, 90th percentile conservative on the suction side (21/23/17 orbits out of 35); same direction as Gavanski-Kopp; Sadek-Simiu split-half test -2.8% |

## Open Items and Next Steps
- **Review ruling (10-17)**: Step 1 passes the internal exploratory gate **under Criterion 2 only** (Gaussian assumption -22.5%, Sadek-Simiu implemented per original paper -2.8%). Ruling: (correction at the end: the "82/135" found during Lead verification was a bug in the Lead's own script and has been invalidated).
- **Corrected Criterion 1 (core, counted across 35 orbits)**: 50th percentile is mostly within 15% (positive pressure 4/0/3, suction 2/0/0), with code-formula peaks slightly low; at the 90th percentile on the suction side, 21/23/17 orbits are conservative. Both percentiles agree in direction with Gavanski-Kopp. Non-Gaussian contributions vary with the metric used, and no universal conclusion is drawn. Report: .
- **Step 2 plan finalized (10-17, core)**: . Sequence: G0 literature and data → G1 stochastic single-point pilot → G2 expand to M2 all wind directions → G3 short AI test → G4 ingest CFD time histories. Thresholds pre-registered before computation (all are assumed values); total effort approx. 9-14 person-days and 0 SU, with G3 additionally requiring 43-130 A100 compute units.
 - **G1 stopped (stop-loss) (10-17, core)**: "training wind-direction interpolation + single-point Hermite" passed the spectral prerequisite gate on only 12/27 holdout wind directions (80% required), preliminarily judged insufficient. Mean, rms, skewness, and kurtosis all passed; BLUE 50%/90% each passed 25/27, while the Gaussian negative control passed only 16/27 and 18/27. None of the taps in the holdout wind directions was strongly non-Gaussian, so the main question was not tested. Report: .
 - **G1b stopped (stop-loss) (core)**: given the first 60 s of statistics, single-point Hermite on the validation half of the strongly non-Gaussian group passed the spectrum gate on 10/30, BLUE 50% on 16/30, 90% on 22/30, with positive-pressure median R_dmg of 1.25-1.30. Report: .
 - **Lead verification**: applying the same thresholds to the first half vs. second half of the measurements themselves passes only 11/30 on the spectrum, 23/30 on kurtosis in the strong group, and 19/30 on R_dmg(s=10). These thresholds are stricter than the data's own sampling variability and cannot distinguish method quality. The genuine failures exceeding noise are BLUE 50% (25/30 between measured halves vs. 16/30 for Hermite) and an approx. 25% damage overestimation on the short-tailed positive-pressure side.
 - **G1c stopped (stop-loss) (core)**: report . The two marginal models are complementary:
 - Hermite: dominant long tail (suction) BLUE50/90 passes 29-30/30, short tail (positive pressure) BLUE50 passes 17/30, overestimating damage by approx. 25-30%.
 - Two-tailed PPCC: short-tail BLUE50 passes 30/30 and R_dmg passes 28/30; however, long-tail BLUE50/90 drops to 21/30, and the group kurtosis gate also fails.
 - The empirical CDF reference passes all gates, showing that the "translation process + spectral correction" framework is adequate and the bottleneck lies in the marginal model for each tail.
 - **G1d failed pre-registration; stochastic single-point route stopped (stop-loss) with no further methods added** (core, report). The new sample consists of 40 strongly non-Gaussian cases. The two failed items:
 - Dominant-tail BLUE50 is 36/40, below Hermite's 38/40 on the same batch, violating "no worse than Hermite"
 - Positive-pressure R_dmg error q90 is 0.28-0.31, exceeding 0.20. However, the discrepancy between the two measured halves themselves is already 0.25-0.29, and the empirical CDF performs similarly.
 - The composite method gives a median positive-pressure R_dmg bias of +4% to +7% (vs. +23% to +27% for Hermite); suction-side q90 is 0.133, below the noise level of 0.151.
 - **Review ruling (10-17)**: .
 - Stop-loss stands.
 - The claim that "failures are near the noise floor and the limitation is mainly record length" is withdrawn: the composite-marginal implementation has a variance-transfer defect, systematically overestimating the dominant BLUE by approx. 8-11%; R_dmg of the empirical CDF equals the split-half difference by construction; "passing in at least one of the two halves" inflated pass counts; and freeze evidence for G1c pre-registration was insufficient.
 - Preliminary conclusion for the stochastic single-point route: **under the tested implementations, providing only the target tap's mean, rms, spectrum, skewness, and kurtosis is insufficient; an empirical marginal or measured time history at the target tap is required.** Holds only for the implementations tested in this round.
 - **Step 2 current status**: G2 will not be launched (the plan requires G1 to pass first). AI (G3) is on hold: AI conditioned solely on low-order statistics will hit the same wall, so we will first answer "when target-tap data are available, what additional value can a generative model provide" (extending return periods, multiple realizations, spatially correlated fields) before deciding whether to spend Colab units. CFD (G4) awaits CAARC time histories from other lines to pass their gates.
 - Scoring unified going forward: two-half median error + per-half reporting + bootstrap intervals stratified by wind direction → orbit; noise baseline evaluated on the exact same basis as formal scoring.
 - G3 (AI) remains on hold: conditional generation faces the same cross-direction interpolation problem, awaiting G1b results before deciding.
 - G0 AI literature returned (litwiki, index):
 - The only direct precedent is the conditional WGAN of Liu et al. 2025 (card). It reconstructs wind pressure time histories at 400 taps on a tall building from sparse taps using only a temporal holdout, without independent wind directions or independent buildings; it compares skewness and kurtosis but underestimates high kurtosis; rare negative-pressure spikes in Fig. 18 still show errors (PDF pp. 15-16 / journal pp. 2821-2822); and it lacks block-maxima distributions, return periods, or damage tests.
 - Kim 2021's GAIN did not evaluate extremes; Chen, Kopp & Surry 2002's ANN compared only maximum and minimum Cp over the same time history (PDF pp. 15-17 / journal pp. 603-605).
 - No literature from 2019-2026 was found using diffusion or flow models to generate wind pressure time histories and evaluate extremes (not an exhaustive proof).
 - Implication for G3: holding out by wind direction and evaluating against BLUE tails and damage-equivalent loads directly fills this gap; Liu 2025 uses the Tokyo Polytechnic University open wind tunnel database, which can serve as a second data source beyond CAARC (check file size before downloading).
 - Left a message for, (notification only): once their CAARC time histories pass the gate, we will use them read-only.
 - G3 (AI, Colab) awaits G1 results before deciding whether to launch.
- Known gaps: mirroring for oblique wind directions is unverified; point pressures are not area-averaged; Silsoe lacks measured higher-order moments.

## Decisions Made
- 2026-10-22 Boundary alignment with Make the World a Better Place L29.6a2: survey of simulation methods, implementation, and error/speed benchmarking belong to L29.6a2; curtain wall impact, cross-direction interpolation, and R_dmg belong to this topic →

projects.title: L31.4a Wind Pressure Sources and Credibility
projects.goal: Answer Liang Hu's Question 1: Where do wind pressures used in curtain wall design come from (wind tunnel, CFD, field measurements, AI reconstruction), up to what statistical level is each credible (mean / rms / peak / tail), and how do urban interference, special wind conditions, and post-breach internal pressure alter them. Deliverables: wind pressure source credibility table (v0 on 11-01, v1 on 11-08), CFD peak acceptance specification v0, a5 internal pressure model note v0, and gap inventory (with associated costs).

projects.digest:
# Wind Pressure Sources and Credibility (Active)

This project evaluates the sources and layer-by-layer credibility (mean, rms, peak, and tail values) of design wind pressures used for building facades across wind tunnels, CFD, full-scale field measurements, and AI reconstruction, including the impacts of aerodynamic interference, special wind phenomena, and post-breakage internal pressure. The Lead agent and worker agents benchmarked lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) and delayed detached eddy simulation (DDES) data against Silsoe full-scale cube measurements, drafted initial CFD peak acceptance criteria, and sampled the TPU database for twin-building aerodynamic interference. In one 600 s LBM run, windward peaks fell within the full-scale scatter, but separated-flow fluctuating rms and negative peaks were roughly half of full scale (ratios about 0.51 to 0.57); for DDES, roof and side median values were 0.87 to 1.22 of full scale after low-pass binning, while leeward fluctuating rms was 1.33 and 1.64 of full scale, and the DDES fluctuations themselves are not validated. In a small TPU sample of two layouts of square twin buildings, a post-hoc envelope of local negative peaks showed amplifications of 1.28 and 1.60, mainly from increases in mean and rms, and a second tandem-layout sample showed no interference-induced bimodal distributions; both results hold only for these samples. A Helmholtz internal pressure solver with discharge coefficient k=0.3 systematically overestimated experimental points by a median of +0.12 (only 11 of 21 points within ±0.15). No quantitative same-tap peak comparison between wind tunnel or CFD and full scale for high-rise facades was found, CAARC CFD time series have no delivery date, and CAARC LBM time series are estimated for December at the earliest. All results are internal and preliminary, not yet reviewed.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The PI approved the sub-project setup under L31.4 plan v2, prompting the Lead agent to launch work packages a1 through a6.
- **2026-10-25**: The Lead agent completed the a1 Silsoe benchmark under matching definitions, finding LBM separated-region fluctuating standard deviations and negative peaks were roughly half of full-scale measurements.
- **2026-10-25**: The CFD line reported that CAARC building simulations remain on hold because inflow calibration has not passed; using its unvalidated Silsoe DDES time series, the Lead agent found binned roof negative peaks within the full-scale band at 5 to 6 of 6 taps.
- **2026-10-25**: In response to the PI's instruction to make work packages visible, the Lead agent established separate nodes for work packages a1 through a6.
- **2026-10-25**: A worker agent delivered isolated building credibility table v0, noting that three studies found wind tunnels underestimate full-scale low-rise separation negative peaks and that no quantitative same-tap peak comparison exists in the reviewed records for high-rise facades.
- **2026-10-25**: A worker agent tested a single-opening Helmholtz internal pressure solver, finding that discharge coefficient k=0.3 systematically overestimated experimental points by a median of +0.12, failing its validation gate with only 11 of 21 points within ±0.15.
- **2026-10-25**: A worker agent completed a 28-file TPU small sample for aerodynamic interference, observing post-hoc envelope negative peak amplifications of 1.28 and 1.60 times, primarily driven by mean and rms increases.
- **2026-10-25**: A worker agent analyzed a 37-file tandem layout sample to test bimodality, finding no interference-induced bimodal distributions in this sample of square twin buildings (0.4% windward incidence versus 0.8% in the quasi-isolated baseline).

## What the PI decided
- Approved the sub-project reset plan v2 on 2026-10-25, ruling: "好的，现在可以按你说的进行了" ("Okay, it can proceed as you described now").
- Instructed the team to make every work package individually visible on the project interface, asking: "这些按前面说的开工作包了吗？我没有看见啊" ("Were these work packages opened as discussed earlier? I haven't seen them").

## Where it stands
Work packages a1 through a5 are assembling their respective credibility table sections, targeting credibility table v0 on 2026-11-01 and v1 on 2026-11-08. Work package a6 remains not started pending correlation scale benchmarks, credibility table v0, and the first archived benchmark run of L29.6d1, while external CAARC numerical time series remain blocked until the CFD and digital twin lines resolve inflow calibration and hardware constraints.

# L31.4a1 Isolated Buildings: Wind Tunnel, CFD and Full-Scale Pressure Comparison (Active)

This work package asks how wind pressures on isolated buildings from wind tunnels, CFD and full-scale measurements differ in mean, rms, peak and tail shape, and why. On 2026-10-25 the package Lead agent compiled existing results and literature, with no new computation, into version 0 of the isolated-building column of a pressure-source credibility table (internal and preliminary, not reviewed). Three low-rise studies agree that wind tunnels underestimate full-scale negative peaks in separated regions; in one typhoon case rms matched (0.93 in both) while minimum peaks did not (−2.3 tunnel, −3 field). For high-rise buildings no quantitative tunnel- or CFD-versus-full-scale peak evidence was found. For the Silsoe cube, the LBM configuration gave separated-region rms and negative peaks of about 0.5–0.57 of full scale, while the DDES configuration gave about 0.87–1.22 on roof and sides and 1.33–1.64 for leeward rms; the two are listed separately and not ranked, since inlets, meshes and durations differ.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Package opened under the plan approved by the PI.
- **2026-10-25**: Version 0 delivered ahead of the 10-31 date; script-generated numbers corrected two earlier statements.
- **2026-10-25**: A check found that subtracting a noisy reference pressure slightly overestimates fluctuations (roof StDev ratio estimated 0.208 to 0.201), weakening but not reversing the LBM finding; new full-text literature cards became available.

## Where it stands
Version 1 is due 11-08, adding a reference-noise footnote, literature values for the TTU and Commerce Court rows, and a Reynolds-number row.

# L31.4a2 CFD Peak Wind Pressure: Methods and Acceptance Criteria (Active)

This work package asks what CFD must satisfy in inflow turbulence, resolvable frequency, wall treatment, record length and sampling to predict peak pressures, and how point and panel-averaged peaks should be accepted; it does not run LES itself. On 2026-10-25 the package Lead agent, using read-only data and small scripts, found that an earlier short spurious-pressure window (12901 samples) came from reading only the first of two data files, and recomputed over the full 42–642 s window (30001 samples, pre-registered). Building-location empty-field rms Cp was 0.053 raw and 0.030 binned, and the ratio to roof-tap fluctuation was 0.40 and 0.30 under the reference-subtracted definition. A post-hoc diagnostic (not pre-registered) showed the reference-point fluctuation (rms Cp about 0.063) is nearly uncorrelated with the building location (0.013), so subtracting it adds independent noise. It also produced panel layouts and coherence-probe coordinates for the CAARC case and a draft v1 of the acceptance criteria. All results are internal and unreviewed.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Package opened under the plan approved by the PI.
- **2026-10-25**: Spurious-pressure window recomputed; reference-noise diagnostic added.
- **2026-10-25**: CAARC panel (8 locations, three sizes) and probe tables produced for the CFD line; draft v1 changes Cp to per-tap mean removal, sets three-tier spurious-pressure thresholds (a line assumption) and replaces the assumed velocity scale with a 3–6 sensitivity range.
- **2026-10-25**: Literature found no usable tolerance for wall-treatment effects on corner peaks, so wall treatment stays report-only.

## Where it stands
The table column is due by 10-31 and the final v1 criteria on 11-08, after the remaining extreme-value literature cards are added.

projects.digest:
# L31.4a3 Interference from Neighboring Buildings (Exploring)

This work package asks how channeling, wake buffeting and shielding by a neighboring building amplify or reduce local peak pressures and their non-Gaussian features (skewness, kurtosis, tails), and how much of the isolated-building picture holds in a city. A literature summary found peak interference factors of about 1.3 to 1.91 at most and reductions down to about 0.57. Because the papers define these factors differently, the values cannot be merged into one coefficient. No study in the library tracks how skewness, kurtosis or tails change under interference, and two papers report bimodal windward pressure distributions. The Lead agent then ran two small analyses on public two-building wind-tunnel data (0 SU, data deleted after use). In two oblique layouts known to be unfavourable, strongly amplified negative peaks reached 2.21 and 3.83 at single taps, and no interference-induced bimodality appeared. A tandem sample also showed no interference-induced bimodality (windward bimodal cases 0.4% against 0.8% in the reference), and unimodal peak models did not fail on the few scattered bimodal cases. All results are internal and preliminary, have not been reviewed, and hold only for these samples and configurations.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The package started under the L31.4 plan v2, which the PI had approved. The Lead agent checked the public database metadata only: two-building sub-databases, .mat files of about 11 MB each, and "all rights reserved" with no open license, so internal research use only.
- **2026-10-25**: The parent Lead approved a small sample of about 0.35 GB. A later note added that certain sealed test sets of another project must not be read and that a sample's real length is about 7.5 s at model scale.
- **2026-10-25**: Sample a3-01 was preregistered before any data were fetched. The Lead agent used 28 files and, because the public isolated-building data were not comparable, a "quasi-isolated" reference (interferer 8.5B downstream). Clearly amplified negative peaks occurred at 9.7% (T1) and 16.3% (T2) of evaluated tap-direction cases, and clear reductions at 19.1% and 23.5%. A post-hoc design-envelope factor of 1.28 / 1.60 came mainly from higher mean and rms (1.26 to 1.44 times). The median peak factor changed by only 5 to 7%.
- **2026-10-25**: Sample a3-02 tested tandem layouts from 1.5B to 6B using 37 files read from another project's copy, with a bimodality criterion calibrated on synthetic data before fetching. Windward bimodal cases were 0.4% in the target group against 0.8% in the reference group. None of the three peak methods met the preregistered failure criterion, but with only 34 bimodal cases this result is weak.
- **2026-10-25**: The Lead agent noted that the literature conditions for bimodality (rectangular model, interferer rotated, 2D to 8D upstream) were not covered, so the null result does not contradict the literature.
- **2026-10-25**: The parent Lead declined a rectangular-database sample until it is explained why that database's Cp is about 3.8 times the usual value. Full-direction envelopes were deferred.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the L31.4 plan v2, under which this package runs. All other approvals in this conversation came from the parent Lead agent.

## Where it stands
The current tasks are to read the existing check record on the rectangular database's Cp issue, without fetching data, and to consolidate the interference column (a3-01, a3-02 and the literature) of the credibility table v1, due 11-06.

# L31.4a4 Special Wind Conditions: Thunderstorm, Tornado and Typhoon Fine-Scale Turbulence (Active)

This work package asks how facade pressure peaks, non-stationarity and spatial distribution under downbursts, tornadoes and typhoon rainband gusts or rolls differ from boundary-layer wind, and whether boundary-layer coefficients can be transferred; it covers only the pressure level and was literature-only (0 SU, 0 Colab). On 2026-10-25 the package Lead agent read 13 papers and delivered version 0 of a special-wind pressure characteristics table ahead of its 10-31 date, as internal, unreviewed results. For low-rise buildings and cubes, with time-varying local wind speed as reference and background static pressure removed, mean and most peak Cp fall near the boundary-layer range, while local peaks in separated regions remain larger; a moving downburst gave peak envelopes about 2 times the quasi-steady estimate, and one full-scale downburst event fell mostly within the range of 128 boundary-layer events on the same building. For tall buildings, none of the papers read compares local peaks with boundary-layer wind on the same reference and time window, and no pressure-level literature was found for typhoon fine-scale structures. Values across papers are not directly comparable: the same full-scale event gave roof-corner Cp of about −40 with a 900 s mean speed and about −3.7 with a 3 s speed.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Table v0 delivered, with evidence grades A–D defined by the Lead agent; a request listing the wind-field quantities needed from L31.2 was passed up.
- **2026-10-25**: A quick literature search yielded leads; one paper (steady thunderstorm-outflow profile on CAARC) was added at grade B.
- **2026-10-25**: New cards added a tornado-simulator tall-building study (peak Cp as low as −4.2, no same-model boundary-layer comparison, grade C). A third paper's abstract reports larger boundary-layer than tornado-vortex pressures on CAARC, opposite to low-rise findings, but its full text was not obtained, so it was not graded.

## Where it stands
Table v1, with a gap list and cost estimates for filling gaps, is due 11-07; the full text of the unverified tornado paper is still missing.

# L31.4a5 Internal Pressure and External Pressure Changes after Envelope Breach (Active)

This work package asks how mean, fluctuating and Helmholtz-resonant internal pressure change once a broken window or door creates a dominant opening, including multi-room and multi-opening cases, and how breaches alter the external pressure field; it supplies input to the facade progressive-damage task (c6) of L31.4c. A version 0 internal-pressure model note already existed. On 2026-10-25 the package Lead agent checked the governing equation of Holmes and Ginger (2012) against the original and re-derived it. The solver reproduced the analytical resonance frequency within 0.3% and the paper's example ratio (1.113 against about 1.1). Two pre-registered checks failed: agreement with the design formula was 16/21 against a required 80%, and against 21 experimental points with discharge coefficient k=0.3 the model ran systematically high (signed median difference +0.12, 11/21 within ±0.15). k=0.2 passed both, but was examined only after seeing results, so it was not adopted. These are internal, unreviewed results.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Package opened under the plan approved by the PI; equation check completed.

# L31.4a6 AI and Interpolation for Wind Pressure Reconstruction (Not started)

This work package asks whether AI or interpolation can reconstruct wind pressures where taps are sparse, missing or absent while preserving peaks and tails. The Lead agent split the question into gap filling at a tap (T1), reconstruction at an unmeasured point (T2, the main concern for curtain-wall corner zones) and cross-direction cases (T3). Its literature reading found that prior studies did not test reconstructed extremes or damage-equivalent loads with whole taps held out, nor compare AI methods with simple interpolation on the same data. Candidate methods run from nearest-point, IDW and Kriging baselines through linear stochastic estimation and gappy POD to ANN and generative models, with error plotted against distance to the nearest tap over correlation length (r/L). # L31.4b1 Marginal Distributions and Sources of Non-Gaussian Wind Pressure (Active)

This work package maps how skewness, kurtosis and tail shape of wind pressure vary by region (windward, side front/middle/rear thirds, corners, leeward, roof) and wind direction on the CAARC model, whether two inflows (with spires, CC-2050; without spires, CC-2051) change them, and how much averaging over neighboring taps weakens non-Gaussianity; causes are described only as associations. Computations were run by a worker agent under a frozen pre-registration, and the package Lead agent checked them on 2026-10-25. Its independent region labelling matched the worker's version 4 labels at all 3784 tap-direction points of CC-2050 (earlier versions had swapped east and west faces). Under the pre-registered criteria (internal, unreviewed): statistics were stable in all 12 groups; only "side rear third stronger than windward" and "roof stronger than windward" held among region comparisons, with the comparison pairs specified after the fact; inflow changed non-Gaussianity on the windward face, side front third and roof, while the side rear third missed the threshold by only 0.000006; and tap-group averaging weakened skewness in all cases, to 0.89–0.96 of single-tap values with spires and 0.96–0.99 without. These group-scale results (about 120–260 m² full scale) are not extrapolated to a curtain wall panel of about 1.5×3 m.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Package opened under the plan approved by the PI; a dry run on already-seen data exposed a wind-direction convention issue and a mismatch with the pre-registered expectation.
- **2026-10-25**: Worker results checked and an atlas v1 draft written; the inflow effect was found to reverse with direction (larger skewness without spires at 0° and 10°, smaller at 20°–90°, down to −0.14 at 80°), so the pooled inflow result cannot be read as a general weakening.
- **2026-10-25**: Panel averaging on a separate dense-tap dataset passed the skewness-reduction criterion in 20/66 regions and the peak-factor criterion in 66/66, with only 14 of 56 panels truly two-dimensional.
- **2026-10-25**: A post-hoc 50 Hz low-pass sensitivity raised strong non-Gaussian counts (132 to 238 with spires, 161 to 212 without), so counts and peak values must be reported both ways.

## Where it stands
Atlas v1 is due 11-08 after adding peak-factor group ratios, handling 3110 of 24772 tap groups that span side subregions, and merging the low-pass results; conclusions go to the parent Lead agent for review.

projects.digest:
# L31.4b2 Spectra, Higher-Order Spectra and Space-Time Correlation of Wind Pressure (Active)

This work package studies regional differences in wind-pressure power spectra and vortex-shedding peaks. It asks whether the bispectrum and bicoherence can describe sources of non-Gaussianity, and how pressures are correlated between taps (coherence decay, correlation length). The results feed panel net-load, interpolation and field-simulation work in L31.4. The Lead agent of the package audited the worker scripts and caught a unit and scale error (coherence decay coefficient c too small by about 6313 times) and swapped windward/leeward labels. It then ran a low-pass sensitivity study on an archived CAARC dataset and, under frozen pre-registrations, analysed correlation, coherence and panel-averaged spectra on a public 1:50 high-rise dataset. All results are limited to these datasets, configurations and wind directions, are sensitivity bounds or descriptions rather than corrected values, and have not been reviewed. The combined spectra and correlation atlas is due on 11-08.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The work package was opened as a sub-thread of L31.4b at the PI's request. The Lead agent reported two errors in the running correlation script: c was too small by about 400 × 15.78 ≈ 6313 times, and the East/West face labels were swapped for 45° to 90°.
- **2026-10-25**: The CAARC data showed no record of a tubing frequency-response correction in the literature or metadata ("not found"). Every tap had a spectral spike at 177.5 Hz (model scale), and 18–29% (median) of the variance lay above 50 Hz. This was read as an inference, not proof. A low-pass sensitivity on two wind directions and 344 taps cut BLUE50 peak Cp by a median of 13–17% (50 Hz) to 17–21% (30 Hz). The step-one gap in error between Gaussian and Sadek–Simiu peak estimates changed by at most 1.1 percentage points. Correlation length L rose by 12–107% after filtering, while c was unaffected.
- **2026-10-25**: A short pre-registration for the public dataset was frozen. A residual-spike check found a same-type spike on one tile but not the other, with variance above 50 Hz of 2–6% (median), compared with 18–29% for CAARC.
- **2026-10-25**: Profile 02 results: 61 of 70 groups met the exponential-correlation criterion. At 1.5 m, 4 groups met "near-full correlation", 10 did not and 56 could not be judged. 98 of 308 panel-band groups met the high-frequency reduction threshold.
- **2026-10-25**: For Profile 03, 37/40 groups met the exponential criterion (40/40 after low-pass). The Lead agent corrected its earlier low-pass ρ shift (+0.02) to a median of +0.04 to 0.05 on one tile and gave lower and upper bounds instead. The two profiles were not compared with a paired test, so no inflow-dependence claim was made.
- **2026-10-25**: The full-scale spectral slope over 1–5 Hz was a median of −1.88 and −1.81 at single taps and about −2.7 for 1.5×3 m panels. The 5–10 Hz band (and therefore 1–10 Hz) was judged unusable because of the spike's rising edge and the nearby Nyquist limit. These values are reported next to the CAARC value of −2.56, not merged with it.

## What the PI decided
- Liang Hu had this work package split off from L31.4b. It falls under the L31.4 redesign he approved on 10-25.

## Where it stands
The CAARC and public-dataset results still need to be merged into the spectra and correlation atlas v1, due on 11-08. Bispectrum results exist, but the literal bicoherence criterion was not met for one inflow, and the literature on surface-pressure bispectra is thin. Contacting the CAARC data authors about tubing lengths was left to the parent Lead agent.

projects.title: L31.4b3 Stationary Extreme-Value Estimation and Uncertainty
projects.digest:
# L31.4b3 Stationary Peak Estimation and Its Uncertainty (Active)

This work package of L31.4b (non-Gaussian wind pressure statistics and extremes) compares peak-estimation methods (Gaussian, Winterstein Hermite, HPM, modified Gamma, Sadek–Simiu, BLUE-Gumbel, and an empirical body with Pareto tail) for bias and sampling uncertainty, asks how long a record is needed, and is to deliver a peak-estimation procedure v0 by 11-08. Computation was run under a frozen preregistration by another agent and finished by the parent Lead; this node checks it and writes the procedure. Under the frozen criterion, no method in any layer was close enough to the noise floor, so nothing could be recommended. The parent Lead and this node found that the preregistered noise floor was defective: it cancels first-order terms, leaving a second-order quantity about one quarter of an ideal predictor's scatter. A corrected floor (F1) was defined after the fact (10-25 15:30) and both readings are reported side by side. Under the corrected reading, BLUE10 at 60 s meets the criterion in the moderate layer, and Gaussian, Winterstein88, Sadek–Simiu and BLUE10 at 60 s do so in the near-Gaussian layer; in the strongly negative-skew layer most relevant to curtain walls no method qualifies, and the strongly positive-skew layer has no samples. These are mechanical outcomes of the criterion, not recommendations, pending review by six reviewer models.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Work-package note and procedure skeleton written; two reuse risks flagged (a hard-coded BLUE extrapolation factor and the tail direction passed to Sadek–Simiu) and relayed via the parent to the computing agent. No compute used.
- **2026-10-25**: The parent Lead asked for a pressure-system frequency-response check after tubing-resonance artefacts above 50 Hz were found in the tap spectra.
- **2026-10-25**: A startup-plan reminder was confirmed by the platform as a false alarm for work packages.
- **2026-10-25**: Noise-floor defect independently verified (simulation with 200 000 Gumbel pairs: ideal predictor q90 0.134, original floor 0.036, corrected floor 0.136). Corrected F1 q90: 0.132 (strong negative skew), 0.148 (moderate), 0.200 (near-Gaussian). In the strong negative-skew layer BLUE10 at 60 s reached the floor but was biased +4.7%, 90% interval [+2.9%, +5.4%], just above the ±5% limit. In the same layer, for BLUE10 only, fitting 12 s or less gave +11% to +13% bias.
- **2026-10-25**: The parent Lead sent a rough first read of 50 Hz low-pass results (e.g. BLUE10 median error +2.9% to +4.4%) and asked for them to be added as a post-hoc sensitivity.

## What the PI decided
- Approved the L31.4 redesign plan v2, which covers this work package.

## Where it stands
The low-pass sensitivity, by layer and under both floors, is still to be merged into procedure v0, with attention to whether the +4.7% BLUE10 bias changes. Any "recommended method" waits for the six-reviewer review.

projects.title: L31.4b4 Nonstationary Testing, Characterization, and Extremes
projects.digest:
# L31.4b4 Non-Stationarity: Testing, Characterization and Extremes (Active)

This work package asks how to tell whether a wind-pressure record is non-stationary, how to estimate time-varying moments, how to compute extremes under non-stationarity, and how much thunderstorm or downburst winds matter. The first data were wind-tunnel downburst (impinging-jet) pressures on the CAARC M2 model at r/D = 1.0 and 0°: three pure-downburst cases and one downburst-plus-boundary-layer case, each with 8 repeats. Stationary boundary-layer records served as the null comparison. All work followed a frozen preregistration plus two dated addenda, ran locally with 0 SU and no Colab, and deleted raw files after use. In the pure-downburst cases, 100% of taps were non-stationary in mean and variance, and 25 to 49% in shape (kurtosis), concentrated on side and leeward faces. A common single-record test detected 77 to 99% of non-stationary cases but gave false alarms at 8 to 22% on stationary records, against a nominal 5%. For extremes, non-stationary methods were not generally better than a stationary Hermite method. Peak underestimation was shared by all methods that rely on the zero-crossing rate and changed with the filter cutoff, so it cannot be attributed to ignoring non-stationarity. All results are internal and preliminary, have not been reviewed, and hold for this configuration only.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The Lead agent wrote the package note and draft preregistration, with no data or computation. The parent Lead froze it with rulings on alignment signal, null groups and assumed values (0.5 s window, 20% active window, 10% threshold).
- **2026-10-25**: In batch 1 (8 repeats), alignment on plenum static pressure failed (offset SD 0.235 s, maximum 0.448 s), so the fallback windward-face signal was used and passed. The extreme-value self-check failed: the stationary baseline overestimated by about 20% on boundary-layer records. The cause was traced to estimator definitions, not code errors, and the package stopped as preregistered.
- **2026-10-25**: The parent Lead chose option A, addendum §14: new stationary baseline candidates, zero-crossing rate counted after a 30 Hz low-pass filter, and revised error metrics. The rerun of batch 1 was marked "non-blind". On batch 2, one hypothesis (non-stationary methods better) was supported only in one case. A comparison computed after seeing the results showed no advantage over the Hermite method. The downburst-plus-boundary-layer case could not be judged because its active window covered the whole record.
- **2026-10-25**: Addendum §15 redefined that case's window (marked post hoc, with the original "cannot judge" reading kept alongside). It then showed a small advantage for non-stationary methods (median differences −0.009 and −0.025) and a peak ratio of 0.802. The single-record test detected only 1.9% there.
- **2026-10-25**: A descriptive cutoff sensitivity check found downburst peak ratios of about 0.80 to 0.90 at 30 Hz, 0.88 to 0.97 at 80 Hz and 0.98 to 1.14 unfiltered. Because of a 177.5 Hz resonance in the measurement chain, no cutoff can be called correct.

## What the PI decided
- Had this work package split off from L31.4b. All rulings in this conversation came from the parent Lead agent.

## Where it stands
The criteria part of the method page v0 can go to L31.4a4, marked internal and unreviewed. Two readings stay internal until method page v1 (due 11-08) is sent for independent review: no general advantage of non-stationary methods in this configuration, and underestimation by zero-crossing-based methods at a 30 Hz cutoff. No pressure data from real typhoon measurements has been found yet.

projects.title: L31.4b5 Relationship Between Probabilistic Features and Wind Speed Parameters
projects.digest:
# L31.4b5 Inflow Parameters and Non-Gaussian Wind-Pressure Statistics (Active)

This work package asks how turbulence intensity, integral scale, wind direction and terrain change the skewness, kurtosis, peak factor and spectra of surface wind pressure on tall buildings, and whether an inflow-to-pressure-statistics mapping can be built. The first step paired two archived wind-tunnel inflows (with and without spires). The Lead agent derived their turbulence intensity (0.210 vs 0.071) and integral scales, but a reference probe showed that the profile-rig values differ from the flow at the building during pressure tests, so they are used only for ranking and order of magnitude. A public high-rise dataset (1:50 model, two dense pressure tiles, two inflow profiles with roof-height turbulence of about 6% and 11%) was verified and adopted as the main data for the second step. Under a frozen pre-registration, an implementation self-check failed one of four conditions (81 taps instead of 91±3 in the 3 m panel); the parent Lead agent then amended that condition post hoc to match the data grid, and both readings were recorded. The analyses then ran: area averaging consistently reduced the peak factor, and the stronger-turbulence profile increased non-Gaussianity on one tile for winds from −15° to +30°; because the two profiles also differ in integral scale, this is not attributed to a single inflow parameter. These are internal stage results, not yet reviewed, limited to one dataset, one record per direction, and ratio-type quantities only.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: The sub-thread was split off from L31.4b at the PI's request. The Lead agent computed inflow parameters and found that the profile-rig and pressure-test layouts differ (at the reference probe, the pressure-test layout had 44–63% higher mean speed and 34–50% lower turbulence). It switched the integral-scale method because the original autocorrelation method was unstable (0.38–3.27 m across segments). The first-step pre-registration was frozen by the parent Lead agent.
- **2026-10-25**: Dataset checks confirmed the public dataset parameters (minimum tap spacing 0.17 m full scale, 500 Hz, 300–360 s records). They also corrected the source of the published panel averages, which used only one inflow profile.
- **2026-10-25**: A joint pre-registration for the second step was frozen. In the self-check, all six panel peak Cp values were within 15% of the published values (3.5–12.1%), but the tap-count condition failed (81 vs 91±3). The parent Lead agent ruled to continue, recording the amendment and the original reading ("self-check failed, do not run") side by side.
- **2026-10-25**: Area averaging (A): skewness reduction passed in 20/66 regions and peak-factor reduction in 66/66. Only 14 of 56 non-overlapping panels were truly two-dimensional.
- **2026-10-25**: Profile pairing (B) was stopped after a configuration mismatch. The file mapping was corrected and a 297 s record was excluded, giving 30 pairs. The worker's reply was lost, but the results on disk were complete and the Lead agent checked them directly.

## What the PI decided
- Liang Hu had this work package split off from L31.4b as a sub-thread. It belongs to the L31.4 redesign that he approved on 10-25.

## Where it stands
The stage summary carries six stated limitations and has not been reviewed. It will go to a six-reviewer review together with the first-step paired results from the two archived inflows. Those results are still waiting on another work package to finish.

projects.title: L31.4b6 Non-Gaussian Wind Pressure Field Simulation
projects.digest:
# L31.4b6 Non-Gaussian Wind Pressure Field Simulation (Not started)

This work package asks whether spatially correlated non-Gaussian field simulation, given empirical marginals at target taps, is good enough for three curtain-wall uses: extending records (for b3), area averaging (for c2) and generating multiple samples (for c5). Each use is to be judged "adequate", "inadequate" or "insufficient evidence" using curtain-wall metrics such as a glass damage-equivalent load ratio and BLUE peaks. The Lead agent wrote the work package description and flagged two risks, stated as its own inference without literature support: an empirical marginal cannot extrapolate beyond the measured range, so extended-record peaks would be capped and biased low; and generators that rank-reorder samples onto one fixed set of values give identical damage loads across samples (a reviewer model computed zero variance), making them useless for c5. It also found that the literature card cited in the brief is Ma et al. 2016, a moment-based parametric method, not an empirical-marginal method, and asked the parent to correct the description. No computation was done.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-25**: Work package created at the PI's request; description written and reported to L31.4b.
- **2026-10-25**: A platform reminder about a missing start-up plan was answered as a false alarm, since the PI had approved the L31.4 redesign plan v2 and work packages do not file separate start-up plans.

## Where it stands
Not started. Start requires b1 and b2 atlases v1 (target 11-08) and a usable multi-point generator from L29.6a2, which is not expected before 11-25.
